734	=================== save-frame
735	---
736	title: "Save Frame"
737	description: "Save the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC, drawn at full size the way an export draws it."
738	---
739	
740	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
741	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
742	
743	Save Frame writes the frame under the playhead to a still image: a thumbnail, a poster frame or a picture for a document.
744	
745	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Save Frame…" keys="⌥⌘E" tools="render_frame" />
746	
747	## Save a frame
748	
749	<Steps>
750	
751	1. Move the playhead to the frame.
752	
753	2. Choose **File ▸ Save Frame…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>. It's greyed out while the timeline is empty.
754	
755	3. Pick a **Format:** and a place. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` in place of `:`, such as `Board 00-00-12-05.png`.
756	
757	4. Choose **Save**.
758	
759	</Steps>
760	
761	The frame is the one the playhead was on when you opened the panel. When the save works, nothing else appears. The file is where you put it.
762	
763	If it doesn't work, an alert says why:
764	
765	| The alert says | What it means |
766	| --- | --- |
767	| "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing." | Frame Job couldn't draw a frame at that time. |
768	| "Could not write PNG to … The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it." | The folder is missing, or Frame Job can't write into it. |
769	| "Could not write HEIC to … This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format." | This Mac has no encoder for the format. |
770	
771	## PNG, JPEG or HEIC
772	
773	| **Format:** | File | Transparency | Depth | Compression |
774	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
775	| **PNG** | `.png` | Kept | 8-bit, or 16-bit for a [deep frame](#deep-and-hdr-frames) | Lossless |
776	| **JPEG** | `.jpg` | None. A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. | Always 8-bit | 90 % quality |
777	| **HEIC** | `.heic` | Kept | 8-bit, or 10-bit for a deep frame | 90 % quality |
778	
779	The popup opens on **PNG** every time and doesn't remember your last choice. A line under it says what the chosen format does with transparency, such as "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
780	
781	Choosing a format changes the extension in the file name and keeps a name you've typed. Only `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` and `.heic` count as extensions, so `Board v1.2` keeps its `.2` and becomes `Board v1.2.jpg`.
782	
783	## Drawn the way an export draws it
784	
785	The frame is drawn the way an [export](/export/what-an-export-includes/) draws it, at the canvas's full size.
786	
787	Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version and Show Selection never change it. It never carries a timecode burn-in, even if you use one on your exports.
788	
789	## Inside a nest
790	
791	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the saved frame is the picture the canvas is showing: the nest's own, at the nest's size and the nest's time. The timecode in the suggested name is the nest's too. Save Frame is greyed out in an empty nest, however full the timeline is.
792	
793	This is the opposite of an export, which always writes the whole timeline.
794	
795	## Deep and HDR frames
796	
797	Most frames are saved at 8 bits a channel and labelled BT.709. These are saved with more:
798	
799	- **A deep frame.** A frame showing a still deeper than 8 bits, or a 10-bit VP9 clip, is saved as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, still labelled BT.709. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip is saved deep too, when every video track in the timeline is that deep.
800	- **An [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/).** Every PNG and HEIC keeps the HLG picture, as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG.
801	
802	JPEG is always 8-bit. In an HDR project a JPEG is the project's [SDR version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), labelled BT.709.
803	
804	See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/) for how depth runs through the rest of the app.
805	
806	## Waiting for masks
807	
808	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, which are made on this Mac. Past that, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the clip's file, for example "speech.mov drawn whole: the person masks were not ready within 30 seconds."
809	
810	Save the frame again once the clip's **Status** row shows the masks are done. An export never does this: it [waits as long as the masks take](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs).
811	
812	## Good to know
813	
814	A graphic that fails draws its error card in the saved frame, and a clip whose cursor file can't be read is drawn without its cursor. Save Frame doesn't warn you about either, so look at the picture.
815	
816	## The same still for an agent
817	
818	`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame for the same frame and format. It returns the picture itself as well as a file, and with no path it writes a temporary PNG and names it. The format comes from `format` if you pass it, otherwise from the path's extension, otherwise PNG.
819	
820	It also reports what Save Frame keeps quiet: when a graphic in the frame warned or failed it names the graphic, its frame and the message, and it names a cursor file it couldn't read. Like Save Frame, it waits 30 seconds for masks and says which clip it drew whole. An agent can ask for more than the menu offers, such as a timecode burn-in, an ungraded picture or scope measurements. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
821

830	---
831	title: "Audio stems"
832	description: Write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor.
833	---
834	
835	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
836	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
837	
838	An audio export can also write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix. These files are stems. Use them to mix or master the project in another editor.
839	
840	<AtAGlance
841	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
842	  keys="⌘E"
843	  where="Export sheet ▸ Stems"
844	  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
845	/>
846	
847	## Export stems
848	
849	<Steps>
850	
851	1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**.
852	
853	2. In **Format:**, choose **Audio only (M4A)**, **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)**.
854	
855	3. In **Stems:**, choose **One per Track** or **One per Track Name**. The footnote on the sheet counts them, for example "3 stems".
856	
857	4. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**, then name the mix in the save panel.
858	
859	</Steps>
860	
861	Frame Job writes the mix, then each stem beside it. The stems are in the same format as the mix and cover the same range.
862	
863	## The Stems row
864	
865	| Choice | What it writes |
866	| --- | --- |
867	| **None** | The mix alone. This is the default. |
868	| **One per Track** | The mix, and one stem for each track you can hear. |
869	| **One per Track Name** | The mix, and one stem for each track name. |
870	
871	The row sits under **Bit depth:**. On every format except the three audio-only ones it's greyed out and keeps your last choice.
872	
873	The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.
874	
875	## Which tracks get a stem
876	
877	Only tracks you can hear get a stem:
878	
879	- A [muted track](/audio/mute-and-solo/) has no stem.
880	- While any track is soloed, only the soloed tracks have one.
881	- A track with no sound on it, only pictures or nothing, has none.
882	
883	With **One per Track Name**, tracks whose names match share one file. The match ignores case and any spaces at either end, and the file is named the way the first of those tracks is spelled. A track with no name gets its own file. Name your tracks in [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
884	
885	If no track can be heard, the sheet shows "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write", and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out.
886	
887	## Stem file names
888	
889	A stem is named after the mix and its track, and sits in the same folder. Exporting `Mix.wav` writes `Mix - Dialogue.wav` and `Mix - Music.wav`.
890	
891	| Case | The stem's name |
892	| --- | --- |
893	| A track with no name | Its header's label: `Mix - Track 3.wav` |
894	| A `/` or `:` in a track name | Written as `-` |
895	| A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case | Its track's label follows: `Mix - vo (Track 2).wav` |
896	| That name is taken too | A count follows the label: `Mix - vo (Track 2, 2).wav` |
897	
898	No two stems share a file.
899	
900	## Overwriting and clean-up
901	
902	:::caution
903	An existing file at a stem's name is replaced without asking. The save panel asks only about the mix.
904	:::
905	
906	There's one exception. If a stem's file would be one of the project's own media files, the export stops before writing any stem and says so:
907	
908	> The stem “Mix - Dialogue.wav” would replace media this project uses; export under another name.
909	
910	The stems are written one after another after the mix, and the progress bar counts them. When it's done, the line reads "Exported “Mix.wav” and 3 stems.", and its loudness figures are the mix's. A row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) ends its first sentence the same way.
911	
912	Cancelling, or a failure part-way, removes the mix and every stem already written.
913	
914	## Stems are pre-master
915	
916	The master is the export's last stage, where the loudness target and the master limiter work on the whole mix. Each stem holds its tracks' sound exactly as the mix plays it, but from before that stage:
917	
918	- It keeps the clips' and tracks' volume, pan, fades, ducking and effects, and a track's own [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
919	- It gets no [loudness target](/export/loudness/), and the [master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) doesn't touch it.
920	
921	So the stems added together are the mix, to within rounding, wherever the master neither raised the level nor limited a peak.
922	
923	A stem can peak higher than the mix. It's clipped only at full scale.
924	
925	## Good to know
926	
927	A stem has no [chapters](/export/chapters/), even in an M4A file. Only the mix carries them.
928	
929	## With an agent
930	
931	`export` takes `stems`: `tracks` for **One per Track**, or `names` for **One per Track Name**. It works on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other format, or when no track can be heard, `export` returns an error and writes nothing. When the job is done, `export_status` lists each stem's name, tracks and path. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/#stems).
932

940	=================== what-an-export-includes
941	---
942	title: "What an export includes"
943	description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
944	---
945	
946	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
947	
948	Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.
949	
950	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />
951	
952	## The same picture and sound
953	
954	An export draws the picture the same way the preview does, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.
955	
956	View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).
957	
958	The sound goes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). A [track compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) is exact in the file and only approximate in the preview.
959	
960	## Waiting for what it needs
961	
962	Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip, except for a cursor track.
963	
964	| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
965	| --- | --- | --- |
966	| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture set to Foreground) and no file is written |
967	| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
968	| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
969	| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
970	| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
971	| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |
972	
973	Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't finished after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.
974	
975	While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.
976	
977	[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.
978	
979	## Missing media
980	
981	A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.
982	
983	An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).
984	
985	## Graphics
986	
987	An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a graphic's module, the code that draws it, is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.
988	
989	If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.
990	
991	That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."
992	
993	## Captions
994	
995	Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).
996	
997	## Colour labels
998	
999	An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.

41	## Export
42	
43	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it writes the file the same way, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
44	
45	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
46	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
47	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
48	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
49	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
50	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
51	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
52	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
53	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
54	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
55	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
56	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
57	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
58	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
59	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
60	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
61	
62	It returns `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
63	
64	Jobs in the queue run one at a time, behind anything already there. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
65	
66	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.

68	## Export status
69	
70	`export_status` reports how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue does, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
71	
72	Every result carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
73	
74	| `status` | Also carries |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
77	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
78	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
79	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
80	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
81	
82	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
83	
84	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
85	
86	A `done` result adds these keys.
87	
88	| Key | What it holds |
89	| --- | --- |
90	| `ok` | `true`. |
91	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
92	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
93	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
94	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
95	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
96	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
97	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
98	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
99	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
100	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
101	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
102	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Collecting stops after 64 distinct reports, so a noisy graphic's list can be cut short. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
103	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |

105	## Cancel export
106	
107	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and returns what `export_status` would. Pass the `export_id`.
108	
109	| The job is | What happens |
110	| --- | --- |
111	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The result reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
112	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The result may still read `running` until writing has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
113	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The result is the finished job's. |
114	
115	## Export id and its lifetime
116	
117	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
118	
119	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` returned are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number returns the error "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
120	
121	## Refusals and failures
122	
123	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
124	
125	| The request | What stops it |
126	| --- | --- |
127	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
128	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
129	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
130	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
131	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
132	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
133	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
134	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." A clip with no module reads "has no module in graphics/" in place of "does not compile — …". It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
135	
136	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
137	
138	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
139	| --- | --- |
140	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
141	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem “…” would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
142	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
143	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
144	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
145	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
146	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." |
147	
148	A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` result.

174	## Frame rate
175	
176	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` result's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
177	
178	## Path handling
179	
180	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
181	
182	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
183	
184	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
185	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
186	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
187	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
188	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
189	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
190	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
191	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
192	
193	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The returned `path` is always the file that gets written.
194	
195	## Size
196	
197	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
198	
199	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
200	| --- | --- | --- |
201	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
202	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
203	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
204	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
205	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
206	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
207	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
208	
209	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
210	
211	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
212	
213	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` result's `width` and `height` are the file's.
214	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
215	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
216	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
217	
218	An unknown size returns an error with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error too. It isn't clamped.
219	
220	## Range
221	
222	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and `export` returns an error when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
223	
224	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is an error too.
225	
226	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
227	
228	## Exact bitrates
229	
230	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
231	
232	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, Frame Job works out a rate from the frame size and frame rate. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
233	
234	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
235	
236	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
237	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
238	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at a constant quality.
239	
240	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
241	
242	## The loudness report
243	
244	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` result, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
245	
246	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
247	
248	| Key | What it holds |
249	| --- | --- |
250	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
251	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
252	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
253	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
254	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
255	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
256	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
257	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
258	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
259	
260	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
261	
262	## Peak dBTP
263	
264	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
265	
266	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
267	
268	## Audio bits
269	
270	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` result repeats it.
271	
272	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is an error, whatever the preset.
273	
274	## Stems
275	
276	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
277	
278	| `stems` | What it writes |
279	| --- | --- |
280	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
281	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
282	
283	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, and [Stem file names](/export/stems/#stem-file-names) has the other cases.
284	
285	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
286	
287	The `done` result lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
288	
289	- On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
290	- With no track heard, the error is "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
291	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
292	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
293	
294	## Dynamic range
295	
296	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
297	
298	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
299	| --- | --- |
300	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
301	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
302	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
303	
304	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
305	
306	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset returns the error "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
307	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project returns the error "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
308	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
309	
310	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the result names the picture that was written. An SDR project's result has no such key.
311	
312	## Encoder speed
313	
314	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` result names the one used.
315	
316	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
317	| --- | --- | --- |
318	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
319	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
320	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
321	
322	On every other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
323	
324	## Transparent presets
325	
326	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
327	
328	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
329	
330	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.

356	## Render a frame
357	
358	With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.
359	
360	```json
361	{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }
362	```
363	
364	The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:
365	
366	```
367	Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
368	```
369	
370	It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.
371	
372	With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open, it draws that nest at its own size, from its own zero, without the nest clip's position, scale or opacity. It takes no `scope`, so open the nest with `set_scope` to look inside.
373	
374	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does | Default |
375	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
376	| [`t`](#t) | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks. | The playhead |
377	| [`path`](#path) | string | No | Where to write the file. | A temporary file |
378	| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |
379	| [`max_width`](#max_width) | integer | No | Caps the width in pixels, 16 to 8192. | The canvas's width |
380	| [`burn_in_timecode`](#burn_in_timecode) | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. | `false` |
381	| [`ungraded`](#ungraded) | boolean | No | Draws every clip as if it weren't graded. | `false` |
382	| [`selection`](#selection) | integer | No | Draws what an adjustment clip's qualifier selects. | None |
383	| [`sdr_version`](#sdr_version) | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version. | `false` |
384	| [`waveform`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the waveform. | `false` |
385	| [`parade`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the RGB parade. | `false` |
386	| [`histogram`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the histogram. | `false` |
387	| [`vectorscope`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | boolean | No | Also measures the vectorscope. | `false` |
388	| [`vectorscope_zoom`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | integer | No | 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope`. | 1 |
389	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. | The frontmost project |
390	
391	## Choose the moment and the file
392	
393	### `t`
394	
395	The moment to render, in ticks, 600,000 to the second. It's rounded to the project's frame grid. Leave it out for the playhead. A time before zero draws the first frame, and a time past the end returns an [error](#when-it-wont-render).
396	
397	With a nest open, `t` and the playhead are the nest's own time.
398	
399	### `path`
400	
401	Where to write the file, for example `~/Desktop/shot.png`. The folder must already exist, because Frame Job won't create one. An empty `path` is an error.
402	
403	Leave it out for a temporary file. Either way, the last sentence of the text names the file written.
404	
405	### `format`
406	
407	The kind of file to write.
408	
409	| `format` | What you get |
410	| --- | --- |
411	| `png` | Lossless, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
412	| `jpeg` | Quality 0.9. JPEG has no transparency, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black, and the text always says so. |
413	| `heic` | Quality 0.9, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
414	
415	With no `format`, the path's extension decides: `.jpg` and `.jpeg` both mean JPEG, and `.heic` means HEIC. Any other path writes a PNG.
416	
417	An explicit `format` wins, and the path's extension is replaced rather than added to, so `{"path": "shot.jpg", "format": "png"}` writes `shot.png`. Only an extension Frame Job knows is replaced: `Talk v1.2` becomes `Talk v1.2.png`, not `Talk v1.png`. A JPEG always ends `.jpg`, so `shot.jpeg` is written as `shot.jpg`.
418	
419	`jpg` also works as a `format`, and capitals don't matter.
420	
421	### `max_width`
422	
423	Caps the image's width in pixels, from 16 to 8192. The picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas. Leave it out for the canvas's own size.
424	
425	A smaller frame is quicker to send and to look at. The [scopes](#measure-the-frame) measure the frame as written, so their counts cover fewer pixels too.
426	
427	## Change what's drawn
428	
429	These four draw something other than the plain picture. The view switches in the window never reach this tool or an export, so an agent asks here.
430	
431	### `burn_in_timecode`
432	
433	Draws the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything, as the export sheet's **Burn in timecode** does. It's the project's own timecode, in the toolbar's spelling. An export from the in/out range shows project time too, so the number always matches the timeline. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/).
434	
435	### `ungraded`
436	
437	Draws every clip as if it weren't graded: Light, Color, wheels and curves neutral, and no look. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Ungraded** gives. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
438	
439	### `selection`
440	
441	Takes an adjustment clip's id and draws what its qualifier selects, in place of grading. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Selection** gives.
442	
443	- White is fully graded, and black is untouched.
444	- It's the blurred selection when the qualifier has a blur, and it's multiplied by any matte cutting the clip.
445	- The clip's strength isn't applied.
446	- Every layer in front of the clip is left out.
447	- Where the clip isn't on the frame, the picture is black.
448	
449	Frame Job won't do this for any other kind of clip. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
450	
451	### `sdr_version`
452	
453	Draws an [HDR project's](/hdr/dynamic-range/) SDR version, the picture **View ▸ Show SDR Version** gives. White titles come back near white, and highlights above reference white roll off. It's what the SDR exports and JPEG frames hold.
454	
455	In an SDR project it changes nothing, and the frame comes out identical. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/).
456	
457	## Measure the frame
458	
459	Each scope argument measures the rendered frame through the same analyser as the [**View ▸ Scopes**](/color/scopes/) panel, so the two can't count differently. The text gives the headline figures, and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts, named after it: `shot.png` gets `shot.png.waveform.json`.
460	
461	The scopes read the frame as it was drawn, so `max_width`, `burn_in_timecode`, `ungraded` and `selection` all change what they count.
462	
463	If the measurement can't run, the call comes back as an error, but the image is already written and the error names it: "Wrote …, but its waveform could not be measured: the GPU pass did not run."
464	
465	### `waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`
466	
467	- **`waveform`** measures luma. The text gives the share of pixels clipping high and low.
468	- **`parade`** measures R′, G′ and B′ the way the waveform measures luma. The text gives the share clipping high and low for each channel.
469	- **`histogram`** counts R′, G′, B′ and Y′ at 256 levels. The text gives the share clipping high and low, read from Y′.
470	
471	For example: "Waveform: highlights clipped in 0.4 % of pixels, shadows in 0.0 %; its 256 × 256 counts are in …". A pixel clips high at level 255 and low at level 0.
472	
473	| JSON key | `waveform` | `parade` | `histogram` |
474	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
475	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured | The frame measured | The frame measured |
476	| `levels` | 256 | 256 | 256 |
477	| `columns` | 256 | 256 | |
478	| `counts` | 256 column bins, each 256 levels | The same, under `red`, `green` and `blue` | |
479	| `red`, `green`, `blue`, `luma` | | | 256 counts each |
480	| `clipped_high`, `clipped_low` | Pixels clipping | Pixels clipping, by channel | Pixels clipping, by Y′ |
481	| `marks_high`, `marks_low` | The column bins where at least 0.5 % of the column clips | The same, by channel | |
482	| `highlights`, `shadows` | Percentages | | Percentages |
483	
484	### `vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`
485	
486	`vectorscope` measures Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in 256 × 256 bins centred on neutral, bin 128. The text gives the share of pixels that are neutral.
487	
488	`vectorscope_zoom` is 1, 2 or 4, like the 1×, 2× and 4× cells on a [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) slot, and it needs `vectorscope: true`. Zooming spreads a near-grey picture over more bins. At 2 and 4, a pixel off the plot isn't counted, and the text also gives the share that lie off it.
489	
490	| JSON key | What it holds |
491	| --- | --- |
492	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured. |
493	| `bins`, `centre` | 256 and 128. |
494	| `matrix`, `values` | `Rec. 709` and `encoded`. |
495	| `counts` | 256 arrays by Cr bin, each indexed by Cb bin. |
496	| `neutral` | Pixels in the neutral bin. |
497	| `zoom` | The zoom. |
498	| `off_plot` | Pixels left off the plot. Always 0 at 1. |
499	| `targets` | The six 75 % colour targets, `R`, `Mg`, `B`, `Cy`, `G` and `Yl`, each `[cb, cr]` in bins at this zoom, or `null` off the plot. |
500	| `skin_line_degrees` | The skin line's angle. |
501	
502	## Read what the answer says
503	
504	The text always starts with the frame's time and sizes and ends with "Written to …". Anything else worth saying sits between the two.
505	
506	### Graphic problems in the answer
507	
508	When a [graphic](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) in the frame had a problem, the answer names it, with its frame and what went wrong:
509	
510	- `Graphic "lower-third" failed at frame 12: …`
511	- `Graphic "lower-third" warned at frame 12: …`
512	- `Graphic "lower-third" does not compile: …`
513	
514	A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
515	
516	### Waiting for cutout masks
517	
518	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 s for the masks the frame needs. Frame Job starts making them as soon as the cutout is set, on your Mac.
519	
520	Past 30 s the clip is drawn whole, and the answer says so: "Clip 12 is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." For a picture with its subject set to foreground, it says "its foreground masks".
521	
522	So after setting a cutout, read that sentence before trusting the frame. [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/) can wait for the masks first.
523	
524	### A cursor that can't be drawn
525	
526	A screen recording's cursor is drawn from its cursor file. When the file can't be read, the clip draws without one and the answer says "The cursor of media 5 is not drawn: …".
527	
528	## Frames from an HDR project
529	
530	In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the frame depends on the format:
531	
532	| What you ask for | What you get |
533	| --- | --- |
534	| `png` | 16-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
535	| `heic` | 10-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
536	| `jpeg` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
537	| Any format with `sdr_version` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
538	
539	Scopes read the picture drawn. On the HLG picture they read the HLG signal, and on the SDR version they read as an SDR project's do.
540	
541	On the HLG signal:
542	
543	- Each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`.
544	- The waveform, parade and histogram JSON add `scale`: `unit` (`cd/m²`), `ticks` (each with `percent`, `level` and `nits`), `reference_white_percent` (75) and `clip_percent` (100).
545	- Luma takes Rec. 2020's weights, and the vectorscope takes Rec. 2020's matrix and targets.
546	- The text says so. The waveform's reads "reference white at 75 %, 203 cd/m², and 100 % at 1,000 cd/m²".
547	
548	See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) and [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
549	
550	## When it won't render
551	
552	Nothing is drawn in these cases, and the answer says why.
553	
554	| It says | What to do |
555	| --- | --- |
556	| "No frame at … Either the time is past the end of the timeline, the media is missing, or the timeline is empty." | Check `duration` and `missing_media` in [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/). |
557	| "There is no folder at … to write into." | Create the folder, or choose another `path`. |
558	| "path must name a file to write — omit it for a temporary one." | The `path` was empty. |
559	| "format must be one of png, jpeg, heic (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
560	| "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got …)." | Use a width in range. |
561	| "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip … is not one." | Pass an adjustment clip's id. An adjustment clip can't be inside a nest, so close any open nest first. |
562	| "vectorscope_zoom must be 1, 2 or 4 (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
563	| "vectorscope_zoom needs vectorscope: true." | Add `vectorscope: true`. |

574	title: "Tools: rendering and export"
575	description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
576	---
577	
578	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
579	
580	These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.
581	
582	<AtAGlance
583	  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
584	  keys={['⌥⌘E', '⌘E']}
585	  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
586	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
587	/>
588	
589	This page is the quick reference. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) have every argument in full, with what the agent gets back and what to do when a call fails.
590	
591	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). `export_status` and `cancel_export` accept it but don't use it, because an `export_id` belongs to the launch, not to a project. None of the four takes `scope`.
592	
593	## `render_frame`
594	
595	Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It's drawn the way an export draws it, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
596	
597	With no arguments, it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file. Every argument is optional.
598	
599	| To set | Use |
600	| --- | --- |
601	| The moment | [`t`](/mcp/render-frame/#t), in ticks. Default: the playhead. |
602	| The file | [`path`](/mcp/render-frame/#path), [`format`](/mcp/render-frame/#format) (`png`, `jpeg` or `heic`) and [`max_width`](/mcp/render-frame/#max_width) (16 to 8192 pixels). |
603	| What's drawn | [`burn_in_timecode`](/mcp/render-frame/#burn_in_timecode), [`ungraded`](/mcp/render-frame/#ungraded), [`sdr_version`](/mcp/render-frame/#sdr_version) and [`selection`](/mcp/render-frame/#selection). |
604	| Scopes | [`waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`](/mcp/render-frame/#waveform-parade-and-histogram), [`vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`](/mcp/render-frame/#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom). Each scope also writes a JSON file beside the image. |
605	
606	The switches in the **View** menu never reach this tool, so an agent asks for those pictures here, whatever a person has switched on.
607	
608	It returns an image and a text block. The text gives the moment and the sizes, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that sentence it can add what each scope measured, or a note about:
609	
610	- A JPEG that flattened a transparent canvas onto black.
611	- A [graphic](/mcp/render-frame/#graphic-problems-in-the-answer) that warned or failed.
612	- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn.
613	- A clip with Remove Background [whose masks weren't ready](/mcp/render-frame/#waiting-for-cutout-masks) after 30 seconds, which is drawn uncut.
614	
615	With a nest open, it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). An HDR project has its own rules for each format. See [Frames from an HDR project](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).
616	
617	## `export`
618	
619	Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and returns at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate. An export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
620	
621	`preset` and `path` are required.
622	
623	| To set | Use |
624	| --- | --- |
625	| The encoding | [`preset`](/mcp/export/#presets): `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` or `apng`. |
626	| The file | [`path`](/mcp/export/#path-handling). The folder must exist, and an existing file is replaced. |
627	| What's written | [`size`](/mcp/export/#size) and [`range`](/mcp/export/#range). |
628	| The picture | [`video_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`dynamic_range`](/mcp/export/#dynamic-range), [`encoder_speed`](/mcp/export/#encoder-speed) and [`burn_in_timecode`](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
629	| The sound | [`audio_bitrate`](/mcp/export/#exact-bitrates), [`loudness_lufs`](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report), [`peak_dbtp`](/mcp/export/#peak-dbtp), [`audio_bits`](/mcp/export/#audio-bits) and [`stems`](/mcp/export/#stems). |
630	
631	It returns `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. Jobs run one at a time, and the queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole project, even with a nest open. Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
632	
633	A problem with the request comes back from this call as an error, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from `export_status`. See [What stops an export](/mcp/export/#refusals-and-failures).
634	
635	In the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), Frame Job asks you before each `export` runs, naming the file it would write or replace. A client connected over MCP isn't asked.
636	
637	## `export_status`
638	
639	Says how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
640	
641	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
642	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
643	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |
644	
645	Every result has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:
646	
647	| Status | Adds |
648	| --- | --- |
649	| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's text, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
650	| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
651	| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
652	| `done` | What the file holds: its size, the settings used, the `loudness` measured, and any `graphic_warnings` and `cursor_warnings`. |
653	| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's text. |
654	
655	[Export status](/mcp/export/#export-status) lists every key of a `done` result, and [The loudness report](/mcp/export/#the-loudness-report) explains `loudness`.
656	
657	Only ids that `export` returned since Frame Job launched are known, so a job a person put on the queue can't be read. Any other id gives an error. A finished job's result outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.
658	
659	## `cancel_export`
660	
661	Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
662	
663	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
664	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
665	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` returned, 1 or more. |
666	
667	A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the result may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.
668	
669	It returns what `export_status` returns, and gives an error for an id `export` didn't return since launch.
670

682	---
683	
684	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
685	
686	This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).
687	
688	<AtAGlance
689	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
690	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
691	  where="Drag to the Media tab"
692	  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions']}

694	
695	## What Frame Job reads
696	
697	| Kind | Files |
698	| --- | --- |
699	| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
700	| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
701	| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
702	| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
703	| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |
704	
705	Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
706	
707	## Movies
708	
709	Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
710	
711	| Video | What Frame Job does |
712	| --- | --- |
713	| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
714	| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, using the decoder that comes with macOS. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
715	| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
716	| VP8 | Doesn't import. |
717	
718	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
719	
720	The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
721	
722	If macOS can't open the file at all and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can [repackage or convert it](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) on import.
723	
724	### Movies with alpha
725	
726	Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
727	
728	A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
729	
730	### Portrait and rotated movies
731	
732	A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
733	
734	### Variable and unusual frame rates
735	
736	Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track. A variable-rate file gets a single rate this way too.
737	
738	A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
739	
740	If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.
741	
742	## WebM and Matroska
743	
744	macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
745	
746	Add or open one as you would any other movie. A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
747	
748	## Sound
749	
750	M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
751	
752	### Any sample rate
753	
754	Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.
755	
756	### MP3 gapless start
757	
758	Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
759	
760	This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
761	
762	## Pictures
763	
764	PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
765	
766	A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
767	
768	Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
769	
770	### Deep and HDR stills
771	
772	| The still is | What Frame Job does |
773	| --- | --- |
774	| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
775	| Labelled HLG or PQ | Reads it as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, not as SDR. PNG and HEIC keep their colour space and depth. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
776	| Carrying an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's), as an iPhone HDR photo does | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
777	
778	A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
779	
780	## LUTs
781	
782	Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
783	
784	- 3D only. A 1D LUT won't import.
785	- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
786	- At most 32 MiB.
787	
788	A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.
789	
790	## Caption files
791	
792	An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
793	
794	Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
795	
796	## Which way in
797	
798	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
799	
800	| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
801	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
802	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
803	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
804	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
805	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
806	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
807	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
808	
809	A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
810	
811	In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.
812

821	=================== reference/limits
822	---
823	title: Limits
824	description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
825	---
826	
827	The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).
828	
829	## Project size
830	
831	| A project holds at most | |
832	| --- | --- |
833	| Clips | 4,096 |
834	| Tracks | 64 |
835	| Markers | 1,024 |
836	| Media files | 1,024 |
837	| Levels of nesting | 8 |
838	
839	Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.
840	
841	An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.
842	
843	A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.
844	
845	Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.
846	
847	## Canvas and layers
848	
849	| Limit | Value |
850	| --- | --- |
851	| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
852	| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
853	| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
854	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
855	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
856	| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
857	| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
858	| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |
859	
860	Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.
861	
862	Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
863	
864	## Timeline and editing
865	
866	| Limit | Value |
867	| --- | --- |
868	| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
869	| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
870	| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
871	| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |
872	
873	A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).
874	
875	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.
876	
877	## Speed
878	
879	| Limit | Value |
880	| --- | --- |
881	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
882	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
883	| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
884	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
885	| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
886	
887	Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
888	
889	With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.
890	
891	## Audio
892	
893	| Limit | Value |
894	| --- | --- |
895	| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
896	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
897	| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
898	| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
899	| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |
900	
901	The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.
902	
903	A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.
904	
905	See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
906	
907	## Captions
908	
909	| Limit | Value |
910	| --- | --- |
911	| Longest file [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) takes | 10 hours |
912	| **Vocabulary** terms | 1,000 |
913	| [Caption import](/captions/import-captions/) | SubRip only |
914	
915	AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
916	
917	Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.
918	
919	A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
920	
921	## Colour
922	
923	| Limit | Value |
924	| --- | --- |
925	| Points on a [curve](/color/curves/) | 2 to 16 |
926	| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
927	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) override | 1 to 10,000 cd/m² |
928	| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |
929	
930	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.
931	
932	The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
933	
934	[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.
935	
936	## Export
937	
938	| Limit | Value |
939	| --- | --- |
940	| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
941	| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
942	| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
943	| [Master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
944	| [24-bit sound](/export/audio-only/) | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
945	| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |

947	[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.
948	
949	On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.
950	
951	Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

955	| Limit | Value |

958	| [Property](/graphics/properties/) values on one clip | 64 |
959	| Options on one property | 32 |
960	| Characters in a string property | 4,096 |
961	| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |

968	
969	| Limit | Value |
970	| --- | --- |
971	| [Camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) frame rate | One of the camera's formats, at that format's highest frame rate |
972	| [Camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) in the panel | Five. A corner layout is always the bottom-right one. |

43	## The controls
44	
45	The paragraph under the sheet's title sums up the main rules. The controls run from top to bottom:
46	
47	| Control | What it does | Default |
48	| --- | --- | --- |
49	| **Preset:** | Applies a set of choices you saved. The gear beside it saves and deletes them. See [Export presets](/export/presets/). | Custom |
50	| **Format:** | The encoding, a container and a codec together. See [Choose a format](/export/formats/). | H.264 (MP4) |
51	| **Dynamic Range:** | Which picture an HDR project writes. The row is there only in an HLG project. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). | HDR (HLG) |
52	| **Speed:** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). | Balanced |
53	| **Size:** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. See [Export size](/export/size/). | The format's first row |
54	| **Frame rate:** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. See [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/). | Project rate |
55	| **Quality:** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). | Format default |
56	| **Bit depth:** | **16-bit** or **24-bit**, for a WAV or an AIFF. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). | 16-bit |
