694	
695	## What Frame Job reads
696	
697	| Kind | Files |
698	| --- | --- |
699	| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
700	| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
701	| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
702	| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
703	| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |
704	
705	Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
706	
707	## Movies
708	
709	Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
710	
711	| Video | What Frame Job does |
712	| --- | --- |
713	| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
714	| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, using the decoder that comes with macOS. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
715	| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
716	| VP8 | Doesn't import. |
717	
718	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
719	
720	The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
721	
722	If macOS can't open the file at all and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can [repackage or convert it](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) on import.
723	
724	### Movies with alpha
725	
726	Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
727	
728	A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
729	
730	### Portrait and rotated movies
731	
732	A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
733	
734	### Variable and unusual frame rates
735	
736	Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track. A variable-rate file gets a single rate this way too.
737	
738	A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
739	
740	If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.
741	
742	## WebM and Matroska
743	
744	macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
745	
746	Add or open one as you would any other movie. A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
747	
748	## Sound
749	
750	M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
751	
752	### Any sample rate
753	
754	Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.
755	
756	### MP3 gapless start
757	
758	Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
759	
760	This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
761	
762	## Pictures
763	
764	PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
765	
766	A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
767	
768	Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
769	
770	### Deep and HDR stills
771	
772	| The still is | What Frame Job does |
773	| --- | --- |
774	| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
775	| Labelled HLG or PQ | Reads it as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, not as SDR. PNG and HEIC keep their colour space and depth. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
776	| Carrying an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's), as an iPhone HDR photo does | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
777	
778	A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
779	
780	## LUTs
781	
782	Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
783	
784	- 3D only. A 1D LUT won't import.
785	- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
786	- At most 32 MiB.
787	
788	A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.
789	
790	## Caption files
791	
792	An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
793	
794	Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
795	
796	## Which way in
797	
798	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
799	
800	| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
801	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
802	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
803	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
804	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
805	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
806	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
807	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
808	
809	A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
810	
811	In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.

829	## Project size
830	
831	| A project holds at most | |
832	| --- | --- |
833	| Clips | 4,096 |
834	| Tracks | 64 |
835	| Markers | 1,024 |
836	| Media files | 1,024 |

839	Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.
840	
841	An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.
842	
843	A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.
844	
845	Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.
846	
847	## Canvas and layers
848	
849	| Limit | Value |
850	| --- | --- |
851	| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
852	| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
853	| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
854	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
855	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
856	| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
857	| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
858	| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |
859	
860	Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.
861	
862	Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
863	
864	## Timeline and editing
865	
866	| Limit | Value |
867	| --- | --- |
868	| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
869	| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
870	| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
871	| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |
872	
873	A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).
874	
875	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.
876	
877	## Speed
878	
879	| Limit | Value |
880	| --- | --- |
881	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
882	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
883	| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
884	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
885	| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
886	
887	Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
888	
889	With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.
890	
891	## Audio
892	
893	| Limit | Value |
894	| --- | --- |
895	| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
896	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
897	| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
898	| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
899	| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |
900	
901	The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.
902	
903	A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.
904	
905	See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
906	
907	## Captions
908	
909	| Limit | Value |
910	| --- | --- |
911	| Longest file [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) takes | 10 hours |
912	| **Vocabulary** terms | 1,000 |
913	| [Caption import](/captions/import-captions/) | SubRip only |
914	
915	AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
916	
917	Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.
918	
919	A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
920	
921	## Colour
922	
923	| Limit | Value |
924	| --- | --- |
925	| Points on a [curve](/color/curves/) | 2 to 16 |
926	| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
927	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) override | 1 to 10,000 cd/m² |
928	| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |
929	
930	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.
931	
932	The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
933	
934	[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.
935	
936	## Export
937	
938	| Limit | Value |
939	| --- | --- |
940	| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
941	| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
942	| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
943	| [Master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
944	| [24-bit sound](/export/audio-only/) | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
945	| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |
946	
947	[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.
948	
949	On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.
950	
951	Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
952	
953	## Graphics
954	
955	| Limit | Value |
956	| --- | --- |
957	| Largest [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | 8,192 px on a side |
958	| [Property](/graphics/properties/) values on one clip | 64 |
959	| Options on one property | 32 |
960	| Characters in a string property | 4,096 |
961	| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |
962	| [Files watched for your saves](/graphics/edit-a-module/) | The first 16 module, font and picture files one by one, as well as the folders that hold them |
963	| [Memory for drawn frames](/graphics/playback-and-memory/) | A quarter of the Mac's memory |
964	
965	In a folder with more than 16 files, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
966	
967	## Recording
968	
969	| Limit | Value |
970	| --- | --- |
971	| [Camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) frame rate | One of the camera's formats, at that format's highest frame rate |
972	| [Camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) in the panel | Five. A corner layout is always the bottom-right one. |
973	| Length shown in the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) | Sized for up to 9:59:59. A longer recording shows a wider label. |
974	
975	There's no global shortcut to stop a recording, so use the menu-bar item or the **File** menu.
976	
977	If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).
978	
979	## Assistant and agents
980	
981	| Limit | Value |
982	| --- | --- |
983	| [Compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) threshold | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens, 300,000 by default |
984	| **Clear old tool results** | Past 150,000 tokens, when it's ticked |
985	| Wait for a launched copy to be ready for calls | 60 seconds |
986	| Wait for `get_media_analysis` | 60 seconds |
987	
988	If Frame Job launches but isn't ready within 60 seconds, the call says so, and later calls in that client session don't launch another copy.
989	
990	Agent calls run one at a time, and any call waits while you hold the mouse down mid-drag. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
991	
992	`get_media_analysis` keeps what it covered in its 60 seconds, then stops and says how much that was. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) for the Assistant's own limits.
993	
994	## Settings
995	
996	| Limit | Value |
997	| --- | --- |
998	| [Background render](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#set-how-long-it-waits)'s **Start after** | 1 to 60 seconds, 5 by default |
999	| Inspector width | 280 to 440 points |
1000	| Timeline height | 140 points to 60 % of the window |
1001	
1002	[Converting on import](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. Frame Job looks on your `PATH`, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. For an install anywhere else, run this in Terminal:
1003	
1004	```sh
1005	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
1006	```
1007	
1008	`ffprobe` is taken from beside it, or else found by the same search.
1009

56	/// The §7.8 set: one row per ENCODING, in menu order. A row is a container
57	/// and a codec and nothing else — no size, no rate — so an export is at the
58	/// document's own size and rate unless a person asks for another, through
59	/// the Size popup the sheet fills from `Project::export_sizes` or the
60	/// overrides a script sends. The size used to be part of the row ("H.264
61	/// 1080p", "HEVC 4K"), and that shape made the format menu two questions
62	/// asked as one: picking HEVC meant picking 1080p or 4K with it, and a
63	/// 1440p or a vertical document had no row that fit it at all. Two
64	/// questions get two controls, and the format is only ever the encoding.
65	///
66	/// The two image rows are the exception and keep a size and a rate,
67	/// because for them the numbers ARE what makes the row worth having: a GIF
68	/// or an APNG costs frames × pixels with no inter-frame prediction to
69	/// spend against, so "at the document's size and rate" is a file no one
70	/// can send, and the cap is the point of the format rather than a default
71	/// it happens to carry (§7.8; the row comments argue each number). Both
72	/// caps are still defaults a size or fps override replaces, and
73	/// `export_sizes` lists each as the first row of its list.
74	///
75	/// The FIRST row is the default: `rc_export_presets` is "in menu order"
76	/// and the export sheet opens on its first entry, so whatever sits here is
77	/// what ⌘E writes unless a person picks otherwise. H.264 in MP4 is the
78	/// file every player and every upload form takes, which is why it leads
79	/// and HEVC — half the size, not yet everywhere — follows.
80	///
81	/// Each movie row carries an `AVAssetExportSession` preset name for the
82	/// record: the three "highest quality" names are the ones a session would
83	/// take the composition's own size under rather than fit it to a fixed
84	/// frame, which is exactly a row with no size of its own. Nothing runs a
85	/// session any more (§7.8), so on the Swift side the name is only the
86	/// signal that AVFoundation can write the row at all; the two image rows
87	/// carry none, which is the signal to write them frame by frame through
88	/// ImageIO instead. The two LPCM rows repeat `audio_m4a`'s name for the
89	/// same reason and with the field doc's caveat: AVFoundation has no
90	/// session preset for LPCM, and a null would route a WAV to ImageIO.
91	///
92	/// **No row carries a default bitrate, deliberately.** On the session path
93	/// the preset name IS the ladder — `AVAssetExportSession` exposes no way to
94	/// set a rate — so a number here would be one the export cannot honour,
95	/// which is worse than none at all. On the writer path VideoToolbox derives
96	/// a rate from the frame size, which beats any constant this table could
97	/// hold: one that suits 4K wastes half the file at 720p. ProRes is fixed by
98	/// its profile and ignores a request outright, and GIF and APNG have no
99	/// bitrate to set. A bitrate is therefore something the user asks for — the
100	/// `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` overrides — never something a preset
101	/// assumes on their behalf.

104	    // and every script that calls it spells them, so a row is named for
105	    // the encoding alone — `h264`, not `h264_document` — because the size
106	    // is no longer anything the id could say.
107	    Preset {
108	        id: "h264",
109	        name: "H.264 (MP4)",
110	        container: Container::Mp4,
111	        codec: "h264",
112	        video: true,
113	        alpha: false,
114	        size: None,
115	        fps: None,
116	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality"),
117	        writer: None,
118	    },

417	/// [`Project::export_settings`] and `Project::export_sizes` go through it,

427	//! One row of the export table (spec §7.8): [`Preset`], what each row
428	//! answers about itself, and [`fps_json`], the rate's one spelling.
429	//!
430	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
431	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
432	//! as codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
433	//! both, so every `crate::export_table::Preset` and
434	//! `crate::export_table::fps_json` path holds; `name` and `to_json` became
435	//! `pub(crate)` because the table's rows and `presets` stay behind.
436	
437	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
438	
439	use crate::export_container::Container;
440	use crate::export_encoder::{EncoderSpeed, Writer};
441	use crate::time::Fps;

443	/// One row of the table. Crate-visible so `export_size.rs` can read the
444	/// cap and the codec of the row it lists sizes for, and so `export.rs`'s
445	/// resolver can read the rest, both through [`preset`]; every field is
446	/// `pub(crate)` because the table's rows are built in `export_table.rs`.
447	pub(crate) struct Preset {
448	    pub(crate) id: &'static str,
449	    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
450	    pub(crate) container: Container,
451	    pub(crate) codec: &'static str,
452	    /// False for the three audio-only presets; every other row carries
453	    /// video.
454	    pub(crate) video: bool,
455	    /// Whether this ENCODING carries an alpha channel — `hevc_alpha`,
456	    /// `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_4444` and `apng`, and nothing else. It says what the FILE can
457	    /// hold, and never that a particular canvas is translucent:
458	    /// `export_settings`
459	    /// emits one flat object for every row, so a flag derived from the
460	    /// project's background would report `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF
461	    /// and a WAV, which reads as a defect from either side of the FFI. A
462	    /// transparent canvas exported through a row with no fourth channel
463	    /// simply composites onto black, and the flag is what lets the sheet
464	    /// and the `export` tool say so before the file exists.
465	    ///
466	    /// **It is a `Preset` field and not a [`Container`] question**, which
467	    /// is the one thing worth arguing here, because the neighbouring
468	    /// capability [`Container::carries_audio`] IS a container question and
469	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
470	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
471	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
472	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
473	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
474	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
475	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
476	    ///
477	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
478	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
479	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
480	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
481	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
482	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
483	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
484	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
485	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
486	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
487	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
488	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
489	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
490	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
491	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
492	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
493	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
494	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
495	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
496	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
497	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
498	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
499	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
500	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
501	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
502	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
503	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
504	    ///
505	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
506	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
507	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
508	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
509	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),
510	    /// so a row that AVFoundation writes must carry SOME name even when
511	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`
512	    /// for LPCM in a WAV or an AIFF, so those two rows carry the audio-only
513	    /// name `audio_m4a` carries: it is the closest true statement
514	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
515	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
516	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table
517	    /// advertises as unsupported. A name also means "the composition is
518	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
519	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.

599	                None => Value::Null,

603	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the

605	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
606	        out.insert(

608	            match self.avf_preset {
609	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
610	                None => Value::Null,
611	            },
612	        );
613	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
614	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
615	        }

617	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
618	            if writer.takes_speed() {
619	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
620	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
621	            }
622	        }

624	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));

628	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
629	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());

634	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
635	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
636	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
637	//!
638	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
639	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
640	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
641	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
642	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
643	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
644	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
645	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
646	//!
647	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
648	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
649	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
650	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
651	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
652	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
653	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
654	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
655	//!
656	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
657	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
658	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
659	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
660	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
661	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
662	//! back.
663	//!
664	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
665	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
666	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
667	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
668	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
669	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
670	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
671	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
672	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
673	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
674	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
675	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
676	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
677	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
678	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
679	//! the canvas as it is.
680	//!
681	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
682	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
683	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
684	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
685	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
686	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
687	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
688	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
689	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
690	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
691	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
692	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
693	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
694	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
695	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
696	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
697	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
698	//!
699	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
700	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
701	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
702	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
703	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
704	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
705	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
706	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
707	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
708	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
709	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
710	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
711

720	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
721	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
722	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
723	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
724	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),
725	    ("720p", "720p", 720),

828	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
829	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
830	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
831	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
832	/// gives `short` × `short`.
833	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
834	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
835	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
836	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
837	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
838	
839	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
840	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
841	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
842	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
843	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
844	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
845	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
846	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
847	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
848	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
849	
850	    if width >= height {
851	        (long, short)
852	    } else {
853	        (short, long)
854	    }
855	}

857	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
858	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
859	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
860	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
861	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
862	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
863	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
864	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
865	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
866	    (even(width), even(height))
867	}
868	
869	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
870	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
871	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
872	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
873	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
874	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
875	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
876	///
877	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
878	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
879	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
880	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
881	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
882	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
883	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
884	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
885	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
886	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
887	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
888	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
889	        return (width, height);
890	    }
891	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
892	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
893	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
894	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
895	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
896	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
897	    } else {
898	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
899	    };
900	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
901	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
902	}
903	
904	/// `a / b` rounded up to a whole number; `b ≥ 1`.
905	fn ceil_div(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
906	    a.div_ceil(b)
907	}

1	//! Export presets and the resolution of one into concrete settings
2	//! (spec §7.8).
3	//!
4	//! Rust decides, AVFoundation does: nothing here encodes anything. The job
5	//! is to turn "H.264, 1920 × 1080, the in/out range, 30 fps" into the exact
6	//! set of values Swift hands to the writer — the preset name, the output
7	//! file type, the time range, the frame size — so that the choice of format
8	//! is testable without a GPU and the MCP agent's `export` tool takes the
9	//! same vocabulary the UI does.
10	//!
11	//! A preset is an ENCODING — a container and a codec — and carries no size:
12	//! an export is at the document's own size unless one is asked for, and
13	//! the sizes on offer for a document and a format are a separate list,
14	//! [`Project::export_sizes`] in `export_size.rs`, whose rows reach the
15	//! resolver here as the same `width`/`height` overrides a script sends.
16	//!
17	//! Two of the presets name a format AVFoundation cannot write at all: an
18	//! animated GIF and an animated PNG are assembled frame by frame through
19	//! ImageIO. That changes nothing here except one field — those rows carry
20	//! no `avf_preset`, and a null `avf_preset` is Swift's signal to take the
21	//! image-sequence path instead of building a session. Everything else
22	//! (the size, the rate, the range, the file's UTI) is resolved identically,
23	//! because it means the same thing on either path.
24	//!
25	//! Four rows, `av1` (spec §11 CX-12), `av1_webm` (CX-15), `vp9_webm`
26	//! (CX-16) and `vp9_alpha_webm` (CX-17), are encoded by a bundled library
27	//! and not by AVFoundation, which still writes `av1`'s container (the core
28	//! writes the three WebMs): their `writer` names the route, and on the two
29	//! AV1 rows `encoder_speed` names SVT-AV1's speed; no other row's settings
30	//! carry either key, and the two VP9 rows' carry no speed, libvpx having one
31	//! (CX-3).
32	//!
33	//! The two uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, carry
34	//! `audio_bits`, 16 or 24 (spec §11 AU-29): 16 when not asked, and refused
35	//! by name on every other row.
36	//!
37	//! The three audio rows take `stems`, `tracks` or `names` (spec §11
38	//! AU-108): asked, the settings end with `stems`, the files beside the mix
39	//! resolved to `[{name, tracks}]` by `export_stems.rs`; a movie row refuses.
40	//!
41	//! The preset table is the single source of truth: [`presets`] serializes
42	//! it for the picker and [`Project::export_settings`] resolves against the
43	//! same rows, so a preset cannot exist in the menu and not in the resolver.
44	//!
45	//! How an override value is READ and REFUSED is `export_overrides.rs`,
46	//! and the rows themselves — the containers, and the presets written into
47	//! them — are `export_table.rs`. The vocabulary and the table: this file
48	//! is the design they serve and the resolution that brings the two of
49	//! them together against one project.

83	    /// (`rc_export_settings`).
84	    ///
85	    /// Overrides may set `width`, `height`, `fps` (`[num, den]`), `range`
86	    /// (`{"start", "duration"}` in ticks), `optimize_for_network`, the two
87	    /// bitrates `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` (bits per second,
88	    /// strictly positive), the two loudness figures `loudness_lufs` /
89	    /// `peak_dbtp`, `dynamic_range` (`hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, spec §11
90	    /// HD-14), `encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, on a
91	    /// row whose bundled encoder has speeds, CX-12, CX-16) and `audio_bits`
92	    /// (16 or 24, on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, AU-29) and `stems`
93	    /// (`tracks` or `names`, on the three audio rows, resolved to
94	    /// `[{name, tracks}]` last in the settings, AU-108); anything else in the object is ignored, so a newer UI
95	    /// can send fields this build does not know. Each is read and refused
96	    /// by `export_overrides.rs`, which is where the spelling of every one
97	    /// of them lives.
98	    ///
99	    /// A bitrate is emitted only when it was asked for. There is no default
100	    /// to fall back on (see `export_table::PRESETS`), and an absent key says
101	    /// exactly that — "let the encoder pick" — where a zero or a null would
102	    /// have to be re-interpreted as the same thing on the Swift side. The two
103	    /// are accepted for every preset, including the ones that cannot use them,
104	    /// on the same principle that reports a width for the audio-only row:
105	    /// one rule for reading overrides, and the format flags say what the
106	    /// output can actually carry.
107	    ///
108	    /// The two loudness figures follow the bitrates exactly — emitted only
109	    /// when asked for, accepted by every preset, either one alone: the
110	    /// ceiling is the export's master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which runs
111	    /// with or without a target.
112	    ///
113	    /// The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and clamped to the
114	    /// project, because an `AVAssetExportSession` `timeRange` that begins
115	    /// between two frames starts the export on a frame the user did not
116	    /// choose. A range that resolves to zero length is refused: an empty
117	    /// export is always a mistake, and AVFoundation reports it far later
118	    /// and far less clearly.
119	    ///
120	    /// `Err` for an unknown preset or a malformed override. This is a QUERY
121	    /// and not an edit: there is no "changes nothing" case, so it has no
122	    /// identity arm and no refusal arm (spec §5.5).
123	    pub fn export_settings(
124	        &self,
125	        preset_id: &str,
126	        overrides: Option<&Value>,
127	    ) -> Result<Value, String> {
128	        let preset = preset(preset_id)?;
129	        let overrides = object(overrides)?;
130	        // The picture the row writes (spec §11 HD-14 (c), `dynamic_range.rs`):
131	        // read before anything else, so a mistyped value is refused by name
132	        // whatever the row, and resolved against the canvas and the row.
133	        let picture = self.deliverable(preset, dynamic_range(overrides)?)?;
134	        // The bundled encoder's speed (spec §11 CX-12 (2)): read on any row
135	        // so a misspelling is named, then refused on a row it cannot apply
136	        // to, and Balanced when a writer row was not asked.
137	        let speed = match (encoder_speed(overrides)?, preset.takes_encoder_speed()) {
138	            (Some(_), false) => {
139	                return Err(format!(
140	                    "{} has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm",
141	                    preset.id
142	                ))
143	            }
144	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(EncoderSpeed::Balanced)),
145	            (None, false) => None,
146	        };
147	        // The uncompressed rows' bit depth (spec §11 AU-29), on the speed's
148	        // terms: read on any row so a 20 is named, refused on a row that
149	        // has no depth to choose, and 16 on those rows when not asked.
150	        let bits = match (audio_bits_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_audio_bits()) {
151	            (Some(_), false) => {
152	                return Err(format!(
153	                    "{} has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff",
154	                    preset.id
155	                ))
156	            }
157	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(16)),
158	            (None, false) => None,
159	        };
160	        // The stems (spec §11 AU-108 (a)), on the depth's terms: read on any
161	        // row so a misspelling is named, refused on a movie row, and
162	        // resolved to the files they are only when asked.
163	        let stems = match (stems_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_stems()) {
164	            (Some(_), false) => {
165	                return Err(format!(
166	                    "{} has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff",
167	                    preset.id
168	                ))
169	            }
170	            (Some(mode), true) => Some(self.export_stems(mode)?),
171	            (None, _) => None,
172	        };
173	
174	        // Size: the preset's cap if it has one, else the canvas — a movie
175	        // preset renders at whatever the project composites at, and a size
176	        // the sheet's popup or a script chose arrives as the override.
177	        let (preset_width, preset_height) = preset
178	            .size
179	            .unwrap_or((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height));
180	        let width = positive_u32(overrides, "width")?.unwrap_or(preset_width);
181	        let height = positive_u32(overrides, "height")?.unwrap_or(preset_height);
182	        // What is reported is the size the FILE will have, so that the
183	        // sheet's readout, its Size popup and the `export` tool's result
184	        // all say the numbers the writer draws (`export_size.rs` has both
185	        // rules and their reasons). An image format is written with the
186	        // picture FITTED inside the size, never letterboxed and never
187	        // upscaled, so its numbers are the fit and not the box. A row that
188	        // needs even dimensions writes an odd edge one pixel smaller
189	        // (spec §11 G-33), whether the edge came from the canvas or was
190	        // asked for. Every other row writes the pair as it stands.
191	        let (width, height) = if preset.fits_inside_size() {
192	            crate::export_size::fit_within((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height), (width, height))
193	        } else if preset.even_sized() {
194	            crate::export_size::even_size((width, height))
195	        } else {
196	            (width, height)
197	        };
198	
199	        // The preset's rate, else the canvas — the image-sequence presets
200	        // cap the rate for the same reason they cap the size, and every
201	        // movie preset exports at the rate the project was cut at.
202	        let fps = fps_override(overrides, preset.fps.unwrap_or(self.canvas.fps))?;
203	
204	        let project_duration = self.duration();
205	        let (mut start, mut duration) = range_override(overrides, (0, project_duration))?;
206	        // Snap first, then clamp: snapping can only move a bound by less
207	        // than a frame, so clamping afterwards cannot be undone by it.
208	        start = time::snap_to_frame(start, fps).clamp(0, project_duration);
209	        duration =
210	            time::snap_to_frame(duration, fps).clamp(0, project_duration.saturating_sub(start));
211	        if duration <= 0 {
212	            return Err(format!(
213	                "export range is empty: {duration} ticks at {start} in a project {project_duration} ticks long"
214	            ));
215	        }
216	
217	        // Bits per second, or nothing at all. No preset supplies one, so an
218	        // absent key here reaches Swift as an absent key there and means
219	        // "the encoder's own ladder".
220	        let video_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "video_bitrate")?;
221	        let audio_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "audio_bitrate")?;
222	
223	        // The integrated loudness target and the master limiter's true-peak
224	        // ceiling, on the bitrates' terms: emitted only when asked for, so
225	        // an absent `loudness_lufs` reaches Swift as an absent key and means
226	        // "do not normalise", and an absent `peak_dbtp` the master's default
227	        // (spec §11 AU-27). The reader is the one place their bounds live.
228	        let (loudness_lufs, peak_dbtp) = loudness(overrides)?;
229	
230	        let optimize = boolean(
231	            overrides,
232	            "optimize_for_network",
233	            preset.container.optimizes_for_network(),
234	        )?;
235	
236	        let mut range = Map::new();
237	        range.insert("start".to_string(), Value::from(start));
238	        range.insert("duration".to_string(), Value::from(duration));
239	
240	        let mut out = Map::new();
241	        out.insert("preset".to_string(), Value::from(preset.id));
242	        // Null here means "AVFoundation cannot write this" — the GIF and
243	        // APNG rows — and is Swift's cue to take the ImageIO path. It is
244	        // NOT "pick a session preset yourself".
245	        out.insert(
246	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
247	            match preset.avf_preset {
248	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
249	                None => Value::Null,
250	            },
251	        );
252	        out.insert(
253	            "container".to_string(),
254	            Value::from(preset.container.as_str()),
255	        );
256	        out.insert(
257	            "file_type".to_string(),
258	            Value::from(preset.container.file_type()),
259	        );
260	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(preset.codec));
261	        // Width and height are reported even for the audio-only preset —
262	        // they cost nothing and let the sheet show one summary line for
263	        // every preset — but `video: false` is what Swift keys off.
264	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(width));
265	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(height));
266	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(Some(fps)));
267	        if let Some(bps) = video_bitrate {
268	            out.insert("video_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
269	        }
270	        if let Some(bps) = audio_bitrate {
271	            out.insert("audio_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
272	        }
273	        if let Some(lufs) = loudness_lufs {
274	            out.insert("loudness_lufs".to_string(), Value::from(lufs));
275	        }
276	        if let Some(dbtp) = peak_dbtp {
277	            out.insert("peak_dbtp".to_string(), Value::from(dbtp));
278	        }
279	        out.insert("range".to_string(), Value::Object(range));
280	        // Audio is offered whenever the container can hold it: a project
281	        // with no sound simply produces no audio track, which is cheaper
282	        // than deciding here. A GIF or an APNG holds none at all.
283	        out.insert(
284	            "audio".to_string(),
285	            Value::from(preset.container.carries_audio()),
286	        );
287	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(preset.video));
288	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — true for
289	        // `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng`, and for nothing else the
290	        // table offers. `export_table.rs`'s `alpha` field doc is where
291	        // `apng` against `gif` is argued — a GIF shows a transparent pixel
292	        // and still answers false, because it has one palette index and no
293	        // fourth channel — and `core/tests/export.rs` pins the three rows
294	        // by name.
295	        //
296	        // It reads `preset.alpha` and not `self.canvas.background`, which
297	        // is the whole decision and is worth one sentence here as well as
298	        // in the field doc: this object is flat and one shape for every
299	        // row, so a flag that answered "the canvas is translucent" would
300	        // say `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF and a WAV — three files with
301	        // nowhere to put it. It is `audio`'s kind of fact, one line up, and
302	        // told the same way: what the file can HOLD, never what this
303	        // document happens to be. A transparent canvas written through a
304	        // row that answers FALSE composites onto black, and this is the key
305	        // that lets the sheet and the `export` tool say so before the file
306	        // exists.
307	        out.insert("alpha".to_string(), Value::from(preset.alpha));
308	        out.insert("optimize_for_network".to_string(), Value::from(optimize));
309	        // An HLG project's video row names the picture it writes (spec §11
310	        // HD-14 (c)): `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`; only then, so every SDR project's
311	        // settings are the text they were and an audio row is unchanged.
312	        if let Some(picture) = picture {
313	            out.insert("color".to_string(), Value::from(picture.as_str()));
314	        }
315	        // The encoder route on a writer row, and its speed where the encoder
316	        // has speeds, so every other row's settings are the text they were
317	        // (spec §11 CX-12, CX-16 (1)).
318	        if let Some(writer) = preset.writer {
319	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
320	        }
321	        if let Some(speed) = speed {
322	            out.insert("encoder_speed".to_string(), Value::from(speed.as_str()));
323	        }
324	        // The depth on the two uncompressed rows only, so every other row's
325	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-29).
326	        if let Some(bits) = bits {
327	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), Value::from(bits));
328	        }
329	        // The stems last, and only when asked, so every other export's
330	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-108).
331	        if let Some(stems) = stems {
332	            let stems = stems.iter().map(|stem| stem.to_json()).collect();
333	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), Value::Array(stems));
334	        }
335	        Ok(Value::Object(out))
336	    }
337	}
338	//! How an export override is READ and REFUSED — the vocabulary the export
339	//! settings resolve from, where `export_table.rs` is the table and
340	//! `export.rs` the resolution.
341	//!
342	//! Cut out of `export.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and cut HERE for the
343	//! reason `props_check.rs` was cut out of `edit_props.rs`: a rule about
344	//! how a value is spelled and what makes it a refusal is a fact about the
345	//! VOCABULARY, not about the resolution. Nothing in this file knows which
346	//! preset asked, what the canvas is, or what the settings object ends up
347	//! looking like; everything in it answers one question — "is this JSON
348	//! value a legal `width` / `fps` / `range` / bitrate / decibel figure, and
349	//! if not, what do we tell the caller it was?".
350	//!
351	//! The cut also paid the size rule's toll. `export.rs` stood at 578 lines
352	//! against the ~600 soft cap and phase 5 added two containers, two preset
353	//! rows, a decibel validator, two override reads and two echo lines; a
354	//! file at the line gives something up before it takes anything on.
355	//!
356	//! Three rules hold for every reader here, and every new one must keep
357	//! them, because the sheet, the `export` tool and the test suite all lean
358	//! on them:
359	//!
360	//! 1. **Absent and explicit null are the same thing** — "use the preset".
361	//!    That is what lets the export sheet build one overrides object and
362	//!    null the fields whose control is greyed out.
363	//! 2. **An unknown key is ignored, silently.** A newer UI may send fields
364	//!    this build has never heard of and must still get an export.
365	//! 3. **A refusal names the offending value**, through [`describe`], and
366	//!    the message is lowercase and starts `export <key> must be …`. The
367	//!    key is in the message because a caller sending six overrides needs
368	//!    to know which one it was.
369	//!
370	//! [`describe`] itself is not about export at all any more: five modules
371	//! outside this one (`edit.rs`, `edit_props.rs`, `edit_action.rs`,
372	//! `edit_paste.rs`, `edit_track.rs`) name it `crate::export::describe` for
373	//! their own error messages, so `export.rs` re-exports it under that path
374	//! and the cut costs those files nothing. [`spelled`] sits beside it for
375	//! the same reason: a vocabulary value's own JSON spelling, for a sentence
376	//! (`lut.rs`, `media_color.rs`, `edit_relink.rs`).
377	
378	use serde_json::Value;
379	
380	use crate::dynamic_range::DynamicRange;
381	use crate::export_table::EncoderSpeed;
382	use crate::time::{Fps, Ticks};
383	
384	// ---- the shared front door -----------------------------------------------
385	
386	/// A JSON value as short text for an error message, truncated on a char
387	/// boundary so a pasted megabyte of JSON cannot become the error string.
388	pub(crate) fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {
389	    let text = value.to_string();
390	    if text.chars().count() <= 40 {
391	        text
392	    } else {
393	        format!("{} …", text.chars().take(40).collect::<String>())
394	    }
395	}
396	
397	/// A vocabulary value's JSON spelling (`warm`, `video`), serde's own, so a
398	/// sentence names it as the file and the schema do.
399	pub(crate) fn spelled<T: serde::Serialize>(value: T) -> String {
400	    serde_json::to_value(value)
401	        .ok()
402	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().map(str::to_string))
403	        .unwrap_or_default()
404	}
405	
406	/// The overrides object itself: `None` for absent, null or an empty
407	/// request, `Some` for an object, and an `Err` naming the value for
408	/// anything else. One place, so "overrides must be a json object" is the
409	/// same sentence however the caller got here.
410	pub(crate) fn object(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<&Value>, String> {
411	    match overrides {
412	        None => Ok(None),
413	        Some(Value::Null) => Ok(None),
414	        Some(value) if value.is_object() => Ok(Some(value)),
415	        Some(value) => Err(format!(
416	            "export overrides must be a json object, not {}",
417	            describe(value)
418	        )),
419	    }
420	}
421	
422	/// An override field, or `None` when absent or explicitly null (null means
423	/// "use the preset", so a caller can build one overrides object and leave
424	/// the fields it does not care about).
425	fn field<'a>(overrides: Option<&'a Value>, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
426	    overrides.and_then(|o| o.get(key)).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
427	}
428	
429	// ---- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------
430	
431	/// A strictly positive integer override — the pixel dimensions and the two
432	/// bitrates, which want the identical check. `u64::MAX` is not the ceiling
433	/// on purpose: a bitrate is bits per second, and `u32`'s 4.3 Gbit/s is an
434	/// order of magnitude past anything deliverable (ProRes 422 at 4K is about
435	/// 0.7), so the same bound that keeps a width sane keeps a bitrate honest.
436	/// Zero and negative both land in the error arm, which names the value.
437	pub(crate) fn positive_u32(overrides: Option<&Value>, key: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
438	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
439	        return Ok(None);
440	    };
441	    match value.as_u64() {
442	        Some(n) if n > 0 && n <= u64::from(u32::MAX) => Ok(Some(n as u32)),
443	        _ => Err(format!(
444	            "export {key} must be a positive integer, not {}",
445	            describe(value)
446	        )),
447	    }
448	}
449	
450	/// A decibel override: a finite number inside `[min, max]`. The f64 twin
451	/// of [`positive_u32`], and a separate function because the two loudness
452	/// figures are NEGATIVE FRACTIONS — −14.5 LUFS is a real request — so
453	/// every guard `positive_u32` applies is the wrong one here.
454	///
455	/// `as_f64` is the whole type check: `serde_json` answers `None` for a
456	/// bool, a string, an array and an object alike, so the error arm catches
457	/// them all and names what arrived. Non-finite is checked even though JSON
458	/// cannot spell a NaN or an infinity — the function takes a `Value` from
459	/// whoever has one, and a bound comparison against a NaN is silently false
460	/// rather than an error.
461	fn decibels(
462	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
463	    key: &str,
464	    min: f64,
465	    max: f64,
466	) -> Result<Option<f64>, String> {
467	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
468	        return Ok(None);
469	    };
470	    match value.as_f64() {
471	        Some(db) if db.is_finite() && db >= min && db <= max => Ok(Some(db)),
472	        _ => Err(format!(
473	            "export {key} must be a number from {min} to {max}, not {}",
474	            describe(value)
475	        )),
476	    }
477	}
478	
479	/// The bottom of the loudness target's range. −70 LUFS is BS.1770-4's own
480	/// absolute gate: a programme quieter than that measures as nothing at
481	/// all, so a target at or below it is a request the measurement cannot
482	/// even express. The top is 0 LUFS — full scale, unwise but legal, and the
483	/// bound is where it is so the message is about the value.
484	const LOUDNESS_MIN: f64 = -70.0;
485	const LOUDNESS_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
486	
487	/// The true-peak ceiling's range. 0 dBTP is legal (and what a master with
488	/// no headroom asks for); −20 is far below anything a deliverable wants
489	/// and exists only so a mistyped LUFS figure lands in the error arm rather
490	/// than turning the programme down by 60 dB.
491	const PEAK_MIN: f64 = -20.0;
492	const PEAK_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
493	
494	/// The two loudness overrides, read together: `loudness_lufs`, the
495	/// integrated target the export is normalised to, and `peak_dbtp`, the
496	/// true-peak ceiling of the export's master limiter.
497	///
498	/// **Either may come alone** (spec §11 AU-27). Every export with sound runs
499	/// through a master limiter at `peak_dbtp`, −1 dBTP when it is not asked
500	/// for, so a ceiling on its own is not inert: it is the limiter's ceiling,
501	/// with or without a target, and is accepted and echoed as every other
502	/// override is.
503	///
504	/// Both are emitted by the resolver only when asked for, exactly as the
505	/// bitrates are: an absent `loudness_lufs` is "do not normalise", which is
506	/// what `ExportSettings.loudnessLufs == nil` says on the Swift side, and an
507	/// absent `peak_dbtp` is the master's default ceiling there.
508	pub(crate) fn loudness(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>), String> {
509	    let target = decibels(overrides, "loudness_lufs", LOUDNESS_MIN, LOUDNESS_MAX)?;
510	    let ceiling = decibels(overrides, "peak_dbtp", PEAK_MIN, PEAK_MAX)?;
511	    Ok((target, ceiling))
512	}
513	
514	/// The `audio_bits` override (spec §11 AU-29): 16 or 24, `None` when absent
515	/// or null. Whether the row takes one is the resolver's question
516	/// (`Preset::takes_audio_bits`); this answers only whether the value is one
517	/// of the two depths, so a 20 or a string is refused by name on any row.
518	pub(crate) fn audio_bits(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
519	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "audio_bits") else {
520	        return Ok(None);
521	    };
522	    match value.as_u64() {
523	        Some(bits @ (16 | 24)) => Ok(Some(bits as u32)),
524	        _ => Err(format!(
525	            "export audio_bits must be 16 or 24, not {}",
526	            describe(value)
527	        )),
528	    }
529	}
530	
531	/// True or false, or `default` when the key is absent — the shape every
532	/// flag override wants and only `optimize_for_network` has so far.
533	pub(crate) fn boolean(overrides: Option<&Value>, key: &str, default: bool) -> Result<bool, String> {
534	    match field(overrides, key) {
535	        None => Ok(default),
536	        Some(value) => value.as_bool().ok_or_else(|| {
537	            format!(
538	                "export {key} must be true or false, not {}",
539	                describe(value)
540	            )
541	        }),
542	    }
543	}
544	
545	/// The `dynamic_range` override (spec §11 HD-14 (c)): `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`,
546	/// `None` when absent or null. Which of them a row may write is the
547	/// resolver's question (`Project::deliverable`); this answers only whether
548	/// the value is one of the three words.
549	pub(crate) fn dynamic_range(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<DynamicRange>, String> {
550	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "dynamic_range") else {
551	        return Ok(None);
552	    };
553	    match value.as_str().and_then(DynamicRange::parse) {
554	        Some(range) => Ok(Some(range)),
555	        None => Err(format!(
556	            "export dynamic_range must be \"hlg\", \"pq\" or \"sdr\", not {}",
557	            describe(value)
558	        )),
559	    }

607	/// The `fps` override as `[num, den]`, or `default` when it is absent.
608	/// Both terms are read as `u64` and bounded by `u32::MAX` because that is
609	/// what [`Fps`] holds, and both must be non-zero: a zero numerator is a
610	/// frozen export and a zero denominator is a division by nothing, and
611	/// either would reach the frame-snapping arithmetic before anyone noticed.
612	pub(crate) fn fps(overrides: Option<&Value>, default: Fps) -> Result<Fps, String> {
613	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "fps") else {
614	        return Ok(default);
615	    };
616	    let terms = value.as_array().and_then(|a| {
617	        match (
618	            a.first().and_then(Value::as_u64),
619	            a.get(1).and_then(Value::as_u64),
620	        ) {
621	            (Some(num), Some(den)) if a.len() == 2 => Some((num, den)),
622	            _ => None,
623	        }
624	    });
625	    match terms {
626	        Some((num, den))
627	            if num > 0 && den > 0 && num <= u64::from(u32::MAX) && den <= u64::from(u32::MAX) =>
628	        {
629	            Ok(Fps {
630	                num: num as u32,
631	                den: den as u32,
632	            })
633	        }
634	        _ => Err(format!(
635	            "export fps must be [num, den] with non-zero terms, not {}",
636	            describe(value)
637	        )),
638	    }
639	}

651	/// The `range` override as the raw `(start, duration)` pair it asked for,
652	/// each falling back to its half of `default` — which is `(0, the whole
653	/// project)`, so `{"start": …}` alone keeps the project's length and
654	/// `{"duration": …}` alone keeps its start.
655	///
656	/// RAW is the word: nothing here snaps or clamps. Both are decisions about
657	/// a project and an export rate, which this file knows nothing about, and
658	/// the ORDER of the two (snap first, then clamp) is load-bearing enough to
659	/// stay visible where the settings are resolved.
660	pub(crate) fn range(
661	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
662	    default: (Ticks, Ticks),
663	) -> Result<(Ticks, Ticks), String> {
664	    let Some(range) = field(overrides, "range") else {
665	        return Ok(default);
666	    };
667	    if !range.is_object() {
668	        return Err(format!(
669	            "export range must be a json object with start and duration, not {}",
670	            describe(range)
671	        ));
672	    }
673	    let (mut start, mut duration) = default;
674	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "start") {
675	        start = ticks(value, "range start")?;
676	    }
677	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "duration") {
678	        duration = ticks(value, "range duration")?;
679	    }
680	    Ok((start, duration))
681	}

750	//! The containers Frame Job writes (spec §7.8), and the four questions
751	//! each one answers about ITSELF: its extension, its UTI, whether a
752	//! leading index is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all.
753	//!
754	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
755	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
756	//! as codec-export C1's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
757	//! [`Container`], so every `crate::export_table::Container` path holds.
758	
759	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
760	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
761	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
762	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
763	pub(crate) enum Container {
764	    Mov,
765	    Mp4,
766	    M4a,
767	    Wav,
768	    Aiff,
769	    Gif,
770	    Apng,
771	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
772	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
773	    Webm,
774	}
775	
776	impl Container {
777	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
778	        match self {
779	            Container::Mov => "mov",
780	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
781	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
782	            Container::Wav => "wav",
783	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
784	            Container::Gif => "gif",
785	            Container::Apng => "apng",
786	            Container::Webm => "webm",
787	        }
788	    }
789	
790	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
791	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
792	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
793	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
794	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
795	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
796	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
797	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
798	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
799	    ///
800	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
801	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
802	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
803	    ///
804	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
805	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
806	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
807	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
808	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
809	        match self {
810	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
811	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
812	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
813	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
814	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
815	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
816	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
817	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
818	        }
819	    }
820	
821	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
822	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
823	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
824	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
825	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
826	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
827	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
828	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
829	    /// starts on the first frame, and
830	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
831	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would
832	    /// be a request the writer has nothing to do about. A WebM's index (its
833	    /// SeekHead) is already at the front, so the flag is off and inert there
834	    /// too (spec §11 CX-15 (1)).
835	    pub(crate) fn optimizes_for_network(self) -> bool {
836	        matches!(self, Container::Mp4 | Container::M4a)
837	    }
838	
839	    /// Whether the container can hold sound. Every movie container can,
840	    /// and M4A, WAV and AIFF are nothing else; GIF and APNG are picture
841	    /// formats with no audio track in the file format at all, so
842	    /// `audio: false` for those is a fact about the container rather than
843	    /// a decision about the project.
844	    pub(crate) fn carries_audio(self) -> bool {
845	        !matches!(self, Container::Gif | Container::Apng)
846	    }
847	}

3	/// What one bundled-encoder export costs (spec §11 CX-18): its resident peak, which the
4	/// Export Queue's limit books (`ExportEncoderLedger`), and its time, which the export
5	/// sheet's estimate reads. Two tables keyed alike, each figure carrying its source.
6	///
7	/// **Both are measured, never guessed, and both are a table edit to replace.** The figures
8	/// are `tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`'s, recorded in `archive/codec-export.md`'s
9	/// "## C6a" and "## C6b" (`vp9_alpha_webm`'s first in "## C5"'s fix pass): one fresh Release
10	/// instance per key and size, the resident peak above the instance's own after a warming
11	/// frame, and the export's wall time. The TIME figures are C6b's: on an idle machine, the
12	/// GH5 4K clip on a 25 fps canvas, the median of three runs per key and size over 250 and
13	/// 50 frames, which separate the fixed start from the per-frame time. A MEMORY figure is the
14	/// larger of C6a's (C5's) single run and C6b's peaks, its source naming the run that won.
15	///
16	/// A figure is given at 1920 × 1080 and 3840 × 2160 and read at an export's pixels:
17	/// proportionally below 1080p, linearly through both points above it, extrapolated past 4K.
18	
19	/// What a cost is keyed by: the row, the AV1 speed, and the bit depth the encoder runs at.
20	struct ExportEncoderKey: Hashable {
21	    /// `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm`.
22	    let preset: String
23	    /// The AV1 rows' speed (`settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced`); nil on every other row.
24	    let speed: EncoderSpeed?
25	    /// 10 on `svt_av1` (CX-14: always 10-bit); on `libvpx` 10 for `hlg`/`pq` (Profile 2,
26	    /// CX-16 (3)), else 8.
27	    let bits: Int
28	
29	    init(preset: String, speed: EncoderSpeed?, bits: Int) {
30	        self.preset = preset
31	        self.speed = speed
32	        self.bits = bits
33	    }
34	
35	    /// The key of an export's settings; nil for an AVFoundation row (no `writer`).
36	    init?(settings: ExportSettings) {
37	        guard let writer = settings.writer else { return nil }
38	        let av1 = writer == "svt_av1"
39	        let deep = settings.dynamicRange == .hlg || settings.dynamicRange == .pq
40	        self.init(
41	            preset: settings.preset, speed: av1 ? settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced : nil,
42	            bits: av1 || deep ? 10 : 8)
43	    }
44	}

46	/// One measured quantity at the two sizes, and where it came from.
47	struct ExportEncoderFigure {
48	    /// At 1920 × 1080.
49	    let at1080: Double
50	    /// At 3840 × 2160.
51	    let at2160: Double
52	    /// The run, its date, the machine and its load.
53	    let source: String
54	
55	    /// The figure at `pixels`: proportional below 1080p, linear through both points above.
56	    func value(pixels: Int) -> Double {
57	        let low = Double(ExportEncoderCosts.pixels1080)
58	        let high = Double(ExportEncoderCosts.pixels2160)
59	        let p = Double(max(0, pixels))
60	        if p <= low { return at1080 * p / low }
61	        return at1080 + (at2160 - at1080) * (p - low) / (high - low)
62	    }
63	}
