217	/// The app-wide account of the bundled-encoder exports running now (spec §11 CX-18): the
218	/// Export Queue's job and every Export… progress sheet's, each booked from just before its
219	/// exporter starts to its finish, at the resident peak `ExportEncoderCosts.memory` measured
220	/// for its key and size.
221	///
222	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
223	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
224	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
225	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
226	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
227	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.
228	///
229	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
230	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when
231	/// nothing is booked — one export always runs, however large — or when the booked costs and
232	/// its own fit.
233	///
234	/// Main thread only, like the queue and the sheets that book into it, and AppKit-free so a
235	/// probe compiles it headless (`tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`).
236	final class ExportEncoderLedger {
237	    /// The app's one ledger. The queue observes it and the sheets book into it.
238	    static let shared = ExportEncoderLedger()
239	
240	    /// Posted after a booking is added or removed, with the ledger as the `object`. The
241	    /// queue re-runs `start()` on it, so a held job launches when a booking ends.
242	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
243	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportEncoderLedgerDidChange")
244	
245	    /// The Mac's memory the budget is a share of — `ProcessInfo`'s, which a probe sets to
246	    /// ask what a Mac of another size would admit.
247	    var physicalMemory: UInt64
248	
249	    private var entries: [(token: UInt64, cost: UInt64)] = []
250	    private var nextToken: UInt64 = 1
251	
252	    init(physicalMemory: UInt64 = ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory) {
253	        self.physicalMemory = physicalMemory
254	    }
255	
256	    /// What bundled-encoder exports may hold together, in bytes.
257	    var budget: UInt64 { Self.budget(physicalMemory: physicalMemory) }
258	
259	    /// Each running booking's cost, in booking order.
260	    var runningCosts: [UInt64] { entries.map(\.cost) }
261	
262	    // MARK: - The rule
263	
264	    /// A quarter of physical memory (CX-18 (3)).
265	    static func budget(physicalMemory: UInt64) -> UInt64 { physicalMemory / 4 }
266	
267	    /// Whether a job costing `cost` may start beside `running`: always when nothing runs,
268	    /// else when the sum fits `budget` (CX-18 (5)).
269	    static func admits(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> Bool {
270	        guard !running.isEmpty else { return true }
271	        let (inUse, over) = running.reduce((UInt64(0), false)) { sum, next in
272	            let added = sum.0.addingReportingOverflow(next)
273	            return (added.partialValue, sum.1 || added.overflow)
274	        }
275	        let total = inUse.addingReportingOverflow(cost)
276	        return !over && !total.overflow && total.partialValue <= budget
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The held job's sentence: what runs, what the Mac allows, what this one needs.
280	    static func waitingSentence(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> String {
281	        let inUse = running.reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 &+ $1 }
282	        return "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about "
283	            + "\(gigabytes(inUse)) of the \(gigabytes(budget)) this Mac allows them, and this "
284	            + "one needs about \(gigabytes(cost))."
285	    }
286	
287	    private static func gigabytes(_ bytes: UInt64) -> String {
288	        String(format: "%.1f GB", Double(bytes) / 1_073_741_824)
289	    }
290	
291	    // MARK: - Asking
292	
293	    /// Whether `settings` may start now, leaving out the booking `token` (the queue's own
294	    /// running job, which a waiting job is behind anyway). True for an AVFoundation row.
295	    func admits(_ settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> Bool {
296	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return true }
297	        return Self.admits(
298	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
299	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
300	    }
301	
302	    /// The held sentence for `settings`, or nil when it is admitted.
303	    func waitingSentence(for settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> String? {
304	        guard !admits(settings, ignoring: token) else { return nil }
305	        return Self.waitingSentence(
306	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
307	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
308	    }
309	
310	    private func costs(ignoring token: UInt64?) -> [UInt64] {
311	        entries.filter { $0.token != token }.map(\.cost)
312	    }
313	
314	    // MARK: - Booking
315	
316	    /// Books an export about to start and answers its token, or nil — booking nothing —
317	    /// for an AVFoundation row. Called BEFORE `Exporter.export`, whose early refusals finish
318	    /// synchronously inside it.
319	    func begin(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> UInt64? {
320	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return nil }
321	        let token = nextToken
322	        nextToken += 1
323	        entries.append(
324	            (token, ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget)))
325	        post()
326	        return token
327	    }
328	
329	    /// Ends a booking. A nil or unknown token is a no-op; a removal posts, and the queue's
330	    /// observer may launch its next job — and book it — inside this call, which is why a
331	    /// caller clears its own token BEFORE calling this.
332	    func end(_ token: UInt64?) {
333	        guard let token, let index = entries.firstIndex(where: { $0.token == token }) else {
334	            return
335	        }
336	        entries.remove(at: index)
337	        post()
338	    }
339	
340	    private func post() {
341	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
342	    }
343	}

406	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
407	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met

425	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for

432	
433	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
434	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
435	    ///
436	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
437	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
438	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
439	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
440	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
441	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets

444	    ///
445	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
446	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is

449	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
450	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
451	    struct QualityTier {
452	        let name: String
453	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
454	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
455	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
456	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
457	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
458	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
459	
460	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
461	        ///
462	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
463	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
464	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
465	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
466	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
467	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
468	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
469	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
470	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
471	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
472	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
473	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
474	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
475	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
476	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
477	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
478	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
479	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
480	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
481	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
482	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
483	        }

485	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
486	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
487	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
488	        }
489	    }

491	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
492	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
493	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
494	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
495	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
496	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
497	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
498	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
499	    ]
500	
501	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
502	    ///
503	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
504	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending

508	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
509	
510	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
511	            self.preset = preset
512	        }
513	
514	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
515	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
516	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
517	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
518	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
519	        }
520	
521	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
522	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
523	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
524	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
525	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
526	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
527	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
528	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
529	        }
530	
531	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
532	
533	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
534	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
535	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
536	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
537	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
538	
539	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
540	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
541	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
542	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
543	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a

545	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
546	
547	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG

550

555	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the

558

571	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
572	        let container = container.lowercased()

586	/// The export sheet's ANSWER half: read the controls, ask the core what they

588	///
589	/// The seam is the §7 rule the sheet is built on, drawn as a file boundary.
590	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` owns the controls — it makes the popups and
591	/// the fields, lists the sizes, and hands a person something to choose with.
592	/// Nothing there decides an output size, a rate or a duration, because
593	/// nothing in this dialog does: every number the card shows comes back from
594	/// `rc_export_settings`, and this file is the whole of the round trip. It
595	/// turns a selection into the override object the core reads (`overrides()`),
596	/// sends it (`resolve()`), and writes the answer into the readout, the
597	/// footnote and the controls' enablement (`syncReadout()`). Between those
598	/// three, the `current…` accessors are the one place a popup index becomes a
599	/// meaning, so a control's index arithmetic is never spelled twice.
600	///
601	/// The one number the sheet DOES choose is the bit rate, and it is here for
602	/// that reason rather than beside the Quality popup: a tier is a REQUEST

606	/// the popup.
607	///
608	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114

610	/// methods, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
611	/// visibility**, for the reason `ExporterLoudness.swift` records — `private`
612	/// on an extension member reaches only its own file, and a stored property
613	/// cannot live in an extension at all. So every control, every field and
614	/// every piece of state this file reads is internal in the file that
615	/// declares it, and the four members the controls call back into —
616	/// `resolve()`, `currentPreset`, `isCustomSize` and `isCustomLoudness` — are
617	/// internal here. Everything else below stays `private`, because a `private`
618	/// extension member is reachable from the rest of THIS file, and nothing
619	/// outside it has ever asked.
620	/// Phase 7 added the OTHER direction to this file, and it belongs here for the
621	/// same reason the first one does: `currentChoice` is a reading of the
622	/// controls, exactly as `overrides()` is, and `apply(_:)` is that reading run
623	/// backwards. Keeping the pair together is what makes a saved preset and the
624	/// remembered choice provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand —
625	/// there is one account of what a stored choice means, and both halves of it
626	/// are on one screen.

628	
629	    // MARK: - Resolving
630	
631	    /// Asks the core for the settings the current controls describe, then
632	    /// repaints the readout from the answer.
633	    ///
634	    /// A refusal is not an error dialog: the message goes in the readout and
635	    /// Export greys out, so a bad override reads as "this combination is not
636	    /// available" rather than interrupting the person adjusting it.
637	    func resolve() {
638	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset else {
639	            resolved = nil
640	            resolveError = "This build has no export presets."
641	            syncReadout()
642	            return
643	        }
644	        // A format whose sizes the core could not list is not exported at
645	        // all, whatever the settings call would answer: the one refusal
646	        // `rc_export_sizes` shares with `rc_export_settings` is an unknown
647	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
648	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
649	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
650	        if let message = sizesError {
651	            resolved = nil
652	            resolveError = message
653	            syncReadout()
654	            return
655	        }
656	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
657	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
658	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
659	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
660	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
661	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
662	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
663	        {
664	            resolved = nil
665	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
666	            syncReadout()
667	            return
668	        }
669	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
670	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
671	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
672	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
673	            resolved = nil
674	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
675	            syncReadout()
676	            return
677	        }
678	        do {
679	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
680	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
681	            resolveError = nil
682	        } catch {
683	            resolved = nil
684	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
685	        }
686	        syncReadout()
687	    }

691	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
692	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
693	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off
694	    /// an audio-only row carries no size, and one saved off a GIF carries no
695	    /// loudness — the record says what was actually asked for and never what
696	    /// a greyed-out popup happened to be sitting on.
697	    ///
698	    /// **The burn-in is gated by that same rule and used not to be**, which
699	    /// broke the sentence above rather than any of the core's: a tick made on
700	    /// an H.264 row and carried across to WAV was written into the record
701	    /// beside a size, an fps and a tier all three deliberately left empty, so
702	    /// a named preset — and the remembered choice, which is this same
703	    /// value — said a file with no picture would carry a burn-in. It is not an
704	    /// override, so nothing downstream ever refused it; `Applies.burnIn`
705	    /// (below) is where it is refused now.
706	    ///
707	    /// The `name` is empty: naming a choice is the Save… item's business.
708	    var currentChoice: ExportChoice {
709	        var choice = ExportChoice(presetID: currentPreset?.id ?? "")
710	        if currentApplies.size {
711	            if isCustomSize {
712	                choice.customSize = [clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField)]
713	            } else {
714	                let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
715	                // The ROW's id, never its index (`ExportChoice.sizeRow`).
716	                // Index 0 is recorded like any other: it is a row a person
717	                // chose, and `sizeOverride()`'s decision to send it as no
718	                // override at all is about the CORE's default and not about
719	                // what the popup was showing.
720	                if index >= 0, index < visibleSizes.count {
721	                    choice.sizeRow = visibleSizes[index].id
722	                }
723	            }
724	        }
725	        choice.fps = currentRate.map { [$0.num, $0.den] }
726	        choice.qualityTier = currentTier?.name
727	        choice.loudness = currentLoudness
728	        choice.inOutRange = rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1
729	        choice.burnInTimecode = currentApplies.burnIn && recipeOptions.burnInTimecode
730	        choice.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeedChoice.rawValue
731	        choice.audioBits = audioBitsChoice
732	        choice.stems = stemsChoice
733	        return choice
734	    }

736	    /// Writes a stored choice back into the controls. **The order is
737	    /// load-bearing and this method is where it is written down**; every
738	    /// caller — the remembered choice in `loadView`, a preset picked from the
739	    /// popup — goes through here so there is only ever one order.
740	    ///
741	    /// 1. **Format FIRST, before the sizes are listed.** A programmatic
742	    ///    `selectItem` sends no action, so `formatChanged`'s `sizesPreset`
743	    ///    guard never fires and nothing rebuilds on its own; listing after the
744	    ///    pick is what makes the rows this format's rows.
745	    /// 2. **Size AFTER `rebuildSizes()`**, which ends with an unconditional
746	    ///    `sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)` and would undo a selection made before
747	    ///    it.
748	    /// 3. **A custom LOUDNESS selects "Custom…" first and fills the field
749	    ///    second**, because `syncReadout` overwrites that field from the popup
750	    ///    whenever the popup is not on Custom — and `resolve()` runs one
751	    ///    `syncReadout` after this returns.
752	    /// 4. **`in_out` degrades to "Whole project"** on a document that has no
753	    ///    range: the popup only carries that row when `range != nil`, so
754	    ///    selecting index 1 would select nothing at all.
755	    ///
756	    /// It does NOT resolve. The caller does, once, after the last control has
757	    /// moved — a resolve per control would be six FFI round trips to paint one
758	    /// card.
759	    func apply(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
760	        if let index = presets.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == choice.presetID }) {
761	            formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
762	        }
763	        rebuildSizes()
764	        applySize(choice)
765	
766	        if let fps = choice.fps, fps.count == 2,
767	            let index = Self.rates.firstIndex(where: { $0.num == fps[0] && $0.den == fps[1] })
768	        {
769	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
770	        } else {
771	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
772	        }
773	
774	        if let name = choice.qualityTier,
775	            let index = Self.tiers.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == name })
776	        {
777	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
778	        } else {
779	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
780	        }
781	
782	        applyLoudness(choice)
783	        rangePopup.selectItem(at: choice.inOutRange && range != nil ? 1 : 0)
784	        burnInCheckbox.state = choice.burnInTimecode ? .on : .off
785	        applySpeed(choice)
786	        applyAudioBits(choice)
787	        applyStems(choice)
788	    }

790	    /// Step 2, after the listing. A row whose id this format does not offer —
791	    /// a GIF's cap under H.264, or a row `visibleSizes` hid because an earlier
792	    /// row already has its numbers — falls back to the SAME NUMBERS under
793	    /// whatever row does show them, and only then to the format's default.
794	    /// Hiding is a tidiness of the popup's (`visibleSizes`), so a choice of
795	    /// "1080p" on a 1920 × 1080 document has to land on "Document size" rather
796	    /// than be dropped: it is the same export.
797	    private func applySize(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
798	        if let row = choice.sizeRow {
799	            if let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == row }) {
800	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
801	                return
802	            }
803	            if let hidden = sizes.first(where: { $0.id == row }),
804	                let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: {
805	                    $0.width == hidden.width && $0.height == hidden.height
806	                })
807	            {
808	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
809	                return
810	            }
811	            return
812	        }
813	        guard let custom = choice.customSize, custom.count == 2 else { return }
814	        // "Custom…" is the item after the last visible row.
815	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: visibleSizes.count)
816	        widthField.integerValue = custom[0]
817	        heightField.integerValue = custom[1]
818	    }

822	        guard let target = choice.loudness else {
823	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
824	            return
825	        }
826	        if let index = Self.loudnessTargets.firstIndex(of: target) {
827	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
828	            return
829	        }
830	        loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1)
831	        loudnessField.doubleValue = target
832	    }

844	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before

871	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
872	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
873	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
874	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
875	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
876	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
877	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
878	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]

880	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
881	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue

887	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
888	    ///
889	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
890	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
891	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
892	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
893	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
894	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
895	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
896	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
897	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
898	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
899	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
900	        if isCustomSize {
901	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
902	        }
903	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
904	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
905	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
906	    }

908	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
909	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
910	    ///
911	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
912	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
913	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
914	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
915	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
916	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
917	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
918	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
919	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
920	        // size (`export.rs`).
921	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
922	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
923	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
924	            width = size.width
925	            height = size.height
926	        }
927	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
928	    }

930	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
931	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
932	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
933	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
934	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
935	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
936	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
937	        let applies = currentApplies
938	        let format = requestedFormat()
939	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
940	            overrides["width"] = size.width
941	            overrides["height"] = size.height
942	        }
943	        if let fps = currentRate {
944	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
945	        }
946	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
947	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
948	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
949	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
950	        // row has neither.
951	        if let tier = currentTier {
952	            if applies.videoBitrate {
953	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
954	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
955	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
956	            }
957	            if applies.audioBitrate {
958	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
959	            }
960	        }
961	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
962	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
963	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
964	        if let target = currentLoudness {
965	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
966	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
967	        }
968	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
969	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
970	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
971	        // in/out range, silently.
972	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
973	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
974	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
975	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
976	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
977	            overrides["range"] = [
978	                "start": range.start,
979	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
980	            ]
981	        }
982	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides
983	    }

985	    private func clampedSize(_ field: NSTextField) -> Int {
986	        min(max(field.integerValue, Self.sizeRange.lowerBound), Self.sizeRange.upperBound)
987	    }

989	    /// Rewrites the readout, the footnote, the controls' enablement and the
990	    /// Export button from `resolved`. The size fields follow the core while
991	    /// a row of the Size popup owns the size, which is what makes "Custom…"
992	    /// readable: pick it and the fields already hold the numbers to edit.
993	    ///
994	    /// Enablement comes from the FORMAT rather than from `resolved`, so a
995	    /// refused resolve leaves the controls where they were instead of
996	    /// greying out the very one that has to be changed to fix it.
997	    private func syncReadout() {
998	        let applies = currentApplies
999	        let custom = isCustomSize
1000	        // A popup whose listing failed holds nothing to choose, and the one
1001	        // control that can put a size back is the Format popup, so the size
1002	        // controls grey out with it — the exception to the rule in the doc
1003	        // comment above, for the one refusal no size can fix.
1004	        let listed = sizesError == nil
1005	        sizePopup.isEnabled = applies.size && listed
1006	        for field in [widthField, heightField] {
1007	            field.isEnabled = applies.size && listed && custom
1008	            field.textColor = field.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
1009	        }
1010	        ratePopup.isEnabled = applies.frameRate
1011	        qualityPopup.isEnabled = applies.quality
1012	        syncQualityTitles(applies)
1013	        loudnessPopup.isEnabled = applies.loudness
1014	        loudnessField.isEnabled = applies.loudness && isCustomLoudness
1015	        loudnessField.textColor = loudnessField.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
1016	        if !isCustomLoudness {
1017	            // The field mirrors the row that is chosen, exactly as the size
1018	            // fields mirror the core's answer, so picking "Custom…" starts
1019	            // from the number that was in force a moment before. "Off" has no
1020	            // number of its own, so it shows the first target — the one
1021	            // Custom is most likely to be an adjustment of.
1022	            loudnessField.doubleValue = currentLoudness ?? Self.loudnessTargets[0]
1023	        }
1024	        // The last control on the card, and the last one to be gated: the
1025	        // burn-in stayed live on the three audio-only rows, alone among the
1026	        // format-dependent controls, offering to write a timecode into a file
1027	        // with no picture to write it into.
1028	        burnInCheckbox.isEnabled = applies.burnIn
1029	        syncDynamicRange(applies)
1030	        syncSpeed(applies)
1031	        syncAudioBits(applies)
1032	        syncStems(applies)
1033	
1034	        guard let settings = resolved else {
1035	            summaryLabel.stringValue = resolveError ?? "These settings are not available."
1036	            summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
1037	            footnote.stringValue = ""
1038	            footnote.toolTip = nil
1039	            exportButton?.isEnabled = false
1040	            return
1041	        }
1042	        if !custom {
1043	            widthField.integerValue = settings.width
1044	            heightField.integerValue = settings.height
1045	        }
1046	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
1047	        summaryLabel.stringValue = summary(for: settings)
1048	        footnote.stringValue = footnoteText(for: settings)
1049	        footnote.toolTip = footnote.stringValue
1050	        exportButton?.isEnabled = settings.duration > 0
1051	    }

1053	    /// Re-titles the tier rows with the rate each would ask for at the size
1054	    /// and frame rate now chosen. "High" on its own says nothing; "High ·
1055	    /// 8.0 Mbps" is the control's actual promise, and it has to move when
1056	    /// the frame it is a rate for moves.
1057	    private func syncQualityTitles(_ applies: Applies) {
1058	        let format = requestedFormat()
1059	        let codec = currentPreset?.codec ?? ""
1060	        for (index, tier) in Self.tiers.enumerated() {
1061	            guard let item = qualityPopup.item(at: index + 1) else { continue }
1062	            if applies.videoBitrate {
1063	                let rate = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
1064	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps, codec: codec)
1065	                let soft = applies.softCap ? "usually ≤ " : ""   // spec §11 CX-13
1066	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(soft)\(Self.rateText(rate))"
1067	            } else if applies.audioBitrate {
1068	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(Self.rateText(tier.audioBitsPerSecond))"
1069	            } else {
1070	                item.title = tier.name
1071	            }
1072	        }
1073	    }

1075	    /// The one-line description of what the file will contain.
1076	    private func summary(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
1077	        if settings.isAudioOnly {
1078	            // Milliseconds rather than frames, and no rate in the line: audio
1079	            // has no frames, which is the same reason the rate popup is
1080	            // greyed out for this preset.
1081	            let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: false)
1082	            return "Audio only · \(duration)"
1083	        }
1084	        let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: true)
1085	        var text = "\(settings.width) × \(settings.height) · \(settings.fps.displayName) fps · "
1086	            + duration
1087	        if Self.isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
1088	            // What a GIF or an APNG costs is frames, not seconds — and it
1089	            // carries no audio however much of it the timeline has, which is
1090	            // worth saying before the export rather than after it.
1091	            text += " · \(settings.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0) frames, no audio"
1092	        }
1093	        // A bundled encoder's estimate (spec §11 CX-18 (9)).
1094	        if let line = ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: settings) { text += "\n" + line }
1095	        return text
1096	    }

1098	    /// The footnote over the buttons: the codec, the container, and the rates
1099	    /// the CORE resolved — never the ones the tier asked for, and not filtered by
1100	    /// what the sheet thinks applies, since a preset is free to carry a rate
1101	    /// of its own that no control here offered.
1102	    ///
1103	    /// The distinction matters because `export.rs` drops override keys it
1104	    /// does not know, silently (the same trap the range comment above names).
1105	    /// A tier picked against a core that has no bit-rate overrides has to
1106	    /// read as "the format's own rate" rather than let the popup imply a
1107	    /// number the file will not have.
1108	    private func footnoteText(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
1109	        var parts = [settings.codec.uppercased()]
1110	        let container = settings.container.uppercased()
1111	        // A frame-sequence preset's codec IS its container: "GIF · GIF".
1112	        if container != parts[0] { parts.append(container) }
1113	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed { parts.append(speed.menuName) }
1114	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { parts.append("24-bit") }
1115	        if case let n = settings.stems.count, n > 0 { parts.append(n == 1 ? "1 stem" : "\(n) stems") }
1116	        if let rate = settings.videoBitrate {
1117	            // A bundled encoder's rate is a soft cap (spec §11 CX-13).
1118	            parts.append((settings.writer == nil ? "" : "usually ≤ ") + Self.rateText(rate))
1119	        }
1120	        if let rate = settings.audioBitrate {
1121	            parts.append("\(Self.rateText(rate)) audio")
1122	        }
1123	        if currentTier != nil, settings.videoBitrate == nil, settings.audioBitrate == nil {
1124	            parts.append("format's own rate")
1125	        }
1126	        // The core's echo, not the popup's row: a build whose
1127	        // `export_settings` has never heard of `loudness_lufs` drops the key
1128	        // silently, and the footnote must not then promise a normalisation
1129	        // the file will not have.
1130	        if let target = settings.loudnessLufs {
1131	            parts.append(
1132	                String(format: "%g LUFS", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−"))
1133	        }
1134	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — the core's own
1135	        // answer for this row (`ExportSettings.alpha`), never a reading of the
1136	        // canvas. It is the one place the sheet says which format keeps a
1137	        // transparent background, and it is a POSITIVE claim only: the rows
1138	        // that answer false are not enumerated here, because the flag says
1139	        // what the settings object says and the footnote's whole rule is that
1140	        // it reports the core rather than the popup.
1141	        if settings.alpha { parts.append("alpha") }
1142	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
1143	    }
1144	}

1	//! The export table: the closed set of files Frame Job can write, and
2	//! nothing whatever about writing one of them (spec §7.8).
3	//!
4	//! Split out of `export.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md: a module
5	//! at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on), which
6	//! that file paid once already — `describe` and the override readers went
7	//! to `export_overrides.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and this is the
8	//! second cut, taken in phase 7 for the same reason and along a different
9	//! seam. The rule both follow: cut where somebody can NAME the line, and
10	//! re-export the piece taken out whole, so not one path anywhere else
11	//! changes.
12	//!
13	//! # The seam: a fact about the world, not about a document
14	//!
15	//! Everything in this file is a constant, and none of it can be
16	//! influenced by a project. [`Container`] is the set of files this
17	//! application knows how to produce and the four questions each one
18	//! answers about ITSELF — its extension, its UTI, whether a leading index
19	//! is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all. [`Preset`] is one
20	//! encoding placed in one of those containers, and [`PRESETS`] is every
21	//! such row in menu order. An APNG's type identifier is PNG's whatever
22	//! the timeline holds; GIF caps its size because of what a palettised
23	//! frame-by-frame format costs, not because of anybody's canvas.
24	//!
25	//! `export.rs` keeps the other half, and the other half is the one with a
26	//! `&self`: `Project::export_settings` is the only code that reads a
27	//! canvas, a duration, a rate or an override, and it is where those meet
28	//! a row from here. So the line runs between them in one direction only —
29	//! the resolver knows the table, the table knows nothing about a project
30	//! — which is also why the module doc that explains the whole export
31	//! design stays over there rather than following the rows here. This file
32	//! says what CAN be written. That one says what this particular document,
33	//! written that way, comes out as.
34	//!
35	//! # Paths
36	//!
37	//! `export.rs` re-exports [`presets`] and [`preset`] at their old names,
38	//! so `crate::export::presets()` (`ffi_query.rs`) and
39	//! `crate::export::preset(id)` (`export_size.rs`) resolve exactly as they
40	//! did — the same trick, and for the same reason, as the `describe`
41	//! re-export sitting a few lines above them. What the cut did cost is
42	//! visibility, mechanically: the [`Preset`] fields the resolver reads and
43	//! the four [`Container`] questions it asks are `pub(crate)` now, where
44	//! one file had been able to keep them private. [`fps_json`] came across
45	//! with the table rather than staying with the resolver and is
46	//! `pub(crate)` for it: both sides spell a rate, and its being one
47	//! function is the whole of why they cannot disagree about the shape.
48

51	pub(crate) use crate::export_container::Container;
52	pub(crate) use crate::export_encoder::{EncoderSpeed, Writer};
53	pub(crate) use crate::export_preset::{fps_json, Preset};
54	use crate::time::Fps;

56	/// The §7.8 set: one row per ENCODING, in menu order. A row is a container
57	/// and a codec and nothing else — no size, no rate — so an export is at the
58	/// document's own size and rate unless a person asks for another, through
59	/// the Size popup the sheet fills from `Project::export_sizes` or the
60	/// overrides a script sends. The size used to be part of the row ("H.264
61	/// 1080p", "HEVC 4K"), and that shape made the format menu two questions
62	/// asked as one: picking HEVC meant picking 1080p or 4K with it, and a
63	/// 1440p or a vertical document had no row that fit it at all. Two
64	/// questions get two controls, and the format is only ever the encoding.
65	///
66	/// The two image rows are the exception and keep a size and a rate,
67	/// because for them the numbers ARE what makes the row worth having: a GIF
68	/// or an APNG costs frames × pixels with no inter-frame prediction to
69	/// spend against, so "at the document's size and rate" is a file no one
70	/// can send, and the cap is the point of the format rather than a default
71	/// it happens to carry (§7.8; the row comments argue each number). Both
72	/// caps are still defaults a size or fps override replaces, and
73	/// `export_sizes` lists each as the first row of its list.
74	///
75	/// The FIRST row is the default: `rc_export_presets` is "in menu order"
76	/// and the export sheet opens on its first entry, so whatever sits here is
77	/// what ⌘E writes unless a person picks otherwise. H.264 in MP4 is the
78	/// file every player and every upload form takes, which is why it leads
79	/// and HEVC — half the size, not yet everywhere — follows.
80	///
81	/// Each movie row carries an `AVAssetExportSession` preset name for the
82	/// record: the three "highest quality" names are the ones a session would
83	/// take the composition's own size under rather than fit it to a fixed
84	/// frame, which is exactly a row with no size of its own. Nothing runs a
85	/// session any more (§7.8), so on the Swift side the name is only the
86	/// signal that AVFoundation can write the row at all; the two image rows
87	/// carry none, which is the signal to write them frame by frame through
88	/// ImageIO instead. The two LPCM rows repeat `audio_m4a`'s name for the
89	/// same reason and with the field doc's caveat: AVFoundation has no
90	/// session preset for LPCM, and a null would route a WAV to ImageIO.
91	///
92	/// **No row carries a default bitrate, deliberately.** On the session path
93	/// the preset name IS the ladder — `AVAssetExportSession` exposes no way to
94	/// set a rate — so a number here would be one the export cannot honour,
95	/// which is worse than none at all. On the writer path VideoToolbox derives
96	/// a rate from the frame size, which beats any constant this table could
97	/// hold: one that suits 4K wastes half the file at 720p. ProRes is fixed by
98	/// its profile and ignores a request outright, and GIF and APNG have no
99	/// bitrate to set. A bitrate is therefore something the user asks for — the
100	/// `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` overrides — never something a preset
101	/// assumes on their behalf.
102	const PRESETS: [Preset; 15] = [

104	    // and every script that calls it spells them, so a row is named for
105	    // the encoding alone — `h264`, not `h264_document` — because the size
106	    // is no longer anything the id could say.
107	    Preset {
108	        id: "h264",
109	        name: "H.264 (MP4)",
110	        container: Container::Mp4,
111	        codec: "h264",
112	        video: true,
113	        alpha: false,
114	        size: None,
115	        fps: None,
116	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality"),
117	        writer: None,
118	    },
119	    Preset {
120	        id: "hevc",
121	        name: "HEVC (MP4)",
122	        container: Container::Mp4,
123	        codec: "hevc",
124	        video: true,
125	        alpha: false,
126	        size: None,
127	        fps: None,
128	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHEVCHighestQuality"),
129	        writer: None,
130	    },
131	    // HEVC with an alpha channel (spec §11 G-33), directly after the row it
132	    // is a variant of. It is the DELIVERY row that keeps transparency — a
133	    // title or a lower third a web page or another editor plays over its
134	    // own background, at HEVC's size where `prores_4444` is a master — and
135	    // it is a MOV because that is the container AVFoundation writes the
136	    // codec into (it refuses it an `.mp4`). The codec is spelled as the id

138	    // `AVVideoCodecType.hevcWithAlpha`, and the sheet's Quality tiers and
139	    // bit-rate controls read the `hevc` prefix, so it takes HEVC's.

142	        name: "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)",
143	        container: Container::Mov,
144	        codec: "hevc_alpha",
145	        video: true,
146	        alpha: true,
147	        size: None,
148	        fps: None,
149	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetHEVCHighestQualityWithAlpha"),
150	        writer: None,

192	        id: "av1_webm",

194	        container: Container::Webm,
195	        codec: "av1",
196	        video: true,
197	        alpha: false,
198	        size: None,
199	        fps: None,
200	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough"),
201	        writer: Some(Writer::SvtAv1),

275	    // under them and want the smaller of the two files, so 422 stays the

295	        // refuse a format this table advertises. The name is
296	        // AVFoundation's real ProRes 4444 preset and is a record of what
297	        // writes the row, nothing more — nothing has run a session since

299	        avf_preset: Some("AVAssetExportPresetAppleProRes4444LPCM"),
300	        writer: None,
301	    },
302	    Preset {
303	        id: "audio_m4a",
304	        name: "Audio only (M4A)",
305	        container: Container::M4a,
306	        codec: "aac",
307	        video: false,
308	        alpha: false,
309	        size: None,
310	        fps: None,

312	        writer: None,

380	        size: Some((480, 270)),

403	        size: Some((960, 540)),
404	        fps: Some(Fps { num: 25, den: 1 }),

427	//! One row of the export table (spec §7.8): [`Preset`], what each row
428	//! answers about itself, and [`fps_json`], the rate's one spelling.
429	//!
430	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
431	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
432	//! as codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
433	//! both, so every `crate::export_table::Preset` and
434	//! `crate::export_table::fps_json` path holds; `name` and `to_json` became
435	//! `pub(crate)` because the table's rows and `presets` stay behind.
436	
437	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
438	
439	use crate::export_container::Container;
440	use crate::export_encoder::{EncoderSpeed, Writer};
441	use crate::time::Fps;

443	/// One row of the table. Crate-visible so `export_size.rs` can read the
444	/// cap and the codec of the row it lists sizes for, and so `export.rs`'s
445	/// resolver can read the rest, both through [`preset`]; every field is
446	/// `pub(crate)` because the table's rows are built in `export_table.rs`.
447	pub(crate) struct Preset {
448	    pub(crate) id: &'static str,
449	    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
450	    pub(crate) container: Container,
451	    pub(crate) codec: &'static str,
452	    /// False for the three audio-only presets; every other row carries
453	    /// video.
454	    pub(crate) video: bool,
455	    /// Whether this ENCODING carries an alpha channel — `hevc_alpha`,
456	    /// `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_4444` and `apng`, and nothing else. It says what the FILE can
457	    /// hold, and never that a particular canvas is translucent:
458	    /// `export_settings`
459	    /// emits one flat object for every row, so a flag derived from the
460	    /// project's background would report `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF
461	    /// and a WAV, which reads as a defect from either side of the FFI. A
462	    /// transparent canvas exported through a row with no fourth channel
463	    /// simply composites onto black, and the flag is what lets the sheet
464	    /// and the `export` tool say so before the file exists.
465	    ///
466	    /// **It is a `Preset` field and not a [`Container`] question**, which
467	    /// is the one thing worth arguing here, because the neighbouring
468	    /// capability [`Container::carries_audio`] IS a container question and
469	    /// the two look alike. Whether a file can hold a sound track is decided
470	    /// by the container's format — a GIF has no audio track to put samples
471	    /// in whatever you encode — so it is answered once for the container.
472	    /// A fourth channel is decided by the CODEC: `Container::Mov` hosts
473	    /// `prores_422` and `prores_4444` alike, and 422 cannot carry alpha at
474	    /// any bitrate, so a container-level answer would have to be wrong for
475	    /// one of the two rows. Same shape of fact, different owner.
476	    ///
477	    /// **`gif` is false and `apng` is true, and the difference is the word
478	    /// CHANNEL.** Both can show a transparent pixel, so both look alike
479	    /// from the outside and a reader who has exported one will call this
480	    /// row a mistake. APNG is true colour with a real fourth channel and a
481	    /// pixel may be any fraction of opaque. A GIF has ONE palette index
482	    /// nominated as transparent: a pixel is either that index or fully
483	    /// opaque, there is no partial value to store, and a soft edge against
484	    /// nothing comes out as a hard jagged one. A flag that answered "yes"
485	    /// for both would license the sheet to promise a translucent GIF.
486	    /// Measured on the way in, not assumed: an `apng` export of a
487	    /// transparent canvas decodes `pix_fmt=rgba` with its corner at
488	    /// alpha 0, and a `gif` of the same timeline decodes with the corner
489	    /// transparent through its palette and no partial value anywhere.
490	    pub(crate) alpha: bool,
491	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas size", which is what every movie
492	    /// row wants: a preset is an encoding, and the size is the document's
493	    /// unless a `width`/`height` override says otherwise. The resolver
494	    /// fills the canvas in for the audio-only rows too, so every settings
495	    /// object carries a width. Only the two image rows pin one — the cap
496	    /// `Project::export_sizes` lists as their default.
497	    pub(crate) size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
498	    /// `None` means "the project's canvas rate", which is what every movie
499	    /// preset wants. Only the image-sequence rows pin one, because their
500	    /// cost is frames × pixels and nothing else.
501	    pub(crate) fps: Option<Fps>,
502	    /// The `AVAssetExportSession` preset name, verbatim; `None` for a
503	    /// container AVFoundation cannot write.
504	    ///
505	    /// Since phase 5 the field means only **"AVFoundation can write this
506	    /// row"**, and the name itself is a record rather than an instruction.
507	    /// Nothing has run a session since M2, but `null` here is still the
508	    /// one thing routing an export to the ImageIO writer
509	    /// (`ExportSettings.isImageSequence` is literally `avPreset == nil`),
510	    /// so a row that AVFoundation writes must carry SOME name even when
511	    /// AVFoundation has no name for it. There is no `AVAssetExportPreset`
512	    /// for LPCM in a WAV or an AIFF, so those two rows carry the audio-only
513	    /// name `audio_m4a` carries: it is the closest true statement
514	    /// available — "an audio-only file AVFoundation writes" — and a null
515	    /// there would hand a WAV to `ImageSequenceWriter`, which would refuse
516	    /// it as an unknown image container and report a format this table
517	    /// advertises as unsupported. A name also means "the composition is
518	    /// read back through AVFoundation" (spec §11 CX-15), which is all it says
519	    /// on `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, whose files the core writes.
520	    pub(crate) avf_preset: Option<&'static str>,
521	    /// The bundled encoder that writes the row's video, or `None` for
522	    /// AVFoundation's own encoders (ImageIO where `avf_preset` is null).
523	    /// A row with a writer takes `encoder_speed` when its encoder has
524	    /// speeds (`Writer::takes_speed`).
525	    pub(crate) writer: Option<Writer>,
526	}

528	/// A rate as the two-element `[num, den]` array the spec spells every rate
529	/// with, or null for "the project's own". One function so the preset row
530	/// and the resolved settings cannot disagree about the shape.
531	pub(crate) fn fps_json(fps: Option<Fps>) -> Value {
532	    match fps {
533	        Some(fps) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(fps.num), Value::from(fps.den)]),
534	        None => Value::Null,
535	    }
536	}

538	impl Preset {
539	    /// True for the rows written frame by frame through ImageIO — the ones
540	    /// with no session preset — whose picture is FITTED inside the size
541	    /// rather than letterboxed to it, so a size on them is a box and the
542	    /// resolved numbers are the fit (`export_size::fit_within`).
543	    pub(crate) fn fits_inside_size(&self) -> bool {
544	        self.video && self.avf_preset.is_none()
545	    }
546	
547	    /// True for the rows whose frame has to have EVEN pixel dimensions:
548	    /// every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444 (spec §11 G-33). On
549	    /// these an odd edge is resolved one pixel smaller, in the size list's
550	    /// Document row and in the resolved settings alike
551	    /// (`export_size::even_size`), so the size reported is the size the
552	    /// writer writes.
553	    ///
554	    /// It is asked of `avf_preset` and the codec rather than listed row by
555	    /// row, so a new AVFoundation row is even-sized until someone exempts
556	    /// it — the safe side, since 4:2:0 chroma needs it and a row that can
557	    /// keep an odd edge has to be measured doing so, as ProRes 4444 was
558	    /// (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`'s `encodedSize`). The audio-only
559	    /// rows answer true: they have no picture and go on reporting what
560	    /// `h264` reports. The two image rows answer false; their numbers are
561	    /// the fit (`fits_inside_size`), odd or not.
562	    pub(crate) fn even_sized(&self) -> bool {
563	        self.avf_preset.is_some() && self.codec != "prores4444"
564	    }

566	    /// True for a row whose bundled encoder has speeds, the rows
567	    /// `encoder_speed` applies to (spec §11 CX-12 (2), CX-16 (2)).
568	    pub(crate) fn takes_encoder_speed(&self) -> bool {
569	        self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)
570	    }
571	
572	    /// True for the uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`,
573	    /// the rows `audio_bits` applies to (spec §11 AU-29). ProRes's LPCM
574	    /// track keeps 16 bits; it is not an `lpcm` row.
575	    pub(crate) fn takes_audio_bits(&self) -> bool {
576	        self.codec == "lpcm"
577	    }
578	
579	    /// True for the three audio-only rows, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and
580	    /// `audio_aiff`, the rows `stems` applies to (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
581	    pub(crate) fn takes_stems(&self) -> bool {
582	        !self.video
583	    }

585	    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
586	        let mut out = Map::new();
587	        out.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(self.id));
588	        out.insert("name".to_string(), Value::from(self.name));
589	        out.insert(
590	            "container".to_string(),
591	            Value::from(self.container.as_str()),
592	        );
593	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(self.codec));
594	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(self.video));
595	        out.insert(
596	            "size".to_string(),
597	            match self.size {
598	                Some((w, h)) => Value::Array(vec![Value::from(w), Value::from(h)]),
599	                None => Value::Null,
600	            },
601	        );
602	        // `size` and `fps` are spelled the same way for the same reason:
603	        // null is "whatever the project is" — the document size, the
604	        // document rate — which the resolver fills in from the canvas.
605	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(self.fps));
606	        out.insert(
607	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
608	            match self.avf_preset {
609	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
610	                None => Value::Null,
611	            },
612	        );
613	        if crate::dynamic_range::HDR_ROWS.contains(&self.id) {
614	            out.insert("hdr".to_string(), Value::from(true));
615	        }
616	        if let Some(writer) = self.writer {
617	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
618	            if writer.takes_speed() {
619	                let speeds = EncoderSpeed::ALL.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str()));
620	                out.insert("encoder_speeds".to_string(), speeds.collect());
621	            }
622	        }
623	        if self.takes_audio_bits() {
624	            let bits = [16, 24].iter().map(|b| Value::from(*b));
625	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), bits.collect());
626	        }
627	        if self.takes_stems() {
628	            let modes = ["tracks", "names"].iter().map(|m| Value::from(*m));
629	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), modes.collect());
630	        }
631	        Value::Object(out)
632	    }

634	//! The output sizes the export sheet offers for one document and one
635	//! format — `rc_export_sizes` (spec §7.8) — and the one rule for what a
636	//! size MEANS on an image format, which `export_settings` applies too.
637	//!
638	//! A preset is an encoding and carries no size (`export.rs`), so the size
639	//! is a second choice, and this module is the list that choice is made
640	//! from: the format's cap if it has one, the document's own size, and the
641	//! standard sizes fitted to the document's aspect. The FIRST row is the
642	//! default — the rule every list the export sheet is built from follows —
643	//! which is the document's size for a movie format and the cap for an
644	//! image format, because an image format's cap is the point of the row
645	//! and not a ceiling that only applies from above.
646	//!
647	//! **The number is the short edge.** A standard size is named by one
648	//! number, and the number people use is the short one: "1080p ultrawide"
649	//! is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920, and both are 1080p
650	//! to everyone who says it. Naming by the long edge would call the
651	//! ultrawide 2560p and the vertical 1920p, which nobody does. So a row
652	//! keeps its short edge exactly and the long edge follows the document:
653	//! L = S × long / short of the document, on whichever axis the document is
654	//! longer along, and S × S for a square.
655	//!
656	//! **The long edge is rounded to even.** 4:2:0 chroma puts one colour
657	//! sample under each 2 × 2 block of luma, so H.264 and HEVC want even
658	//! dimensions, and `ExporterWriter.evenDimension` rounds an odd one down
659	//! before writing. Rounding here — to the nearest even integer, a tie
660	//! going up — means the size the popup shows is the size the file has;
661	//! leaving it to the writer would change the size behind the sheet's
662	//! back.
663	//!
664	//! **The even rule (spec §11 G-33).** The same is true of the document row
665	//! and of any size asked for, so on every row that needs even dimensions
666	//! (`Preset::even_sized`: every row AVFoundation writes but ProRes 4444)
667	//! the size is resolved HERE, by [`even_size`]: the document row's numbers
668	//! in this list, and in `export_settings` whatever was asked. An odd edge
669	//! is one pixel SMALLER. Down, because that is the size the writer already
670	//! wrote, so the report moves to the file and no file changes size;
671	//! because rounding up would hand the encoder a frame larger than the
672	//! picture on that axis; and because every listed row is then its own
673	//! fixed point, as an image format's is. The row is named "Document
674	//! (even)" when its numbers are not the canvas's, which is the whole of
675	//! how the popup says why. The argument this replaces was that a "Document
676	//! size" that was not the document's size would be a lie; the lie was the
677	//! row that said 321 × 181 over a file of 320 × 180. ProRes 4444 and the
678	//! two image formats keep an odd edge, and their row is "Document size",
679	//! the canvas as it is.
680	//!
681	//! **An image format's numbers are the file's.** A GIF or an APNG is
682	//! written frame by frame with the picture FITTED inside the size — aspect
683	//! kept, never upscaled — where a movie is letterboxed to exactly the frame
684	//! asked for (`ExporterImageSequence`, spec §7.8): padding costs bytes in
685	//! every frame for pixels that carry nothing, and a bigger frame carries no
686	//! more detail. So on those two formats every row here, and every size
687	//! `export_settings` resolves — the cap, a standard row, a custom size — is
688	//! the canvas fitted inside that box ([`fit_within`]), so that the popup,
689	//! the sheet's readout and the `export` tool all report the numbers the
690	//! file will have: a vertical 1080 × 1920 timeline's "GIF default" is
691	//! 152 × 270, not 480 × 270. The fit is decided here, once; the writer
692	//! draws each frame at exactly this size and does not fit a second time.
693	//! It is also its own fixed point — a fitted size fed back as the box
694	//! fits to itself — because that is exactly what happens: the sheet and
695	//! the tool send a listed row's numbers back through `export_settings` as
696	//! `width` and `height`, and a fit that could move a derived edge by a
697	//! pixel on the second pass would show one size and write another.
698	//!
699	//! **Rows may repeat.** A 1920 × 1080 document's 1080p row IS the document
700	//! row, and on a 1080 × 1920 document every image-format row from 1080p up
701	//! is the document again. They are listed anyway, because an id is the
702	//! `export` tool's vocabulary and a request for `1080p` has to mean the
703	//! same thing on every document — refusing it exactly where it is a no-op
704	//! would be the popup's tidiness leaking into an API. The sheet hides a
705	//! row whose numbers an earlier row already has, so a person never sees one
706	//! size under two names, and the row that shows is the one whose name says
707	//! more ("Document size" over "1080p"). Rows larger than the document are
708	//! offered for a movie — they were before, as the 4K preset — because a
709	//! 720p screen recording exported at 4K for a platform that picks its
710	//! bitrate by resolution is a real request.
711

719	/// only for 4K, which nobody calls 2160p out loud but which needs a
720	/// short-edge id to sit in the same vocabulary as the other three.
721	const STANDARD: [(&str, &str, u32); 4] = [
722	    ("2160p", "4K", 2160),
723	    ("1440p", "1440p", 1440),
724	    ("1080p", "1080p", 1080),
725	    ("720p", "720p", 720),

748	    /// The sizes the export sheet offers for `preset_id` against this
749	    /// document, as the JSON array of `{id, name, width, height}` rows
750	    /// `rc_export_sizes` returns, in menu order — the first is the default.
751	    ///
752	    /// The rows:
753	    ///
754	    /// 1. `preset` — the format's cap, "GIF default" / "APNG default", for
755	    ///    the two rows of the table that carry one; nothing for the rest.
756	    /// 2. `document` — "Document size", the canvas as it is; on a row that
757	    ///    needs even dimensions the canvas evened ([`even_size`]), named
758	    ///    "Document (even)" when that is not the canvas's own size.
759	    /// 3. `2160p` ("4K"), `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — the short edge named,
760	    ///    the long edge fitted to the canvas and rounded to even.
761	    ///
762	    /// On an image format every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside
763	    /// that row's box, never upscaled — the size the file will have. Rows
764	    /// may repeat an earlier row's numbers and are listed anyway (the
765	    /// module doc says why); the sheet hides the repeats.
766	    ///
767	    /// One list for every movie format, the audio-only row included: a
768	    /// width is reported for it the way `export_settings` reports one, and
769	    /// the sheet disables the control rather than this module keeping a
770	    /// second rule for one row. `Err` for an unknown preset, naming it —
771	    /// the same lookup and the same words as `export_settings`.
772	    pub fn export_sizes(&self, preset_id: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
773	        let preset = export::preset(preset_id)?;
774	        let document = (self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height);
775	        let fits = preset.fits_inside_size();
776	        let sized = |(width, height): (u32, u32)| {
777	            if fits {
778	                fit_within(document, (width, height))
779	            } else {
780	                (width, height)
781	            }
782	        };
783	
784	        let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
785	        if let Some(cap) = preset.size {
786	            // The codec in capitals is the format's name as people write
787	            // it — GIF, APNG — for the two rows that carry a cap.
788	            let (width, height) = sized(cap);
789	            rows.push(Row {
790	                id: "preset",
791	                name: format!("{} default", preset.codec.to_uppercase()),
792	                width,
793	                height,
794	            });
795	        }
796	        // The id is `document` either way: the name is the popup's, and it
797	        // changes only when the numbers are not the canvas's.
798	        let listed = if preset.even_sized() {
799	            even_size(document)
800	        } else {
801	            document
802	        };
803	        let name = if listed == document {
804	            "Document size"
805	        } else {
806	            "Document (even)"
807	        };
808	        rows.push(Row {
809	            id: "document",
810	            name: name.to_string(),
811	            width: listed.0,
812	            height: listed.1,
813	        });
814	        for (id, name, short) in STANDARD {
815	            let (width, height) = sized(fitted(document, short));
816	            rows.push(Row {
817	                id,
818	                name: name.to_string(),
819	                width,
820	                height,
821	            });
822	        }
823

828	/// The size whose short edge is `short`, in the aspect of a `width` ×
829	/// `height` document: the long edge is `short` × the document's long edge
830	/// over its short one, rounded to the nearest even integer with a tie
831	/// going up, on the axis the document is longer along. A square document
832	/// gives `short` × `short`.
833	fn fitted((width, height): (u32, u32), short: u32) -> (u32, u32) {
834	    let doc_long = u64::from(width.max(height));
835	    // `validate` refuses a zero edge; the `max` keeps the division total
836	    // regardless, since no input may panic.
837	    let doc_short = u64::from(width.min(height)).max(1);
838	
839	    // The nearest even integer to short × doc_long / doc_short is twice
840	    // the nearest integer to half of it, and round(a / b) with a tie going
841	    // up is (2a + b) / 2b in integer division — here a = short × doc_long
842	    // and b = 2 × doc_short, so the whole thing is one division. u64
843	    // because a canvas need only be non-zero (`validate`), not inside
844	    // `set_canvas`'s 16..16384, so the product is not bounded by u32.
845	    let half = (u64::from(short) * doc_long + doc_short) / (2 * doc_short);
846	    // A canvas far outside those bounds can carry a ratio no u32 holds;
847	    // the row is then unusable, but a query must answer, and evenly.
848	    let long = u32::try_from(half * 2).unwrap_or(u32::MAX - 1);
849	
850	    if width >= height {
851	        (long, short)
852	    } else {
853	        (short, long)
854	    }
855	}

857	/// A size as a row that needs even dimensions writes it (spec §11 G-33),
858	/// each edge on its own: below 2 it is 2, an odd edge is one SMALLER, and an
859	/// even edge is itself. The rule `export_settings` and
860	/// [`Project::export_sizes`] share, so the list and the resolver cannot
861	/// disagree about what an H.264 will measure; the module doc says why down.
862	/// It is `ExporterWriter.evenDimension`'s arithmetic, which stays as the
863	/// floor under any caller that did not come through here.
864	pub(crate) fn even_size((width, height): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
865	    let even = |edge: u32| if edge < 2 { 2 } else { edge - edge % 2 };
866	    (even(width), even(height))
867	}
868	
869	/// A `width` × `height` canvas fitted inside a box: the canvas itself when
870	/// it already fits — never upscaled — and otherwise scaled down, aspect
871	/// kept, so that the edge which meets the box first takes the box's value
872	/// exactly and the other is the scaled value rounded UP to a whole pixel.
873	/// The rule an image format's size means (module doc), shared by
874	/// `export_settings` and [`Project::export_sizes`] so the two cannot
875	/// disagree about what a GIF will measure.
876	///
877	/// Up rather than to the nearest, so that the fit is its own fixed point.
878	/// Fitting the result again compares box × canvas products on the two
879	/// axes, and the derived edge — never below its exact value — keeps the
880	/// same axis limiting, whose derived edge is the same ceiling; rounded to
881	/// the nearest it can fall below the exact value, flip the limiting axis
882	/// on the second pass, and take a pixel off the other edge (a 3024 × 1964
883	/// recording's 1080p box, 1662 × 1080, came back 1662 × 1079 and then
884	/// 1661 × 1079). The ceiling never leaves the box: the limiting axis is
885	/// the one whose exact scaled value fits, and a whole number no smaller
886	/// than a value that fits inside a whole box edge fits too.
887	pub(crate) fn fit_within((width, height): (u32, u32), (box_w, box_h): (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
888	    if width <= box_w && height <= box_h {
889	        return (width, height);
890	    }
891	    let (w, h) = (u64::from(width).max(1), u64::from(height).max(1));
892	    let (bw, bh) = (u64::from(box_w).max(1), u64::from(box_h).max(1));
893	    // The width meets the box first when box_w / w ≤ box_h / h, which is
894	    // box_w × h ≤ box_h × w with no division to round.
895	    let (fw, fh) = if bw * h <= bh * w {
896	        (bw, ceil_div(h * bw, w))
897	    } else {
898	        (ceil_div(w * bh, h), bh)
899	    };
900	    let edge = |value: u64| u32::try_from(value).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).max(1);
901	    (edge(fw), edge(fh))
902	}
903	
904	/// `a / b` rounded up to a whole number; `b ≥ 1`.
905	fn ceil_div(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
906	    a.div_ceil(b)
907	}

1	//! Export presets and the resolution of one into concrete settings
2	//! (spec §7.8).
3	//!
4	//! Rust decides, AVFoundation does: nothing here encodes anything. The job
5	//! is to turn "H.264, 1920 × 1080, the in/out range, 30 fps" into the exact
6	//! set of values Swift hands to the writer — the preset name, the output
7	//! file type, the time range, the frame size — so that the choice of format
8	//! is testable without a GPU and the MCP agent's `export` tool takes the
9	//! same vocabulary the UI does.
10	//!
11	//! A preset is an ENCODING — a container and a codec — and carries no size:
12	//! an export is at the document's own size unless one is asked for, and
13	//! the sizes on offer for a document and a format are a separate list,
14	//! [`Project::export_sizes`] in `export_size.rs`, whose rows reach the
15	//! resolver here as the same `width`/`height` overrides a script sends.
16	//!
17	//! Two of the presets name a format AVFoundation cannot write at all: an
18	//! animated GIF and an animated PNG are assembled frame by frame through
19	//! ImageIO. That changes nothing here except one field — those rows carry
20	//! no `avf_preset`, and a null `avf_preset` is Swift's signal to take the
21	//! image-sequence path instead of building a session. Everything else
22	//! (the size, the rate, the range, the file's UTI) is resolved identically,
23	//! because it means the same thing on either path.
24	//!
25	//! Four rows, `av1` (spec §11 CX-12), `av1_webm` (CX-15), `vp9_webm`
26	//! (CX-16) and `vp9_alpha_webm` (CX-17), are encoded by a bundled library
27	//! and not by AVFoundation, which still writes `av1`'s container (the core
28	//! writes the three WebMs): their `writer` names the route, and on the two
29	//! AV1 rows `encoder_speed` names SVT-AV1's speed; no other row's settings
30	//! carry either key, and the two VP9 rows' carry no speed, libvpx having one
31	//! (CX-3).
32	//!
33	//! The two uncompressed audio rows, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, carry
34	//! `audio_bits`, 16 or 24 (spec §11 AU-29): 16 when not asked, and refused
35	//! by name on every other row.
36	//!
37	//! The three audio rows take `stems`, `tracks` or `names` (spec §11
38	//! AU-108): asked, the settings end with `stems`, the files beside the mix
39	//! resolved to `[{name, tracks}]` by `export_stems.rs`; a movie row refuses.
40	//!
41	//! The preset table is the single source of truth: [`presets`] serializes
42	//! it for the picker and [`Project::export_settings`] resolves against the
43	//! same rows, so a preset cannot exist in the menu and not in the resolver.
44	//!
45	//! How an override value is READ and REFUSED is `export_overrides.rs`,
46	//! and the rows themselves — the containers, and the presets written into
47	//! them — are `export_table.rs`. The vocabulary and the table: this file
48	//! is the design they serve and the resolution that brings the two of
49	//! them together against one project.
50

52	
53	use crate::export_overrides::{
54	    audio_bits as audio_bits_override, boolean, dynamic_range, encoder_speed, fps as fps_override,
55	    loudness, object, positive_u32, range as range_override, stems as stems_override,
56	};

58	use crate::model::Project;
59	use crate::time;

66	pub(crate) use crate::export_overrides::describe;
67	
68	/// Re-exported at their old paths too, on the same terms and for the same
69	/// reason: the rows went out to `export_table.rs` under the size rule, and

72	/// `rc_export_presets` with `export::presets()`, and `export_size.rs`
