78	// ---- resolution ----------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	impl Project {
81	    /// Resolves `preset_id` plus optional `overrides` against this project
82	    /// into the concrete settings Swift configures the export session with
83	    /// (`rc_export_settings`).
84	    ///
85	    /// Overrides may set `width`, `height`, `fps` (`[num, den]`), `range`
86	    /// (`{"start", "duration"}` in ticks), `optimize_for_network`, the two
87	    /// bitrates `video_bitrate` / `audio_bitrate` (bits per second,
88	    /// strictly positive), the two loudness figures `loudness_lufs` /
89	    /// `peak_dbtp`, `dynamic_range` (`hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, spec §11
90	    /// HD-14), `encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, on a
91	    /// row whose bundled encoder has speeds, CX-12, CX-16) and `audio_bits`
92	    /// (16 or 24, on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`, AU-29) and `stems`
93	    /// (`tracks` or `names`, on the three audio rows, resolved to
94	    /// `[{name, tracks}]` last in the settings, AU-108); anything else in the object is ignored, so a newer UI
95	    /// can send fields this build does not know. Each is read and refused
96	    /// by `export_overrides.rs`, which is where the spelling of every one
97	    /// of them lives.
98	    ///
99	    /// A bitrate is emitted only when it was asked for. There is no default
100	    /// to fall back on (see `export_table::PRESETS`), and an absent key says
101	    /// exactly that — "let the encoder pick" — where a zero or a null would
102	    /// have to be re-interpreted as the same thing on the Swift side. The two
103	    /// are accepted for every preset, including the ones that cannot use them,
104	    /// on the same principle that reports a width for the audio-only row:
105	    /// one rule for reading overrides, and the format flags say what the
106	    /// output can actually carry.
107	    ///
108	    /// The two loudness figures follow the bitrates exactly — emitted only
109	    /// when asked for, accepted by every preset, either one alone: the
110	    /// ceiling is the export's master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which runs
111	    /// with or without a target.
112	    ///
113	    /// The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and clamped to the
114	    /// project, because an `AVAssetExportSession` `timeRange` that begins
115	    /// between two frames starts the export on a frame the user did not
116	    /// choose. A range that resolves to zero length is refused: an empty
117	    /// export is always a mistake, and AVFoundation reports it far later
118	    /// and far less clearly.
119	    ///
120	    /// `Err` for an unknown preset or a malformed override. This is a QUERY
121	    /// and not an edit: there is no "changes nothing" case, so it has no
122	    /// identity arm and no refusal arm (spec §5.5).
123	    pub fn export_settings(
124	        &self,
125	        preset_id: &str,
126	        overrides: Option<&Value>,
127	    ) -> Result<Value, String> {
128	        let preset = preset(preset_id)?;
129	        let overrides = object(overrides)?;
130	        // The picture the row writes (spec §11 HD-14 (c), `dynamic_range.rs`):
131	        // read before anything else, so a mistyped value is refused by name
132	        // whatever the row, and resolved against the canvas and the row.
133	        let picture = self.deliverable(preset, dynamic_range(overrides)?)?;
134	        // The bundled encoder's speed (spec §11 CX-12 (2)): read on any row
135	        // so a misspelling is named, then refused on a row it cannot apply
136	        // to, and Balanced when a writer row was not asked.
137	        let speed = match (encoder_speed(overrides)?, preset.takes_encoder_speed()) {
138	            (Some(_), false) => {
139	                return Err(format!(
140	                    "{} has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm",
141	                    preset.id
142	                ))
143	            }
144	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(EncoderSpeed::Balanced)),
145	            (None, false) => None,
146	        };
147	        // The uncompressed rows' bit depth (spec §11 AU-29), on the speed's
148	        // terms: read on any row so a 20 is named, refused on a row that
149	        // has no depth to choose, and 16 on those rows when not asked.
150	        let bits = match (audio_bits_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_audio_bits()) {
151	            (Some(_), false) => {
152	                return Err(format!(
153	                    "{} has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff",
154	                    preset.id
155	                ))
156	            }
157	            (asked, true) => Some(asked.unwrap_or(16)),
158	            (None, false) => None,
159	        };
160	        // The stems (spec §11 AU-108 (a)), on the depth's terms: read on any
161	        // row so a misspelling is named, refused on a movie row, and
162	        // resolved to the files they are only when asked.
163	        let stems = match (stems_override(overrides)?, preset.takes_stems()) {
164	            (Some(_), false) => {
165	                return Err(format!(
166	                    "{} has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff",
167	                    preset.id
168	                ))
169	            }
170	            (Some(mode), true) => Some(self.export_stems(mode)?),
171	            (None, _) => None,
172	        };
173	
174	        // Size: the preset's cap if it has one, else the canvas — a movie
175	        // preset renders at whatever the project composites at, and a size
176	        // the sheet's popup or a script chose arrives as the override.
177	        let (preset_width, preset_height) = preset
178	            .size
179	            .unwrap_or((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height));
180	        let width = positive_u32(overrides, "width")?.unwrap_or(preset_width);
181	        let height = positive_u32(overrides, "height")?.unwrap_or(preset_height);
182	        // What is reported is the size the FILE will have, so that the
183	        // sheet's readout, its Size popup and the `export` tool's result
184	        // all say the numbers the writer draws (`export_size.rs` has both
185	        // rules and their reasons). An image format is written with the
186	        // picture FITTED inside the size, never letterboxed and never
187	        // upscaled, so its numbers are the fit and not the box. A row that
188	        // needs even dimensions writes an odd edge one pixel smaller
189	        // (spec §11 G-33), whether the edge came from the canvas or was
190	        // asked for. Every other row writes the pair as it stands.
191	        let (width, height) = if preset.fits_inside_size() {
192	            crate::export_size::fit_within((self.canvas.width, self.canvas.height), (width, height))
193	        } else if preset.even_sized() {
194	            crate::export_size::even_size((width, height))
195	        } else {
196	            (width, height)
197	        };
198	
199	        // The preset's rate, else the canvas — the image-sequence presets
200	        // cap the rate for the same reason they cap the size, and every
201	        // movie preset exports at the rate the project was cut at.
202	        let fps = fps_override(overrides, preset.fps.unwrap_or(self.canvas.fps))?;
203	
204	        let project_duration = self.duration();
205	        let (mut start, mut duration) = range_override(overrides, (0, project_duration))?;
206	        // Snap first, then clamp: snapping can only move a bound by less
207	        // than a frame, so clamping afterwards cannot be undone by it.
208	        start = time::snap_to_frame(start, fps).clamp(0, project_duration);
209	        duration =
210	            time::snap_to_frame(duration, fps).clamp(0, project_duration.saturating_sub(start));
211	        if duration <= 0 {
212	            return Err(format!(
213	                "export range is empty: {duration} ticks at {start} in a project {project_duration} ticks long"
214	            ));
215	        }
216	
217	        // Bits per second, or nothing at all. No preset supplies one, so an
218	        // absent key here reaches Swift as an absent key there and means
219	        // "the encoder's own ladder".
220	        let video_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "video_bitrate")?;
221	        let audio_bitrate = positive_u32(overrides, "audio_bitrate")?;
222	
223	        // The integrated loudness target and the master limiter's true-peak
224	        // ceiling, on the bitrates' terms: emitted only when asked for, so
225	        // an absent `loudness_lufs` reaches Swift as an absent key and means
226	        // "do not normalise", and an absent `peak_dbtp` the master's default
227	        // (spec §11 AU-27). The reader is the one place their bounds live.
228	        let (loudness_lufs, peak_dbtp) = loudness(overrides)?;
229	
230	        let optimize = boolean(
231	            overrides,
232	            "optimize_for_network",
233	            preset.container.optimizes_for_network(),
234	        )?;
235	
236	        let mut range = Map::new();
237	        range.insert("start".to_string(), Value::from(start));
238	        range.insert("duration".to_string(), Value::from(duration));
239	
240	        let mut out = Map::new();
241	        out.insert("preset".to_string(), Value::from(preset.id));
242	        // Null here means "AVFoundation cannot write this" — the GIF and
243	        // APNG rows — and is Swift's cue to take the ImageIO path. It is
244	        // NOT "pick a session preset yourself".
245	        out.insert(
246	            "avf_preset".to_string(),
247	            match preset.avf_preset {
248	                Some(name) => Value::from(name),
249	                None => Value::Null,
250	            },
251	        );
252	        out.insert(
253	            "container".to_string(),
254	            Value::from(preset.container.as_str()),
255	        );
256	        out.insert(
257	            "file_type".to_string(),
258	            Value::from(preset.container.file_type()),
259	        );
260	        out.insert("codec".to_string(), Value::from(preset.codec));
261	        // Width and height are reported even for the audio-only preset —
262	        // they cost nothing and let the sheet show one summary line for
263	        // every preset — but `video: false` is what Swift keys off.
264	        out.insert("width".to_string(), Value::from(width));
265	        out.insert("height".to_string(), Value::from(height));
266	        out.insert("fps".to_string(), fps_json(Some(fps)));
267	        if let Some(bps) = video_bitrate {
268	            out.insert("video_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
269	        }
270	        if let Some(bps) = audio_bitrate {
271	            out.insert("audio_bitrate".to_string(), Value::from(bps));
272	        }
273	        if let Some(lufs) = loudness_lufs {
274	            out.insert("loudness_lufs".to_string(), Value::from(lufs));
275	        }
276	        if let Some(dbtp) = peak_dbtp {
277	            out.insert("peak_dbtp".to_string(), Value::from(dbtp));
278	        }
279	        out.insert("range".to_string(), Value::Object(range));
280	        // Audio is offered whenever the container can hold it: a project
281	        // with no sound simply produces no audio track, which is cheaper
282	        // than deciding here. A GIF or an APNG holds none at all.
283	        out.insert(
284	            "audio".to_string(),
285	            Value::from(preset.container.carries_audio()),
286	        );
287	        out.insert("video".to_string(), Value::from(preset.video));
288	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — true for
289	        // `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng`, and for nothing else the
290	        // table offers. `export_table.rs`'s `alpha` field doc is where
291	        // `apng` against `gif` is argued — a GIF shows a transparent pixel
292	        // and still answers false, because it has one palette index and no
293	        // fourth channel — and `core/tests/export.rs` pins the three rows
294	        // by name.
295	        //
296	        // It reads `preset.alpha` and not `self.canvas.background`, which
297	        // is the whole decision and is worth one sentence here as well as
298	        // in the field doc: this object is flat and one shape for every
299	        // row, so a flag that answered "the canvas is translucent" would
300	        // say `alpha: true` on an H.264, a GIF and a WAV — three files with
301	        // nowhere to put it. It is `audio`'s kind of fact, one line up, and
302	        // told the same way: what the file can HOLD, never what this
303	        // document happens to be. A transparent canvas written through a
304	        // row that answers FALSE composites onto black, and this is the key
305	        // that lets the sheet and the `export` tool say so before the file
306	        // exists.
307	        out.insert("alpha".to_string(), Value::from(preset.alpha));
308	        out.insert("optimize_for_network".to_string(), Value::from(optimize));
309	        // An HLG project's video row names the picture it writes (spec §11
310	        // HD-14 (c)): `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`; only then, so every SDR project's
311	        // settings are the text they were and an audio row is unchanged.
312	        if let Some(picture) = picture {
313	            out.insert("color".to_string(), Value::from(picture.as_str()));
314	        }
315	        // The encoder route on a writer row, and its speed where the encoder
316	        // has speeds, so every other row's settings are the text they were
317	        // (spec §11 CX-12, CX-16 (1)).
318	        if let Some(writer) = preset.writer {
319	            out.insert("writer".to_string(), Value::from(writer.as_str()));
320	        }
321	        if let Some(speed) = speed {
322	            out.insert("encoder_speed".to_string(), Value::from(speed.as_str()));
323	        }
324	        // The depth on the two uncompressed rows only, so every other row's
325	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-29).
326	        if let Some(bits) = bits {
327	            out.insert("audio_bits".to_string(), Value::from(bits));
328	        }
329	        // The stems last, and only when asked, so every other export's
330	        // settings are the text they were (spec §11 AU-108).
331	        if let Some(stems) = stems {
332	            let stems = stems.iter().map(|stem| stem.to_json()).collect();
333	            out.insert("stems".to_string(), Value::Array(stems));
334	        }
335	        Ok(Value::Object(out))
336	    }
337	}
338	//! How an export override is READ and REFUSED — the vocabulary the export
339	//! settings resolve from, where `export_table.rs` is the table and
340	//! `export.rs` the resolution.
341	//!
342	//! Cut out of `export.rs` in road map 2's phase 5, and cut HERE for the
343	//! reason `props_check.rs` was cut out of `edit_props.rs`: a rule about
344	//! how a value is spelled and what makes it a refusal is a fact about the
345	//! VOCABULARY, not about the resolution. Nothing in this file knows which
346	//! preset asked, what the canvas is, or what the settings object ends up
347	//! looking like; everything in it answers one question — "is this JSON
348	//! value a legal `width` / `fps` / `range` / bitrate / decibel figure, and
349	//! if not, what do we tell the caller it was?".
350	//!
351	//! The cut also paid the size rule's toll. `export.rs` stood at 578 lines
352	//! against the ~600 soft cap and phase 5 added two containers, two preset
353	//! rows, a decibel validator, two override reads and two echo lines; a
354	//! file at the line gives something up before it takes anything on.
355	//!
356	//! Three rules hold for every reader here, and every new one must keep
357	//! them, because the sheet, the `export` tool and the test suite all lean
358	//! on them:
359	//!
360	//! 1. **Absent and explicit null are the same thing** — "use the preset".
361	//!    That is what lets the export sheet build one overrides object and
362	//!    null the fields whose control is greyed out.
363	//! 2. **An unknown key is ignored, silently.** A newer UI may send fields
364	//!    this build has never heard of and must still get an export.
365	//! 3. **A refusal names the offending value**, through [`describe`], and
366	//!    the message is lowercase and starts `export <key> must be …`. The
367	//!    key is in the message because a caller sending six overrides needs
368	//!    to know which one it was.
369	//!
370	//! [`describe`] itself is not about export at all any more: five modules
371	//! outside this one (`edit.rs`, `edit_props.rs`, `edit_action.rs`,
372	//! `edit_paste.rs`, `edit_track.rs`) name it `crate::export::describe` for
373	//! their own error messages, so `export.rs` re-exports it under that path
374	//! and the cut costs those files nothing. [`spelled`] sits beside it for
375	//! the same reason: a vocabulary value's own JSON spelling, for a sentence
376	//! (`lut.rs`, `media_color.rs`, `edit_relink.rs`).
377	
378	use serde_json::Value;
379	
380	use crate::dynamic_range::DynamicRange;
381	use crate::export_table::EncoderSpeed;
382	use crate::time::{Fps, Ticks};
383	
384	// ---- the shared front door -----------------------------------------------
385	
386	/// A JSON value as short text for an error message, truncated on a char
387	/// boundary so a pasted megabyte of JSON cannot become the error string.
388	pub(crate) fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {
389	    let text = value.to_string();
390	    if text.chars().count() <= 40 {
391	        text
392	    } else {
393	        format!("{} …", text.chars().take(40).collect::<String>())
394	    }
395	}
396	
397	/// A vocabulary value's JSON spelling (`warm`, `video`), serde's own, so a
398	/// sentence names it as the file and the schema do.
399	pub(crate) fn spelled<T: serde::Serialize>(value: T) -> String {
400	    serde_json::to_value(value)
401	        .ok()
402	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().map(str::to_string))
403	        .unwrap_or_default()
404	}
405	
406	/// The overrides object itself: `None` for absent, null or an empty
407	/// request, `Some` for an object, and an `Err` naming the value for
408	/// anything else. One place, so "overrides must be a json object" is the
409	/// same sentence however the caller got here.
410	pub(crate) fn object(overrides: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Option<&Value>, String> {
411	    match overrides {
412	        None => Ok(None),
413	        Some(Value::Null) => Ok(None),
414	        Some(value) if value.is_object() => Ok(Some(value)),
415	        Some(value) => Err(format!(
416	            "export overrides must be a json object, not {}",
417	            describe(value)
418	        )),
419	    }
420	}
421	
422	/// An override field, or `None` when absent or explicitly null (null means
423	/// "use the preset", so a caller can build one overrides object and leave
424	/// the fields it does not care about).
425	fn field<'a>(overrides: Option<&'a Value>, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
426	    overrides.and_then(|o| o.get(key)).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
427	}
428	
429	// ---- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------
430	
431	/// A strictly positive integer override — the pixel dimensions and the two
432	/// bitrates, which want the identical check. `u64::MAX` is not the ceiling
433	/// on purpose: a bitrate is bits per second, and `u32`'s 4.3 Gbit/s is an
434	/// order of magnitude past anything deliverable (ProRes 422 at 4K is about
435	/// 0.7), so the same bound that keeps a width sane keeps a bitrate honest.
436	/// Zero and negative both land in the error arm, which names the value.
437	pub(crate) fn positive_u32(overrides: Option<&Value>, key: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
438	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
439	        return Ok(None);
440	    };
441	    match value.as_u64() {
442	        Some(n) if n > 0 && n <= u64::from(u32::MAX) => Ok(Some(n as u32)),
443	        _ => Err(format!(
444	            "export {key} must be a positive integer, not {}",
445	            describe(value)
446	        )),
447	    }
448	}
449	
450	/// A decibel override: a finite number inside `[min, max]`. The f64 twin
451	/// of [`positive_u32`], and a separate function because the two loudness
452	/// figures are NEGATIVE FRACTIONS — −14.5 LUFS is a real request — so
453	/// every guard `positive_u32` applies is the wrong one here.
454	///
455	/// `as_f64` is the whole type check: `serde_json` answers `None` for a
456	/// bool, a string, an array and an object alike, so the error arm catches
457	/// them all and names what arrived. Non-finite is checked even though JSON
458	/// cannot spell a NaN or an infinity — the function takes a `Value` from
459	/// whoever has one, and a bound comparison against a NaN is silently false
460	/// rather than an error.
461	fn decibels(
462	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
463	    key: &str,
464	    min: f64,
465	    max: f64,
466	) -> Result<Option<f64>, String> {
467	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, key) else {
468	        return Ok(None);
469	    };
470	    match value.as_f64() {
471	        Some(db) if db.is_finite() && db >= min && db <= max => Ok(Some(db)),
472	        _ => Err(format!(
473	            "export {key} must be a number from {min} to {max}, not {}",
474	            describe(value)
475	        )),
476	    }
477	}
478	
479	/// The bottom of the loudness target's range. −70 LUFS is BS.1770-4's own
480	/// absolute gate: a programme quieter than that measures as nothing at
481	/// all, so a target at or below it is a request the measurement cannot
482	/// even express. The top is 0 LUFS — full scale, unwise but legal, and the
483	/// bound is where it is so the message is about the value.
484	const LOUDNESS_MIN: f64 = -70.0;
485	const LOUDNESS_MAX: f64 = 0.0;
486	
487	/// The true-peak ceiling's range. 0 dBTP is legal (and what a master with
488	/// no headroom asks for); −20 is far below anything a deliverable wants
489	/// and exists only so a mistyped LUFS figure lands in the error arm rather
490	/// than turning the programme down by 60 dB.
491	const PEAK_MIN: f64 = -20.0;
492	const PEAK_MAX: f64 = 0.0;

607	/// The `fps` override as `[num, den]`, or `default` when it is absent.
608	/// Both terms are read as `u64` and bounded by `u32::MAX` because that is
609	/// what [`Fps`] holds, and both must be non-zero: a zero numerator is a
610	/// frozen export and a zero denominator is a division by nothing, and
611	/// either would reach the frame-snapping arithmetic before anyone noticed.
612	pub(crate) fn fps(overrides: Option<&Value>, default: Fps) -> Result<Fps, String> {
613	    let Some(value) = field(overrides, "fps") else {
614	        return Ok(default);
615	    };
616	    let terms = value.as_array().and_then(|a| {
617	        match (
618	            a.first().and_then(Value::as_u64),
619	            a.get(1).and_then(Value::as_u64),
620	        ) {
621	            (Some(num), Some(den)) if a.len() == 2 => Some((num, den)),
622	            _ => None,
623	        }
624	    });
625	    match terms {
626	        Some((num, den))
627	            if num > 0 && den > 0 && num <= u64::from(u32::MAX) && den <= u64::from(u32::MAX) =>
628	        {
629	            Ok(Fps {
630	                num: num as u32,
631	                den: den as u32,
632	            })
633	        }
634	        _ => Err(format!(
635	            "export fps must be [num, den] with non-zero terms, not {}",
636	            describe(value)
637	        )),
638	    }
639	}

651	/// The `range` override as the raw `(start, duration)` pair it asked for,
652	/// each falling back to its half of `default` — which is `(0, the whole
653	/// project)`, so `{"start": …}` alone keeps the project's length and
654	/// `{"duration": …}` alone keeps its start.
655	///
656	/// RAW is the word: nothing here snaps or clamps. Both are decisions about
657	/// a project and an export rate, which this file knows nothing about, and
658	/// the ORDER of the two (snap first, then clamp) is load-bearing enough to
659	/// stay visible where the settings are resolved.
660	pub(crate) fn range(
661	    overrides: Option<&Value>,
662	    default: (Ticks, Ticks),
663	) -> Result<(Ticks, Ticks), String> {
664	    let Some(range) = field(overrides, "range") else {
665	        return Ok(default);
666	    };
667	    if !range.is_object() {
668	        return Err(format!(
669	            "export range must be a json object with start and duration, not {}",
670	            describe(range)
671	        ));
672	    }
673	    let (mut start, mut duration) = default;
674	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "start") {
675	        start = ticks(value, "range start")?;
676	    }
677	    if let Some(value) = field(Some(range), "duration") {
678	        duration = ticks(value, "range duration")?;
679	    }
680	    Ok((start, duration))
681	}

750	//! The containers Frame Job writes (spec §7.8), and the four questions
751	//! each one answers about ITSELF: its extension, its UTI, whether a
752	//! leading index is worth rewriting, whether it can hold sound at all.
753	//!
754	//! Moved whole out of `export_table.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md:
755	//! a module at ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on),
756	//! as codec-export C1's toll T1, a pure move. `export_table.rs` re-exports
757	//! [`Container`], so every `crate::export_table::Container` path holds.
758	
759	/// The containers Frame Job writes. Kept as an enum rather than a string so
760	/// the container, its UTI, its network-optimization default and whether it
761	/// can hold sound at all are decided in exactly one exhaustive place.
762	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
763	pub(crate) enum Container {
764	    Mov,
765	    Mp4,
766	    M4a,
767	    Wav,
768	    Aiff,
769	    Gif,
770	    Apng,
771	    /// WebM, written by the core's own writer (`webm_writer.rs`, spec §11
772	    /// CX-15), not by AVFoundation.
773	    Webm,
774	}
775	
776	impl Container {
777	    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
778	        match self {
779	            Container::Mov => "mov",
780	            Container::Mp4 => "mp4",
781	            Container::M4a => "m4a",
782	            Container::Wav => "wav",
783	            Container::Aiff => "aiff",
784	            Container::Gif => "gif",
785	            Container::Apng => "apng",
786	            Container::Webm => "webm",
787	        }
788	    }
789	
790	    /// The output file's UTI. On the AVFoundation path Swift passes this
791	    /// straight to `outputFileType`, whose raw values ARE UTIs; on the
792	    /// ImageIO path it is the destination type
793	    /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` takes. Either way it is what the
794	    /// save panel's content type and file extension are derived from, which
795	    /// is why the two image formats name a real UTI here rather than
796	    /// nothing — an export that could not tell the panel it writes a `.gif`
797	    /// would be worse off than one whose type string a session would
798	    /// reject, and a session is never built for them.
799	    ///
800	    /// An APNG is written to an ordinary PNG destination — the animation
801	    /// lives in `acTL`/`fcTL` chunks inside a file that is still a PNG — so
802	    /// its type identifier is PNG's, not one of its own.
803	    ///
804	    /// The two LPCM rows' identifiers are exactly `AVFileType.wav` and
805	    /// `AVFileType.aiff`'s raw values, which is what lets
806	    /// `Exporter.fileType(for:)` resolve them from this string alone
807	    /// rather than growing a container list of its own.
808	    pub(crate) fn file_type(self) -> &'static str {
809	        match self {
810	            Container::Mov => "com.apple.quicktime-movie",
811	            Container::Mp4 => "public.mpeg-4",
812	            Container::M4a => "com.apple.m4a-audio",
813	            Container::Wav => "com.microsoft.waveform-audio",
814	            Container::Aiff => "public.aiff-audio",
815	            Container::Gif => "com.compuserve.gif",
816	            Container::Apng => "public.png",
817	            Container::Webm => "org.webmproject.webm",
818	        }
819	    }
820	
821	    /// Whether `shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse` defaults on. MP4 and M4A are
822	    /// the delivery containers people upload, and a leading `moov` atom
823	    /// lets a player start before the file is fully fetched. A ProRes MOV
824	    /// is an editing master handed to another application, where the
825	    /// rewrite pass buys nothing. An HEVC-with-alpha MOV is a delivery file
826	    /// too, and its default stays off all the same: that was the owner's
827	    /// choice for the row (spec §11 G-33), and the override turns it on. GIF
828	    /// and APNG have no `moov` atom and nothing to move: a viewer already
829	    /// starts on the first frame, and
830	    /// neither do WAV and AIFF — a RIFF or an IFF file is a header
831	    /// followed by samples, with no index to relocate, so the flag would
832	    /// be a request the writer has nothing to do about. A WebM's index (its
833	    /// SeekHead) is already at the front, so the flag is off and inert there
834	    /// too (spec §11 CX-15 (1)).
835	    pub(crate) fn optimizes_for_network(self) -> bool {
836	        matches!(self, Container::Mp4 | Container::M4a)
837	    }
838	
839	    /// Whether the container can hold sound. Every movie container can,
840	    /// and M4A, WAV and AIFF are nothing else; GIF and APNG are picture
841	    /// formats with no audio track in the file format at all, so
842	    /// `audio: false` for those is a fact about the container rather than
843	    /// a decision about the project.
844	    pub(crate) fn carries_audio(self) -> bool {
845	        !matches!(self, Container::Gif | Container::Apng)
846	    }
847	}

3	/// What one bundled-encoder export costs (spec §11 CX-18): its resident peak, which the
4	/// Export Queue's limit books (`ExportEncoderLedger`), and its time, which the export
5	/// sheet's estimate reads. Two tables keyed alike, each figure carrying its source.
6	///
7	/// **Both are measured, never guessed, and both are a table edit to replace.** The figures
8	/// are `tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`'s, recorded in `archive/codec-export.md`'s
9	/// "## C6a" and "## C6b" (`vp9_alpha_webm`'s first in "## C5"'s fix pass): one fresh Release
10	/// instance per key and size, the resident peak above the instance's own after a warming
11	/// frame, and the export's wall time. The TIME figures are C6b's: on an idle machine, the
12	/// GH5 4K clip on a 25 fps canvas, the median of three runs per key and size over 250 and
13	/// 50 frames, which separate the fixed start from the per-frame time. A MEMORY figure is the
14	/// larger of C6a's (C5's) single run and C6b's peaks, its source naming the run that won.
15	///
16	/// A figure is given at 1920 × 1080 and 3840 × 2160 and read at an export's pixels:
17	/// proportionally below 1080p, linearly through both points above it, extrapolated past 4K.
18	
19	/// What a cost is keyed by: the row, the AV1 speed, and the bit depth the encoder runs at.
20	struct ExportEncoderKey: Hashable {
21	    /// `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm`.
22	    let preset: String
23	    /// The AV1 rows' speed (`settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced`); nil on every other row.
24	    let speed: EncoderSpeed?
25	    /// 10 on `svt_av1` (CX-14: always 10-bit); on `libvpx` 10 for `hlg`/`pq` (Profile 2,
26	    /// CX-16 (3)), else 8.
27	    let bits: Int
28	
29	    init(preset: String, speed: EncoderSpeed?, bits: Int) {
30	        self.preset = preset
31	        self.speed = speed
32	        self.bits = bits
33	    }
34	
35	    /// The key of an export's settings; nil for an AVFoundation row (no `writer`).
36	    init?(settings: ExportSettings) {
37	        guard let writer = settings.writer else { return nil }
38	        let av1 = writer == "svt_av1"
39	        let deep = settings.dynamicRange == .hlg || settings.dynamicRange == .pq
40	        self.init(
41	            preset: settings.preset, speed: av1 ? settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced : nil,
42	            bits: av1 || deep ? 10 : 8)
43	    }
44	}

46	/// One measured quantity at the two sizes, and where it came from.
47	struct ExportEncoderFigure {
48	    /// At 1920 × 1080.
49	    let at1080: Double
50	    /// At 3840 × 2160.
51	    let at2160: Double
52	    /// The run, its date, the machine and its load.
53	    let source: String
54	
55	    /// The figure at `pixels`: proportional below 1080p, linear through both points above.
56	    func value(pixels: Int) -> Double {
57	        let low = Double(ExportEncoderCosts.pixels1080)
58	        let high = Double(ExportEncoderCosts.pixels2160)
59	        let p = Double(max(0, pixels))
60	        if p <= low { return at1080 * p / low }
61	        return at1080 + (at2160 - at1080) * (p - low) / (high - low)
62	    }
63	}

217	/// The app-wide account of the bundled-encoder exports running now (spec §11 CX-18): the
218	/// Export Queue's job and every Export… progress sheet's, each booked from just before its
219	/// exporter starts to its finish, at the resident peak `ExportEncoderCosts.memory` measured
220	/// for its key and size.
221	///
222	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
223	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
224	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
225	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
226	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
227	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.
228	///
229	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
230	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when
231	/// nothing is booked — one export always runs, however large — or when the booked costs and
232	/// its own fit.
233	///
234	/// Main thread only, like the queue and the sheets that book into it, and AppKit-free so a
235	/// probe compiles it headless (`tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`).
236	final class ExportEncoderLedger {
237	    /// The app's one ledger. The queue observes it and the sheets book into it.
238	    static let shared = ExportEncoderLedger()
239	
240	    /// Posted after a booking is added or removed, with the ledger as the `object`. The
241	    /// queue re-runs `start()` on it, so a held job launches when a booking ends.
242	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
243	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportEncoderLedgerDidChange")
244	
245	    /// The Mac's memory the budget is a share of — `ProcessInfo`'s, which a probe sets to
246	    /// ask what a Mac of another size would admit.
247	    var physicalMemory: UInt64
248	
249	    private var entries: [(token: UInt64, cost: UInt64)] = []
250	    private var nextToken: UInt64 = 1
251	
252	    init(physicalMemory: UInt64 = ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory) {
253	        self.physicalMemory = physicalMemory
254	    }
255	
256	    /// What bundled-encoder exports may hold together, in bytes.
257	    var budget: UInt64 { Self.budget(physicalMemory: physicalMemory) }
258	
259	    /// Each running booking's cost, in booking order.
260	    var runningCosts: [UInt64] { entries.map(\.cost) }
261	
262	    // MARK: - The rule
263	
264	    /// A quarter of physical memory (CX-18 (3)).
265	    static func budget(physicalMemory: UInt64) -> UInt64 { physicalMemory / 4 }
266	
267	    /// Whether a job costing `cost` may start beside `running`: always when nothing runs,
268	    /// else when the sum fits `budget` (CX-18 (5)).
269	    static func admits(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> Bool {
270	        guard !running.isEmpty else { return true }
271	        let (inUse, over) = running.reduce((UInt64(0), false)) { sum, next in
272	            let added = sum.0.addingReportingOverflow(next)
273	            return (added.partialValue, sum.1 || added.overflow)
274	        }
275	        let total = inUse.addingReportingOverflow(cost)
276	        return !over && !total.overflow && total.partialValue <= budget
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The held job's sentence: what runs, what the Mac allows, what this one needs.
280	    static func waitingSentence(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> String {
281	        let inUse = running.reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 &+ $1 }
282	        return "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about "
283	            + "\(gigabytes(inUse)) of the \(gigabytes(budget)) this Mac allows them, and this "
284	            + "one needs about \(gigabytes(cost))."
285	    }
286	
287	    private static func gigabytes(_ bytes: UInt64) -> String {
288	        String(format: "%.1f GB", Double(bytes) / 1_073_741_824)
289	    }
290	
291	    // MARK: - Asking
292	
293	    /// Whether `settings` may start now, leaving out the booking `token` (the queue's own
294	    /// running job, which a waiting job is behind anyway). True for an AVFoundation row.
295	    func admits(_ settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> Bool {
296	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return true }
297	        return Self.admits(
298	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
299	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
300	    }
301	
302	    /// The held sentence for `settings`, or nil when it is admitted.
303	    func waitingSentence(for settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> String? {
304	        guard !admits(settings, ignoring: token) else { return nil }
305	        return Self.waitingSentence(
306	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
307	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
308	    }
309	
310	    private func costs(ignoring token: UInt64?) -> [UInt64] {
311	        entries.filter { $0.token != token }.map(\.cost)
312	    }
313	
314	    // MARK: - Booking
315	
316	    /// Books an export about to start and answers its token, or nil — booking nothing —
317	    /// for an AVFoundation row. Called BEFORE `Exporter.export`, whose early refusals finish
318	    /// synchronously inside it.
319	    func begin(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> UInt64? {
320	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return nil }
321	        let token = nextToken
322	        nextToken += 1
323	        entries.append(
324	            (token, ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget)))
325	        post()
326	        return token
327	    }
328	
329	    /// Ends a booking. A nil or unknown token is a no-op; a removal posts, and the queue's
330	    /// observer may launch its next job — and book it — inside this call, which is why a
331	    /// caller clears its own token BEFORE calling this.
332	    func end(_ token: UInt64?) {
333	        guard let token, let index = entries.firstIndex(where: { $0.token == token }) else {
334	            return
335	        }
336	        entries.remove(at: index)
337	        post()
338	    }
339	
340	    private func post() {
341	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
342	    }
343	}

346	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
347	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
348	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
349	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
350	/// take.
351	///
352	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
353	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
354	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
355	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
356	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
357	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
358	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
359	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
360	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
361	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
362	///
363	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
364	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
365	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
366	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
367	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
368	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
369	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
370	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
371	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
372	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
373	/// before it took the Preset row on.
374	extension ExportSheetController {
375	
376	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
377	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
378	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
379	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
380	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
381	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
382	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192
383	
384	    // MARK: - Loudness
385	
386	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
387	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
388	    ///
389	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
390	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
391	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
392	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
393	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
394	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
395	
396	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
397	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
398	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
399	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
400	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
401	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
402	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
403	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
404	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
405	
406	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
407	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
408	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
409	    ///
410	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
411	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
412	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
413	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
414	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
415	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
416	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
417	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")

419	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
420	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"

422	        }
423	    }

425	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
426	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
427	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message
428	    /// back.
429	    static let loudnessRange: ClosedRange<Double> = -70...0

431	    // MARK: - Quality
432	
433	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
434	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
435	    ///
436	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
437	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
438	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
439	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
440	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
441	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
442	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
443	    /// on both sides.
444	    ///
445	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
446	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
447	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
448	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
449	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
450	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
451	    struct QualityTier {
452	        let name: String
453	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
454	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
455	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
456	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
457	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
458	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
459	
460	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
461	        ///
462	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
463	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
464	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
465	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
466	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
467	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
468	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
469	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
470	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
471	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
472	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
473	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
474	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
475	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
476	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
477	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
478	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
479	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
480	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
481	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
482	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
483	        }

485	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
486	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
487	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
488	        }
489	    }

533	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
534	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
535	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
536	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }

476	    /// a master stays a master, and AAC everywhere else. `settings.audioBitrate`
477	    /// when the core resolved one, else 192 kbps — stereo AAC's

480	    /// **Two codecs mean LPCM (`ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`), and
481	    /// the CONTAINER decides the byte order.** ProRes has since M2 (§7.8
482	    /// pairs the profile with uncompressed sound), and phase 5's `audio_wav`
483	    /// / `audio_aiff` rows carry the codec `lpcm` outright. The dictionary handed to the encoder is then literally
484	    /// `decodedAudioSettings` — at 24 bits when `settings.audioBits` asks
485	    /// (spec §11 AU-29) — so nothing is converted on the way:
486	    /// `ExportAudioMaster` produces that shape from the float read. The exception is
487	    /// AIFF, which is big-endian by definition where WAV and QuickTime are
488	    /// little. Getting that flag wrong is not a subtle bug, and it was measured rather than
489	    /// reasoned about: on macOS 26.5.1 `AVAssetWriter.canAdd` answers FALSE
490	    /// for AAC settings into a `.wav` and FALSE for a little-endian LPCM
491	    /// dictionary into an `.aiff`, so either mistake reaches the user as
492	    /// `.presetUnavailable` for a format the table advertises. With the
493	    /// branch as written, one twenty-second tone came out of both rows the
494	    /// same size and decoded to identical PCM, sample for sample.
495	    ///
496	    /// A row whose codec is `lpcm` in a container this build has no rule for
497	    /// still gets little-endian LPCM rather than AAC, because AAC in an
498	    /// uncompressed container is the failure that reads as
499	    /// `.presetUnavailable` and sends the reader looking at the preset table.
500	    static func audioSettings(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> [String: Any] {
501	        guard ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: settings.codec) else {
502	            return [
503	                AVFormatIDKey: Int(kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC),
504	                AVSampleRateKey: 48000,
505	                AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 2,
506	                AVEncoderBitRateKey: settings.audioBitrate.map { max(1, $0) } ?? 192_000,
507	            ]
508	        }
509	        var lpcm = decodedAudioSettings
510	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { lpcm[AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey] = 24 }
511	        if settings.container.lowercased() == "aiff" { lpcm[AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey] = true }
512	        return lpcm
513	    }

93	            // bitrate refusals do; either may come alone, the ceiling being
94	            // the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27).
95	            // Restating a bound here would be a second spelling of it to
96	            // drift from the first.
97	            // The sheet sends both together and fixes the ceiling at
98	            // −1 dBTP; a caller that wants −0.3 or −2.0 says so here.
99	            if let target = try self.doubleArg(a, "loudness_lufs") {
100	                overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
101	            }
102	            if let ceiling = try self.doubleArg(a, "peak_dbtp") {
103	                overrides["peak_dbtp"] = ceiling
104	            }
105	            // The sheet's Size popup: a row id, or "Custom…" as an explicit
106	            // [width, height]. Absent is no override at all, so the tool's
107	            // default and the sheet's are one code path in the core — the
108	            // document's size, or an image format's cap.
109	            if let size = try self.exportSizeArg(a, document.project, preset: presetID) {
110	                overrides["width"] = size.width
111	                overrides["height"] = size.height
112	            }
113	            // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-14 (c)), forwarded
114	            // unread: the core's reader and resolver own its three words, its
115	            // per-row defaults and both refusals, each in its own sentence.
116	            if let range = a["dynamic_range"] {
117	                overrides["dynamic_range"] = range
118	            }
119	            // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-12 (2)), forwarded unread on the
120	            // same terms: the core reads the three words and refuses a row without one.
121	            if let speed = a["encoder_speed"] {
122	                overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed
123	            }
124	            // The sheet's Bit depth popup (spec §11 AU-29), forwarded unread on the
125	            // same terms: the core reads 16 or 24 and refuses a row without a depth.
126	            if let bits = a["audio_bits"] {
127	                overrides["audio_bits"] = bits
128	            }
129	            // The sheet's Stems popup (spec §11 AU-108), forwarded unread on the same
130	            // terms: the core reads "tracks" or "names", refuses a movie row, and refuses
131	            // a project with no track heard.
132	            if let stems = a["stems"] {
133	                overrides["stems"] = stems
134	            }
135	            let settings: ExportSettings
136	            do {
137	                settings = try ReelExport.settings(
138	                    document.project, preset: presetID, overrides: overrides)
139	            } catch {
140	                throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
141	            }
142	            return (
143	                document, document.project, document.mediaURLs(), settings,
144	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
145	            )
146	        }
147	        let (document, project, urls, settings, graphics) = prepared
148	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
149	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)))
150	
151	        // The graphics gate, here rather than only in the writer: a module
152	        // that does not compile refuses the CALL, so nothing is queued that
153	        // could only fail (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, the writer's own gate).
154	        if let refusal = Exporter.graphicsRefusal(
155	            project: project, settings: settings, graphics: graphics)
156	        {
157	            throw ToolError(message: refusal.localizedDescription)
158	        }
159	        let (id, status) = onMain { () -> (UInt64, String) in
160	            // The editor pauses before its own export so the player is not
161	            // decoding the same media; the agent's does the same.
162	            self.editor(document)?.playback.pause()
163	            let id = ExportQueueController.shared.enqueue(
164	                project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: url, options: options,
165	                graphics: graphics)
166	            AgentExports.shared.track(
167	                id, settings: settings, burnInTimecode: options.burnInTimecode, started: started)
168	            let word = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id).map {
169	                Self.exportStatusWord($0.state)
170	            }
171	            return (id, word ?? "queued")
172	        }
173	        return try jsonResult(["export_id": id, "path": url.path, "status": status])
174	    }

176	    /// The `size` argument of `export`, in the Size popup's vocabulary: a row
177	    /// id resolved through the same `rc_export_sizes` the popup is built from
178	    /// (`document`, `preset`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — `ExportSize`
179	    /// in `ReelCore.swift` says what each means, and `core/src/export_size.rs`
180	    /// why every document lists every row), or the popup's "Custom…" as an
181	    /// explicit `[width, height]`. nil when absent, which is no override: the
182	    /// core's default for the preset.
183	    ///
184	    /// A value that is neither is refused by NAME, never read as absent — the
185	    /// rule every reader in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` keeps, and the root
186	    /// `CLAUDE.md`'s: a value a handler cannot read is refused by name, never
187	    /// dropped. A `size` dropped in silence would export at the wrong size
188	    /// and report success. A custom
189	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
190	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
191	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
192	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
193	    private func exportSizeArg(
194	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
195	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
196	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
197	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
198	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
199	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
200	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
201	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
202	        let rows: [ExportSize]
203	        do {
204	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
205	        } catch {
206	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
207	        }
208	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
209	        if let id = raw as? String {
210	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
211	                throw ToolError(
212	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
213	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
214	            }
215	            return (row.width, row.height)
216	        }
217	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
218	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
219	            if edges.count == 2 {
220	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
221	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
222	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
223	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
224	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
225	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
226	                    throw ToolError(
227	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
228	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
229	                            + "row: \(ids).")
230	                }
231	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
232	            }
233	        }
234	        throw ToolError(
235	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
236	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
240	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
241	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
242	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
243	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
244	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
245	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
246	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
247	    /// `1`.
248	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
249	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
250	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
251	            let real = number.doubleValue
252	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
253	        }
254	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
255	    }
256	
257	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
258	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
259	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
260	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
261	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
262	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
263	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
264	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
265	    /// lead.
266	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
267	        let message = error.localizedDescription
268	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
269	            return ToolError(message: message)
270	        }
271	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
272	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
273	    }
274	
275	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
276	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
277	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
278	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
279	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
280	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
281	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
282	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
283	        return text
284	    }
285	}

290	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
291	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
292	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
293	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
294	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
295	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
296	///
297	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
298	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
299	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
300	///
301	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
302	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
303	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
304	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
305	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
306	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
307	extension AgentServer {
308	
309	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
310	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
311	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
312	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
313	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
314	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
315	        }
316	        return try jsonResult(status)
317	    }
318	
319	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
320	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
321	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
322	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
323	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
324	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
325	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
326	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
327	        }
328	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
329	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
330	        }
331	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
332	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
333	        }
334	        return try jsonResult(status)
335	    }
336	
337	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
338	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
339	        switch state {
340	        case .waiting: return "queued"
341	        case .running: return "running"
342	        case .completed: return "done"
343	        case .failed: return "failed"
344	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
345	        }
346	    }
347	
348	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
349	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
350	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
351	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
352	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
353	        }
354	        guard raw >= 1 else {
355	            throw ToolError(
356	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
357	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
358	        }
359	        return UInt64(raw)
360	    }
361	
362	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
363	        ToolError(
364	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "
365	                + "last until Frame Job quits.")
366	    }
367	}

369	/// What `AgentExports` keeps of one tracked job: the queue row's fields as
370	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
371	private struct AgentExportRecord {
372	    let settings: ExportSettings
373	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
374	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
375	    let started: TimeInterval
376	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
377	    var progress: Double
378	    var phase: String?
379	    var message: String?
380	    var destination: URL
381	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
382	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
383	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
384	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
385	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
386	    var finished: TimeInterval?
387	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
388	    var bytes: Int = 0
389	
390	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
391	        state = job.state
392	        progress = job.progress
393	        phase = job.phase
394	        message = job.message
395	        destination = job.destination
396	        loudness = job.loudness
397	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
398	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
399	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
400	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
401	        bytes =
402	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
403	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0
404	    }

407	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
408	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
409	final class AgentExports {
410	    static let shared = AgentExports()
411	
412	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
413	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
414	
415	    private init() {
416	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
417	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
418	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
419	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
420	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
421	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
422	    }
423	
424	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
425	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
426	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
427	    func track(
428	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
429	    ) {
430	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
431	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
432	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
433	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
434	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
435	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
436	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
437	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
438	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
439	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
440	        record.copy(job)
441	        records[id] = record
442	    }
443	
444	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
445	    /// returned this launch.
446	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
447	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
448	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
449	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
450	        switch record.state {
451	        case .running:
452	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
453	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
454	        case .completed:
455	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
456	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
457	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
458	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
459	        case .failed, .cancelled:
460	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
461	        case .waiting:
462	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
463	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
464	        }
465	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
466	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
467	        {
468	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
469	        }
470	        answer["export_id"] = id
471	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
472	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
473	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
474	        return answer
475	    }
476	
477	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
478	    private func refresh() {
479	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
480	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
481	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
482	            var updated = record
483	            updated.copy(job)
484	            records[id] = updated
485	        }
486	    }
487	}

490	/// What a finished export's answer carries: the resolved settings and the
491	/// facts about the file that was written, read off the queue's job once it
492	/// has finished — `export_status`'s `done` answer
493	/// (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`), which since spec §11 #326 is what
494	/// `export` itself answered before it returned at once.
495	extension AgentServer {
496	
497	    /// The `done` answer's keys, exactly the ones `export` answered when it
498	    /// blocked to the file. `bytes` is the file's size as read at the finish.
499	    static func exportResult(
500	        settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, path: String, bytes: Int,
501	        loudness: ExportLoudness?, graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning],
502	        cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
503	    ) -> [String: Any] {
504	        var result: [String: Any] = [
505	            "ok": true,
506	            "path": path,
507	            "bytes": bytes,
508	            "preset": settings.preset,
509	            "container": settings.container,
510	            "codec": settings.codec,
511	            "width": settings.width,
512	            "height": settings.height,
513	            "fps": [settings.fps.num, settings.fps.den],
514	            "start": settings.start,
515	            "duration": settings.duration,
516	            // Not one of the resolved settings — the core never saw it — but
517	            // it is a fact about the file that was written, and every other
518	            // key here is one too.
519	            //
520	            // What it establishes is exactly one link and not the chain: this
521	            // is `options.burnInTimecode`, the local decoded a few lines up,
522	            // so a caller reading it back knows the argument was READ rather
523	            // than dropped in argument reading — the failure `boolArg`'s
524	            // refusal covers from the other side. It does NOT say the writer
525	            // used it; only a pixel can say that, and
526	            // `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py` is where one does.
527	            "burn_in_timecode": burnInTimecode,
528	        ]
529	        // The picture an HLG project's file was written as (`hlg`, `pq` or
530	        // `sdr`); absent for every SDR project and audio row.
531	        if let color = settings.color {
532	            result["dynamic_range"] = color
533	        }
534	        // The speed the `av1` row was encoded at (spec §11 CX-12 (2)); absent elsewhere.
535	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed {
536	            result["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue
537	        }
538	        // The depth a WAV or AIFF was written at (spec §11 AU-29); absent elsewhere.
539	        if let bits = settings.audioBits {
540	            result["audio_bits"] = bits
541	        }
542	        // Each stem written beside the mix, in order (spec §11 AU-108); absent without.
543	        if !settings.stems.isEmpty {
544	            let mix = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
545	            result["stems"] = settings.stems.map {
546	                [
547	                    "name": $0.name, "tracks": $0.tracks,
548	                    "path": ExportStemsPipeline.url(for: $0, mix: mix).path,
549	                ] as [String: Any]
550	            }
551	        }
552	        if let measured = loudnessResult(loudness) {
553	            result["loudness"] = measured
554	        }
555	        if let warned = graphicWarningsResult(graphicWarnings) {
556	            result["graphic_warnings"] = warned
557	        }
558	        if let warned = cursorWarningsResult(cursorWarnings) {
559	            result["cursor_warnings"] = warned
560	        }
561	        return result
562	    }
563	
564	    /// What the export's sound MEASURED, for the result — nil, and then the
565	    /// key is simply absent, wherever `Exporter` published no report: a
566	    /// format that holds no audio track at all (GIF and APNG), and a
567	    /// timeline with no sound in it, which is the case a caller actually
568	    /// meets. A missing `loudness` is therefore "there was nothing to
569	    /// measure", never "the measurement was skipped".
570	    ///
571	    /// This is `detect_silence`'s posture applied to the writer: the numbers
572	    /// are read back off the file's own mix rather than repeated from the
573	    /// request, so a caller can check that a −14 LUFS export actually landed
574	    /// at −14, which is what makes phase 5's ±0.5 LU claim a claim anyone can
575	    /// test over MCP. `target` is what was ASKED for and is absent when
576	    /// nothing was — every export measures itself and reports, normalised or
577	    /// not.
578	    ///
579	    /// It is read off the queue's job (`ExportQueueController.Job.loudness`),
580	    /// which `finished` copies from the `Exporter` before dropping it:
581	    /// `Exporter.finish` publishes the report before it calls back, so every
582	    /// consumer (this, the queue's row and the progress sheet) reads it after
583	    /// the completion has fired.
584	    ///
585	    /// Every level goes through `jsonLevel`: a silent programme measures
586	    /// −∞ dBTP, and `JSONSerialization` throws on an infinity — which would
587	    /// report a successful export as a failed tool call.
588	    static func loudnessResult(_ report: ExportLoudness?) -> [String: Any]? {
589	        guard let report = report else { return nil }
590	        var measured: [String: Any] = [
591	            // The same sentence the progress sheet's last line shows, so the
592	            // two consumers of one measurement cannot describe it differently.
593	            "summary": report.summary,
594	            "true_peak_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.truePeakDBTP),
595	            // The shifted sample peak, never above the true peak the master
596	            // held (spec §11 AU-28).
597	            "sample_peak_dbfs": jsonLevel(
598	                min(report.measured.samplePeakDBFS + report.gainDB, report.truePeakDBTP)),
599	            "gain_db": report.gainDB,
600	            "ceiling_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.ceiling),
601	            "limited_db": report.limitedDB,
602	            "capped_by_gain": report.cappedByGain,
603	        ]
604	        // Absent rather than null, and for a reason worth the line: a
