4	// `ExportWriter`'s settings half: what an `ExportSettings` row becomes in
5	// AVFoundation's own terms — the video composition, the alpha guard, the
6	// encoder dictionaries for the picture and the sound, and which containers
7	// carry chapters. A pure move out of `ExporterWriter.swift` at its size cap
8	// (issue batch B60); the members `ExporterWriter.swift` calls lost
9	// `private`, and nothing else changed.
10	extension ExportWriter {
11	
12	    // MARK: - Settings → AVFoundation
13	
14	    /// The video composition to render through: the one the plan built,
15	    /// unless the settings ask for a different frame rate.
16	    ///
17	    /// `CompositionBuilder` ticks the composition at the PROJECT's rate, and
18	    /// the sheet's Frame-rate popup overrides `settings.fps` — which the
19	    /// session path could not honour at all (a preset name carries no rate),
20	    /// so the readout promised 25 fps and the file held 30. The builder's
21	    /// configuration with the asked-for `frameDuration` samples the same
22	    /// timeline at the asked-for instants (#91); the recipes are evaluated per
23	    /// frame at whatever tick is requested, so nothing else has to know.
24	    static func videoComposition(
25	        _ built: BuiltComposition, settings: ExportSettings
26	    ) -> AVVideoComposition {
27	        let fps = settings.fps
28	        var configuration = built.videoConfiguration
29	        guard fps.num > 0, fps.den > 0 else { return built.videoComposition }
30	        configuration.frameDuration = CompositionBuilder.frameDuration(fps)
31	        guard configuration.frameDuration != built.videoConfiguration.frameDuration
32	        else { return built.videoComposition }
33	        return AVVideoComposition(configuration: configuration)
34	    }
35	
36	    /// The reader output the video pump reads: the composition's video tracks
37	    /// through the video composition (`videoComposition`), in the one format
38	    /// the compositor produces. `ExportWebMWriter` reads through it too.
39	    static func videoReadOutput(
40	        _ built: BuiltComposition, settings: ExportSettings
41	    ) -> AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput {
42	        let output = AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput(
43	            videoTracks: built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .video),
44	            videoSettings: [
45	                // The one format the compositor produces (`Compositor.
46	                // outputPixelFormat`, 64RGBAHalf). Asking for it here means no
47	                // conversion between the render context and the encoder.
48	                kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: Int(Compositor.outputPixelFormat),
49	                kCVPixelBufferMetalCompatibilityKey as String: true,
50	            ])
51	        output.videoComposition = videoComposition(built, settings: settings)
52	        // AVFoundation's default, kept explicit: `ExportStraightAlpha` rewrites an
53	        // alpha row's frame in place, which is safe only on the reader's own copy.
54	        output.alwaysCopiesSampleData = true
55	        return output
56	    }
57	
58	    /// The mix's reader output: every composition audio track through the
59	    /// plan's mix, as the float mix the measurement read
60	    /// (`ExportAudioMaster.floatMixSettings`, spec §11 AU-27), which the
61	    /// master turns into the encoder's samples. `ExportWebMWriter` reads
62	    /// through it too. A stem's build (`audioSelection`, spec §11 AU-108 (e))
63	    /// reads only its own tracks through a mix of only their parameters, and
64	    /// so does a sub-mix of `ExportMixRead` (`only`, AU-152), both at once
65	    /// for a stem's sub-mix.
66	    static func audioReadOutput(
67	        _ built: BuiltComposition, only: Set<CMPersistentTrackID>? = nil
68	    ) -> AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput {
69	        var tracks = built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .audio)
70	        var mix = built.audioMix
71	        if built.audioSelection != nil || only != nil {
72	            let reads = { (id: CMPersistentTrackID) in
73	                (built.audioSelection?.contains(id) ?? true) && (only?.contains(id) ?? true)
74	            }
75	            tracks = tracks.filter { reads($0.trackID) }
76	            let selected = AVMutableAudioMix()
77	            selected.inputParameters = built.audioMix.inputParameters.filter {
78	                reads($0.trackID)
79	            }
80	            mix = selected
81	        }
82	        let output = AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput(
83	            audioTracks: tracks, audioSettings: ExportAudioMaster.floatMixSettings)
84	        output.audioMix = mix
85	        // AVFoundation's own default, kept explicit because the other reader
86	        // in this tree (`MediaImporter.peaks`) turns it off.
87	        output.alwaysCopiesSampleData = true
88	        return output
89	    }

91	    /// Refuses an alpha-carrying export whose size would have to be PADDED
92	    /// (road map 2, phase 7b; `Exporter.ExportError.alphaAspectMismatch`
93	    /// carries the argument and the measurement).
94	    ///
95	    /// The composition renders at the canvas size and
96	    /// `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect` fits it into the asked-for frame —
97	    /// which is right for an opaque row, and destroys the alpha channel
98	    /// when it has to pad: the picture comes back at alpha 0 and the bars at
99	    /// alpha 255, the answer inverted. A pure SCALE is safe at any factor,
100	    /// up or down, so what is refused is the shape change and not the
101	    /// resize.
102	    ///
103	    /// The test is `shapeGap`'s, the one `fillsTheBox` asks too (spec §11
104	    /// G-33 (c)): a frame of the canvas's exact shape is written as it is, a
105	    /// frame within a pixel of it is FILLED, and only a frame further off —
106	    /// `gap > limit` — would be padded, which is what is refused here. So an
107	    /// alpha row is exact or filled and never padded, and it reaches
108	    /// `hevc_alpha` as it reaches `prores_4444`, because the row's `alpha`
109	    /// is true.
110	    ///
111	    /// **The box is `encodedSize`'s and not `settings`'.** The encoder is
112	    /// handed `AVVideoWidthKey`/`AVVideoHeightKey`, and it is that frame's
113	    /// shape the picture has to meet. On settings the core resolved the two
114	    /// are one pair (G-33 (b): the core evens the size on the rows that need
115	    /// it, and ProRes 4444 keeps an odd edge), so asking `encodedSize` is the
116	    /// floor under any other caller: a rounding there moves the box, and a
117	    /// comparison against `settings` would not see it. An odd-edged
118	    /// transparent document is legal — `set_canvas` refuses an odd dimension,
119	    /// `Project::new` and `validate` do not, so an odd-sized PNG opened as a
120	    /// document or an odd display size gets one — and at 1001 × 667 its
121	    /// Document row is 1001 × 667 on ProRes 4444, the canvas's exact shape,
122	    /// and the evened 1000 × 666 on `hevc_alpha`, within a pixel and filled.
123	    ///
124	    /// **The pixel of slack does not cost an edge.** It is there for
125	    /// `export_size.rs`'s even-rounding — a standard row's long edge, the
126	    /// evened Document row on a canvas with an odd edge, and an odd size
127	    /// typed in the canvas's proportions can each miss the canvas's exact
128	    /// shape by a pixel, and refusing them would be a false refusal. A frame
129	    /// inside the slack is FILLED (`videoSettings`),
130	    /// so every edge of it is the picture's; fitted, the pad put an edge
131	    /// column at the backdrop's alpha instead (ProRes 4444 at 255,
132	    /// `hevc_alpha` up to 16, where the canvas is transparent — G-33 (c)).
133	    /// `hevc_alpha_proof.py`'s rows O1, O4, O5, P1 and P2 read all four
134	    /// edges of such files at alpha 0.
135	    static func checkAlphaSurvivesTheSize(
136	        _ settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize
137	    ) throws {
138	        guard settings.alpha, canvas.width >= 1, canvas.height >= 1,
139	            settings.width >= 1, settings.height >= 1
140	        else { return }
141	        let shape = shapeGap(encodedSize(settings), canvas: canvas)
142	        guard shape.gap > shape.limit else { return }
143	        // The MESSAGE names `settings`' size and not the box. That is the
144	        // size the core RESOLVED (spec §11 G-33): on ProRes 4444, which
145	        // keeps an odd edge, the pair that was asked for — so the sentence
146	        // still tells the person what to type instead, with no number in it
147	        // they never typed — and on a row the core evens, the even pair the
148	        // sheet and the `export` tool reported.
149	        throw Exporter.ExportError.alphaAspectMismatch(
150	            width: Int(canvas.width.rounded()), height: Int(canvas.height.rounded()),
151	            wantWidth: settings.width, wantHeight: settings.height)
152	    }
153	
154	    /// How far a frame is from the canvas's shape, and how far counts as
155	    /// "within a pixel" — the ONE shape test, in integers, which the alpha
156	    /// guard and the scaling mode both ask (spec §11 G-33 (c)). Nothing else
157	    /// compares shapes.
158	    ///
159	    /// With `cw` × `ch` the canvas and `bw` × `bh` the frame,
160	    /// `d = bw·ch − bh·cw` and `gap = |d|`; 0 is the canvas's exact shape.
161	    /// When `d > 0` the frame is wider than the canvas's shape: a fit leaves
162	    /// `gap/ch` px of width uncovered and a fill overshoots the height by
163	    /// `gap/cw` px; when `d < 0` it is the other way round. `limit` has two
164	    /// arms. A canvas-SHAPED size less at most one pixel on each axis —
165	    /// `(bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw` for some `a`, `b` in {0, 1}: the evened
166	    /// Document row, an odd size typed in the canvas's own proportions once
167	    /// the core has evened it (720 × 405 on 1920 × 1080 arrives as
168	    /// 720 × 404), and on ProRes 4444 a typed frame one pixel short —
169	    /// `max(cw, ch)`: the fit leaves at most a pixel OR the fill overshoots
170	    /// by at most one. There `gap` is `|b·cw − a·ch|`, never above the
171	    /// limit, so such a frame is always exact or filled. Any other frame:
172	    /// `ch` when `d > 0`, else `cw` — the fit leaves at most a pixel, which
173	    /// is the phase-7b guard in integers. `gap <= limit` is "within a
174	    /// pixel", and it is `<=` on purpose: an evened canvas whose odd edge is
175	    /// the SHORT one sits exactly on the limit (181 × 320 into 180 × 320:
176	    /// gap 320, limit 320).
177	    ///
178	    /// The first arm is what lets an evened size through — fitted, it can
179	    /// miss by more than a pixel (1.77 px at 181 × 320) — at ANY scale,
180	    /// smaller than the canvas or larger, because a size of the canvas's
181	    /// shape is never refused for being odd (the owner's answer). Swift is
182	    /// handed only the even frame, so on 400 × 100 it cannot tell a typed
183	    /// 396 × 98 or 404 × 100 from an evened 396 × 99 or 404 × 101: those are
184	    /// filled too, on every row, where they were letterboxed — the costs
185	    /// G-33 (c) records as accepted. A frame typed to pad the canvas by any
186	    /// other amount (402 × 100 on 400 × 100: gap 200, limit 100) is
187	    /// letterboxed as it always was. The quotients are arithmetic, not what
188	    /// the scaler cuts: it drops whole source pixels and stretches the rest
189	    /// (G-33 (c) has the measurement).
190	    private static func shapeGap(
191	        _ frame: (width: Int, height: Int), canvas: CGSize
192	    ) -> (gap: Int, limit: Int) {
193	        let cw = max(1, Int(canvas.width.rounded()))
194	        let ch = max(1, Int(canvas.height.rounded()))
195	        let d = frame.width * ch - frame.height * cw
196	        // (bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw for some a, b in {0, 1} is d == b·cw − a·ch.
197	        let inside = [0, cw, -ch, cw - ch].contains(d)
198	        let limit = inside ? max(cw, ch) : (d > 0 ? ch : cw)
199	        return (abs(d), limit)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// Whether the picture FILLS the frame rather than being fitted inside
203	    /// it: a frame within a pixel of the canvas's shape and not exactly it
204	    /// (`shapeGap`). No codec is asked — an opaque row fills where it used to
205	    /// write a black line, an alpha row where it used to write an edge at the
206	    /// wrong alpha.
207	    static func fillsTheBox(_ settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize) -> Bool {
208	        let shape = shapeGap(encodedSize(settings), canvas: canvas)
209	        return shape.gap > 0 && shape.gap <= shape.limit
210	    }

221	    /// IDENTITY, and the size the sheet, the queue and the `export` tool

229	    /// away — and padding is the one thing an alpha export cannot survive.
230	    /// Measured here (macOS 26.5.1, `AVAssetWriter` +
231	    /// `AVVideoCodecType.proRes4444`): asked for 1001 × 667 the writer
232	    /// accepts it and the file comes back `prores`, `yuva444p12le`,

234	    /// at 255 — exact at every pixel; asked for 1000 × 666 with the same
235	    /// 1001 × 667 picture, fitted, it came back with its right-hand column
236	    /// OPAQUE where the canvas is transparent. So the one row that could not
237	    /// afford the rounding turns out not to need it — and since G-33 a frame
238	    /// a pixel short is filled rather than fitted, so the master keeps its
239	    /// odd edge because it can be the document's own pixels, not because the
240	    /// rounding would still break it.
241	    /// Every other row keeps the rounding it has always had, ProRes 422
242	    /// included — it does not need it either (measured: 1001 × 667 survives
243	    /// as `yuv422p10le`), but changing the bytes a shipped row writes for a
244	    /// case no proof covers is not this guard's business.
245	    static func encodedSize(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> (width: Int, height: Int) {
246	        guard codecType(for: settings.codec) == .proRes4444 else {
247	            return (evenDimension(settings.width), evenDimension(settings.height))
248	        }
249	        return (max(1, settings.width), max(1, settings.height))
250	    }

252	    /// The encoder settings for the picture.
253	    ///
254	    /// **Size.** The composition renders at the CANVAS size (§7.2), and the
255	    /// core resolves the export size — the document's unless the sheet's
256	    /// Size popup, its Custom fields or the `export` tool asked for another
257	    /// — and they are not the same number; the session path simply dropped
258	    /// the second one on the floor: the preset scaled to fit whatever it

261	    /// (spec §11 G-33 (c)). A frame of the canvas's exact shape, or one more
262	    /// than a pixel off it, gets `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect`: the canvas

266	    /// frame, where a fit wrote one or two black lines along an edge — the
267	    /// evened Document row on a canvas with an odd edge, an odd size typed
268	    /// in the canvas's proportions, and a standard row whose long edge
269	    /// rounded. The frame itself is `encodedSize`'s answer,
270	    /// because `checkAlphaSurvivesTheSize` and `fillsTheBox` have to compare

275	    /// says what the pixels handed to the encoder ARE: straight, because the
276	    /// video pump un-premultiplies an alpha row's frames first
277	    /// (`ExportStraightAlpha`, spec §11 G-35 (e), amending G-33 (d)). There
278	    /// is no alpha-quality key and no profile key (G-33 (d) has what was

284	    /// `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` VideoToolbox picks a conservative default

297	            AVVideoWidthKey: frame.width,

308	            ],

316	            output[AVVideoColorPropertiesKey] = [

481	    /// the CONTAINER decides the byte order.** ProRes has since M2 (§7.8

504	                AVSampleRateKey: 48000,

506	                AVEncoderBitRateKey: settings.audioBitrate.map { max(1, $0) } ?? 192_000,

188	    /// and report success. A custom
189	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
190	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
191	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
192	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
193	    private func exportSizeArg(
194	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
195	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
196	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
197	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
198	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
199	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
200	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
201	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
202	        let rows: [ExportSize]
203	        do {
204	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
205	        } catch {
206	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
207	        }
208	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
209	        if let id = raw as? String {
210	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
211	                throw ToolError(
212	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
213	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
214	            }
215	            return (row.width, row.height)
216	        }
217	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
218	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
219	            if edges.count == 2 {
220	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
221	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
222	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
223	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
224	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
225	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
226	                    throw ToolError(
227	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
228	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
229	                            + "row: \(ids).")
230	                }
231	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
232	            }
233	        }
234	        throw ToolError(
235	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
236	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
240	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
241	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
242	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
243	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
244	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
245	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
246	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
247	    /// `1`.
248	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
249	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
250	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
251	            let real = number.doubleValue
252	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
253	        }
254	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
255	    }
256	
257	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
258	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
259	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
260	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
261	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
262	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
263	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
264	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
265	    /// lead.
266	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
267	        let message = error.localizedDescription
268	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
269	            return ToolError(message: message)
270	        }
271	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
272	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
273	    }
274	
275	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
276	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
277	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
278	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
279	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
280	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
281	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
282	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
283	        return text
284	    }
285	}

290	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
291	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
292	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
293	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
294	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
295	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
296	///
297	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
298	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
299	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
300	///
301	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
302	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
303	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
304	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
305	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
306	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
307	extension AgentServer {
308	
309	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
310	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
311	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
312	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
313	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
314	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
315	        }
316	        return try jsonResult(status)
317	    }
318	
319	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
320	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
321	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
322	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
323	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
324	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
325	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
326	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
327	        }
328	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
329	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
330	        }
331	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
332	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
333	        }
334	        return try jsonResult(status)
335	    }

337	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
338	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
339	        switch state {
340	        case .waiting: return "queued"
341	        case .running: return "running"
342	        case .completed: return "done"
343	        case .failed: return "failed"
344	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
345	        }
346	    }

348	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
349	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
350	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
351	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
352	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
353	        }
354	        guard raw >= 1 else {
355	            throw ToolError(
356	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
357	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
358	        }
359	        return UInt64(raw)
360	    }

362	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
363	        ToolError(
364	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "

369	/// What `AgentExports` keeps of one tracked job: the queue row's fields as
370	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
371	private struct AgentExportRecord {
372	    let settings: ExportSettings
373	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
374	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
375	    let started: TimeInterval
376	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
377	    var progress: Double
378	    var phase: String?
379	    var message: String?
380	    var destination: URL
381	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
382	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
383	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
384	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
385	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
386	    var finished: TimeInterval?
387	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
388	    var bytes: Int = 0
389	
390	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
391	        state = job.state
392	        progress = job.progress
393	        phase = job.phase
394	        message = job.message
395	        destination = job.destination
396	        loudness = job.loudness
397	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
398	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
399	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
400	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
401	        bytes =
402	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
403	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0

407	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
408	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
409	final class AgentExports {
410	    static let shared = AgentExports()
411	
412	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
413	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
414	
415	    private init() {
416	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
417	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
418	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
419	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
420	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
421	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
422	    }
423	
424	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
425	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
426	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
427	    func track(
428	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
429	    ) {
430	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
431	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
432	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
433	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
434	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
435	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
436	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
437	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
438	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
439	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
440	        record.copy(job)
441	        records[id] = record
442	    }
443	
444	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
445	    /// returned this launch.
446	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
447	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
448	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
449	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
450	        switch record.state {
451	        case .running:
452	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
453	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
454	        case .completed:
455	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
456	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
457	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
458	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
459	        case .failed, .cancelled:
460	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
461	        case .waiting:
462	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
463	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
464	        }
465	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
466	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
467	        {
468	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
469	        }
470	        answer["export_id"] = id
471	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
472	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
473	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
474	        return answer
475	    }
476	
477	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
478	    private func refresh() {
479	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
480	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
481	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
482	            var updated = record
483	            updated.copy(job)
484	            records[id] = updated
485	        }
486	    }
487	}

490	/// What a finished export's answer carries: the resolved settings and the
491	/// facts about the file that was written, read off the queue's job once it
492	/// has finished — `export_status`'s `done` answer
493	/// (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`), which since spec §11 #326 is what
494	/// `export` itself answered before it returned at once.
495	extension AgentServer {
496	
497	    /// The `done` answer's keys, exactly the ones `export` answered when it
498	    /// blocked to the file. `bytes` is the file's size as read at the finish.
499	    static func exportResult(
500	        settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, path: String, bytes: Int,
501	        loudness: ExportLoudness?, graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning],
502	        cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
503	    ) -> [String: Any] {
504	        var result: [String: Any] = [
505	            "ok": true,
506	            "path": path,
507	            "bytes": bytes,
508	            "preset": settings.preset,
509	            "container": settings.container,
510	            "codec": settings.codec,
511	            "width": settings.width,
512	            "height": settings.height,
513	            "fps": [settings.fps.num, settings.fps.den],
514	            "start": settings.start,
515	            "duration": settings.duration,
516	            // Not one of the resolved settings — the core never saw it — but
517	            // it is a fact about the file that was written, and every other
518	            // key here is one too.
519	            //
520	            // What it establishes is exactly one link and not the chain: this
521	            // is `options.burnInTimecode`, the local decoded a few lines up,
522	            // so a caller reading it back knows the argument was READ rather
523	            // than dropped in argument reading — the failure `boolArg`'s
524	            // refusal covers from the other side. It does NOT say the writer
525	            // used it; only a pixel can say that, and
526	            // `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py` is where one does.
527	            "burn_in_timecode": burnInTimecode,
528	        ]
529	        // The picture an HLG project's file was written as (`hlg`, `pq` or
530	        // `sdr`); absent for every SDR project and audio row.
531	        if let color = settings.color {
532	            result["dynamic_range"] = color
533	        }
534	        // The speed the `av1` row was encoded at (spec §11 CX-12 (2)); absent elsewhere.
535	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed {
536	            result["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue
537	        }
538	        // The depth a WAV or AIFF was written at (spec §11 AU-29); absent elsewhere.
539	        if let bits = settings.audioBits {
540	            result["audio_bits"] = bits
541	        }
542	        // Each stem written beside the mix, in order (spec §11 AU-108); absent without.
543	        if !settings.stems.isEmpty {
544	            let mix = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
545	            result["stems"] = settings.stems.map {
546	                [
547	                    "name": $0.name, "tracks": $0.tracks,
548	                    "path": ExportStemsPipeline.url(for: $0, mix: mix).path,
549	                ] as [String: Any]
550	            }
551	        }
552	        if let measured = loudnessResult(loudness) {
553	            result["loudness"] = measured
554	        }
555	        if let warned = graphicWarningsResult(graphicWarnings) {
556	            result["graphic_warnings"] = warned
557	        }
558	        if let warned = cursorWarningsResult(cursorWarnings) {
559	            result["cursor_warnings"] = warned
560	        }
561	        return result
562	    }

564	    /// What the export's sound MEASURED, for the result — nil, and then the
565	    /// key is simply absent, wherever `Exporter` published no report: a
566	    /// format that holds no audio track at all (GIF and APNG), and a
567	    /// timeline with no sound in it, which is the case a caller actually
568	    /// meets. A missing `loudness` is therefore "there was nothing to
569	    /// measure", never "the measurement was skipped".
570	    ///
571	    /// This is `detect_silence`'s posture applied to the writer: the numbers
572	    /// are read back off the file's own mix rather than repeated from the
573	    /// request, so a caller can check that a −14 LUFS export actually landed
574	    /// at −14, which is what makes phase 5's ±0.5 LU claim a claim anyone can
575	    /// test over MCP. `target` is what was ASKED for and is absent when
576	    /// nothing was — every export measures itself and reports, normalised or
577	    /// not.
578	    ///
579	    /// It is read off the queue's job (`ExportQueueController.Job.loudness`),
580	    /// which `finished` copies from the `Exporter` before dropping it:
581	    /// `Exporter.finish` publishes the report before it calls back, so every
582	    /// consumer (this, the queue's row and the progress sheet) reads it after
583	    /// the completion has fired.
584	    ///
585	    /// Every level goes through `jsonLevel`: a silent programme measures
586	    /// −∞ dBTP, and `JSONSerialization` throws on an infinity — which would
587	    /// report a successful export as a failed tool call.
588	    static func loudnessResult(_ report: ExportLoudness?) -> [String: Any]? {
589	        guard let report = report else { return nil }
590	        var measured: [String: Any] = [
591	            // The same sentence the progress sheet's last line shows, so the
592	            // two consumers of one measurement cannot describe it differently.
593	            "summary": report.summary,
594	            "true_peak_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.truePeakDBTP),
595	            // The shifted sample peak, never above the true peak the master
596	            // held (spec §11 AU-28).
597	            "sample_peak_dbfs": jsonLevel(
598	                min(report.measured.samplePeakDBFS + report.gainDB, report.truePeakDBTP)),
599	            "gain_db": report.gainDB,
600	            "ceiling_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.ceiling),
601	            "limited_db": report.limitedDB,
602	            "capped_by_gain": report.cappedByGain,
603	        ]
604	        // Absent rather than null, and for a reason worth the line: a
605	        // programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose every
606	        // block fell under the standard's absolute gate, HAS no integrated
607	        // loudness. `summary` says so in words.
608	        if let integrated = report.integratedLUFS, integrated.isFinite {
609	            measured["integrated_lufs"] = integrated
610	        }
611	        if let target = report.target {
612	            measured["target_lufs"] = target
613	        }
614	        return measured
615	    }

617	    /// Each distinct warning the export's graphics gave while the file was
618	    /// drawn (G-24 (c)), `[{name, frame, message}]` — `frame` the graphic's
619	    /// own, null when it has none — or nil, and then the key is absent,
620	    /// when there was none. Read off the queue's job after the completion,
621	    /// as `loudnessResult` is: `Exporter.finish` publishes it before the
622	    /// unpin. A failed export answers as it did.
623	    static func graphicWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
624	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
625	        return warnings.map {
626	            ["name": $0.name, "frame": $0.frame ?? NSNull(), "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
627	        }
628	    }
629	
630	    /// Each media whose cursor file the export could not draw (spec §11
631	    /// CU-37 (c)), `[{media, path, message}]`, or nil, and then the key is
632	    /// absent, when there was none — `graphicWarningsResult`'s shape (G-24 (c)).
633	    static func cursorWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
634	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
635	        return warnings.map {
636	            ["media": $0.media, "path": $0.path, "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
637	        }
638	    }
639	}

Up and Down are one action [from, to) ending at `rate`; Dip and Burst are two, of r = max(snapped_down((to − from)·(1 − hold)/2), one frame) each, [from, from + r) ending at `rate` and [to − r, to) ending at b, the span between holding the target. `hold` (Dip and Burst only) is clamped to 0–0.9, 0.5 when absent; `curve` is every new action's, `ease_in_out` when absent. export/gif-and-apng.mdx:3:description: "Export a short silent loop as an Animated GIF or Animated PNG, and keep it inside the size and the 600-frame limit."
export/gif-and-apng.mdx:9:GIF and APNG are for short silent loops you can send or drop into a page. Each stores every frame as a whole picture, so a long or large one quickly becomes a file nobody can send. That's why both start small and hold at most 600 frames.
export/gif-and-apng.mdx:48:## The 600-frame limit
export/gif-and-apng.mdx:50:An animated GIF or APNG holds at most 600 frames. That's 48 seconds at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 seconds at APNG's 25 fps. content.content:
---
title: Glossary
description: Frame Job's own words in plain terms, from action and canvas to nest, ramp, stem and tick, each linked to its page.
---

The words Frame Job uses, in plain terms, each with a link to the page that explains it.

## Projects and the timeline

- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **In–Out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
- **No-change edit, or identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It beeps, makes no undo step and shows no message. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/#a-beep-with-no-message).
- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
- **Refusal.** A rule stopping an edit. Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's sentence after "Refused: " at the foot of the inspector. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. The "Refused: " line and agent tools give lengths in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## Picture and sound

content.content:
An HDR (HLG) project can leave Frame Job as an HLG master, as an HDR10 file, or as an SDR version for everywhere HDR won't play. You choose on the export sheet's **Dynamic Range:** row.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Dynamic Range"
  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
  needs="An HDR (HLG) project."
/>

## Export an HDR file

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>).

2. In **Format:**, choose one of the [six formats that carry HDR](#which-formats-carry-hdr).

3. In **Dynamic Range:**, choose **HDR (HLG)**, **HDR10 (PQ)** or **SDR version**.

4. Finish the rest of the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) as usual.

</Steps>

## The Dynamic Range row

The row sits under **Format:**, and it only appears in an HDR (HLG) project. An SDR project's sheet doesn't have it. To make a project HDR, see [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

The choice lasts while the sheet is open. If you switch to a format that can't carry HDR and back, your choice returns. It isn't remembered for the next export, and an [export preset](/export/presets/) doesn't save it.

### HDR (HLG)

The BT.2100 HLG master, tagged with BT.2020 primaries and matrix and the HLG transfer. It's first on the row and the default.

### HDR10 (PQ)

An HDR10 file: BT.2100 PQ, mastered at 1,000 cd/m², with [fixed metadata](#fixed-hdr10-metadata). It's available on the same six formats as HLG.

### SDR version

The project's SDR version, in Rec. 709. It's the same picture as [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). White titles stay near white, and highlights above reference white are rolled off.

## Which formats carry HDR

Six formats can carry an HDR picture, each at 10 bits or more:

- **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)**
- **AV1 (MP4)**
- **AV1 (WebM)**
- **VP9 (WebM)**
- **ProRes 422 (MOV)**
- **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**

On every other format the **Dynamic Range:** row is disabled and shows **SDR version**. **H.264 (MP4)**, **HEVC (MP4)**, **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**, **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)**, **Animated GIF** and **Animated PNG** always write the SDR version. The audio-only formats have no picture, so the row does nothing there.

### VP9 and HDR

**VP9 (WebM)** writes HLG and HDR10 as 10-bit VP9 Profile 2, and the SDR version as 8-bit Profile 0. VP9 itself can't say which transfer it uses, so the WebM file's colour information is what tells a player it's HLG or PQ.

## Fixed HDR10 metadata

Every HDR10 file carries the same metadata:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mastering display | P3 D65, 0.005–1,000 cd/m² |
| MaxCLL | 1,000 |
| MaxFALL | 0 |

The picture never goes above 1,000 cd/m², so this metadata is always accurate. The [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) in the Media tab describes a source file and doesn't change it.

## HDR frames

**File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) in an HDR (HLG) project writes the HLG picture as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, labelled BT.2100 HLG. A JPEG writes the SDR version, labelled BT.709. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

## Good to know

- There's no Dolby Vision output. None is added to an HLG or HDR10 file.
- [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) changes the preview only. It never reaches an export or a saved frame, so the file is whatever the sheet says.

## With an agent

`export` takes the same three choices as `dynamic_range`: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Where the sheet disables the row, the tool fails with a message instead. Asking for HLG or HDR10 on a format that can't carry it, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, names the six formats that can. Asking for either in an SDR project says to make the project HDR first. Asking for the SDR version in an SDR project changes nothing, and an audio-only format ignores the choice.

`export` returns an id for the job straight away. Once `export_status` reports a video job done in an HDR (HLG) project, its `dynamic_range` names the picture that was written. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) and [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export).

`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame, and `sdr_version` draws the SDR version in any image format. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#frames-from-an-hdr-project).

## Related

If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.

## An export won't start or stops

An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.

While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out. Add a clip first.

"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | Frame Job won't export a graphic that can't draw itself. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |

A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

:::caution
Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
:::

See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).

## A feature asks for a key

Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

## Import and apply a LUT

<Steps>

1. Select the clips you want to grade.

2. Open the **Look** section of the **Color** sub-tab, and click **Import LUT…** under the gallery. The sub-tab doesn't show if the selection holds a text, shape, graphic or nest clip.

3. Choose a `.cube` file.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="05e-clip-look-lut.inspector"
  alt="The Look section with the eight built-in look tiles and None, then an Imported group holding two tiles, Warm Print and Bleach, with Warm Print outlined in blue. The Import LUT… button sits underneath, and the section header reads Warm Print 80%."
/>

The file joins the project and goes on the selected clips as one undo step, **Import LUT**. If the file is already in the project, Frame Job reuses its entry rather than adding it twice. If Frame Job can't read the file, an error appears and nothing changes.

## Add a LUT without applying it

Add the file to the project and apply it later:

- Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>). A file with the `.cube` extension, in any case, counts as a LUT.
- Or drop the file on the **Media** tab. It's the only place in the window that takes a dropped `.cube`.

## Apply a LUT already in the project

14:Every video source is decoded to 16-bit float, and every frame is composited at 16-bit float. Blends run there too, so a heavy grade keeps its precision. A 10-bit source keeps its detail all the way to a 10-bit or ProRes export.
16:A 16-bit float frame takes twice the memory of an 8-bit one, so an export needs about twice the memory for its frames.
18:## 10-bit exports
20:The format you choose on the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) decides how much of that depth reaches the file.

A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip gets the same, when every video track in the timeline is that deep. A JPEG is always 8-bit. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

            "| [24-bit sound](/export/audio-only/) |",
            "| [24-bit sound](/export/bit-depth/) |",
        ),
    ],
}


def main() -> int:
    failed = 0
    for rel, rows in EDITS.items():
        path = ROOT / rel
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        changed = 0
        for old, new in rows:
            count = text.count(old)
            if count != 1:
                print(f"SKIP {rel}: {count} matches for {old[:70]!r}")
                failed += 1
                continue
            text = text.replace(old, new)
            changed += 1
        if changed:
            path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"{rel}: {changed}/{len(rows)}")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

app_defects.title: A refused export still deletes the file it was going to replace
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/Exporter.swift:347 removes the destination before Exporter.pipeline at :360.
